item.title: Investment Analyst - Manufacturing and Services
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Knowledge Bank is the WBG’s platform for generating, curating, and applying global knowledge to support development impact at scale. It connects operational experience, analytical work, data, and global expertise to inform policy dialogue, country programs, and investments across the World Bank Group. The WBG’s Prosperity Vice Presidency, which includes the Bank’s Manufacturing and Manufacturing Services expertise, works to connect our operational teams with clients by providing public and private sector solutions to expand Manufacturing opportunities in emerging markets. Within this structure, the Manufacturing and Services Solutions and Impact Department (WKPTM) focuses on supporting investments in Manufacturing value chains including but not limited to those in Construction Materials (steel, cement, glass, etc.), Chemicals, Fertilizers, Automotive, Electronics, Batteries, Machinery, Textiles and Apparel, Packaging and other sectors involved in industrial production, value enhancement, and processing. The WKPTM group is looking to hire an Investment Analyst to support the implementation of the Manufacturing and Manufacturing Services sectors’ investments and solutions work. The Investment Analyst will help (i) prepare sector mappings, strategies, and management briefings; (ii) further WBG expertise in Manufacturing through benchmarking, analyzing industry trends, and tracking lessons learned and disseminating the same across the organization; (iii) develop new business, support transactions; and (ii) manage key global client relationships. The Investment Analyst will work closely with sector and team leads, industry specialists and advisors, regional teams, and other partners to support industry and market research. The position will be based in Washington, DC. Some travel may be required. Duties and Accountabilities: The responsibilities of the Investment Analyst will include but are not limited to: Sector Support, Business Development and Knowledge Management : • Provide market research and analysis, including comparator analysis, assessment of market dynamics, benchmarking, and competitiveness; • Prepare sector mapping to identify and target potential global clients and business opportunities; • Research prospective client companies; • Assist in preparing sector strategies and client pitchbooks; and • Contribute to dissemination and exchange of knowledge. Deal Execution and Investment Portfolio : • Collect market data and coordinate with clients to obtain necessary information to support financial, operational and development impact assessments; • Analyze company financial statements and projections, build financial models, and prepare sensitivity analyses; and • With supervision from senior colleagues, coordinate with internal resources (legal, ES G, economists, sector specialists, etc.) for input on relevant investment documents and analyses.

item.title: E T Consultant- Data Scientist Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity to help clients address their most pressing development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities—the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the world’s largest development bank, it provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org. Infrastructure Vertical The World Bank Group (WBG) Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure The Disaster Management, Solutions Impact Unit (KIUSD) supports low and middle-income countries to understand, manage, and reduce their risks from natural hazards and climate change. Within KIUSD, the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) umbrella trust fund is a global partnership that helps low- and middle-income countries better understand and reduce their vulnerability to natural hazards and climate change. GFDRR supports analytics and technical assistance to governments in the most vulnerable countries and communities where it will have the greatest positive impact. As a donor-funded program, GFDRR consults regularly with donors and actively strives to maintain and develop new partnerships for increased impact. For more information: https://www.gfdrr.org/en Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The overall objective of the assignment is to develop and apply in-house resilient infrastructure analytics covering exposure, vulnerability, criticality analyses. The Data Scientist will support the Resilient Infrastructure thematic area in GFDRR (RI). The immediate focus is to further develop and apply the “Infrascan” tool, which produces multi-hazard exposure, vulnerability, and risk assessments for infrastructure assets. RI anticipates strong demand for these outputs from World Bank task teams, both for operations and for advisory and advocacy products. The Data Scientist will play a key role in responding to task teams by producing semi-standardized “Infrascan” notes and supporting teams in interpreting and communicating results, including in policy preliminary investment dialogues. On tool development, the Data Scientist will help refine and expand the tool by: adding additional hazards (potentially including drought, extreme heat, and wildfires); increasing automation to make the workflow as close to plug-and-play as feasible across sectors and hazards; and contributing to a bottom-up repository of local datasets covering infrastructure assets, hazards, vulnerability curves, and asset cost estimates. In addition, the Data Scientist will contribute to other RI workstreams and help catalyze collaboration with other GFDRR thematic areas and relevant analytics produced by WBG teams. This includes: (i) running network analysis tools to assess the impacts of hazard-related transport disruptions at urban and inter-regional scales; (ii) advancing the development and analytics for geospatial “predicted employment” layers based on an existing algorithm; (iii) supporting the application of methodologies to generate extreme event damage scenarios for system stress testing; and (iv) contributing to other RI analytics, including work on cost–benefit ratios of resilience investments and the identification of critical elements required to maintain infrastructure services. The Data Scientist will be a core member of the RI, providing analytics to support World Bank regional teams and strengthen the systematic integration of resilience into infrastructure-related policy and investment operations, including: • Take a leading role in the development and application of geospatial and other quantitative tools within RI. • Support the development and delivery of knowledge products and operational toolkits to enhance capacity of task teams to deliver operations related to resilient infrastructure, including assessing impacts and identifying mitigation measures for climate-related hazards and geohazards. • Support task teams in communicating results from RI tool applications through presentations, training, talking points, and concise summaries in multiple formats. • Coordinate with key partners inside and outside the WBG that manage or develop geospatial tools. • Contribute to program deliverables, including preparation of GFDRR communication and dissemination materials, results monitoring, reporting, budgeting, and branding. • Deliver presentations and workshops in a variety of settings, including with task teams, government counterparts, and internal and external events. • Carry out other tasks, as needed, to support the overall objective of the position.

item.title: E T Consultant - Senior Infrastructure Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. The WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure The Disaster Management, Solutions Impact Unit (KIUSD) supports low and middle-income countries to understand, manage, and reduce their risks from natural hazards and climate change. Within KIUSD, the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) umbrella trust fund is a global partnership that helps low- and middle-income countries better understand and reduce their vulnerability to natural hazards and climate change. GFDRR supports analytics and technical assistance to governments in the most vulnerable countries and communities where it will have the greatest positive impact. As a donor-funded program, GFDRR consults regularly with donors and actively strives to maintain and develop new partnerships for increased impact. For more information: https://www.gfdrr.org/en Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The Senior Infrastructure Consultant will serve as a global technical advisor within KIUSD- Resilient Infrastructure Thematic Area, providing strategic and operational support to World Bank regional teams to strengthen the systematic integration of resilience into infrastructure-related policies, investment operations, and analytical work, including: • Support the development of knowledge products and operational toolkit to enhance capacity of task teams to deliver operations related to resilient infrastructure, assessing the impact and identifying mitigation measures to climate-related hazards and geohazards, such as soil erosion and landslides. • Support the coherent integration of resilience considerations across the policy–investment–analytics continuum, ensuring alignment between upstream diagnostics, design standards, investment design, and implementation support. • Provide advice on resilience engineering standards, performance metrics, indicators, and results frameworks in infrastructure operations. • As part of country activities, provide technical advice on rapid diagnostics of policies and design of resilient infrastructure, as well as exposure, vulnerability, risk and post-disaster assessments. • Provide targeted, demand-driven advisory support to regional task teams and client counterparts, focusing on the preparation and implementation of lending operation projects that involve resilient infrastructure activities, focusing on roads and drainage. Activities include but are not limited to supporting the formulation of terms of reference, technical review of reports and due diligence of the project scoping, preparation, or implementation. • Liaise with stakeholders across government, contractors, and development partners as part of country activities and technical assistance. • Oversee the implementation of TA activities including but not limited to planning, budgeting, preparation of terms of references, quality control, supervision of external consultants and technical specialists work as well as developing and reviewing Trust Fund Proposals, contributing to Trust Funds reporting, and developing of terms of reference. • Contribute and support capacity building activities for WBG Task Teams and client countries’ teams involved in resilient infrastructure projects. • Participate in field missions and provide technical input and guidance to client counterparts as required by operational and analytical task team leaders. • Contribute to program deliverables, including preparation of GFDRR communication and dissemination materials, results monitoring, reporting, budgeting, and branding. • Carry out other tasks relevant to support the overall objective of the position.

item.title: (Associate) Investment Officer - Energy
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The World Bank’s Infrastructure Vice Presidency, part of the WBG Knowledge Bank, provides investment and advisory services for private and public sector clients across energy, mining and metals, transport, waste, and tourism sectors, and further mobilizes private sector capital from institutional investors and other financial institutions. It acts as a strategic partner to the private sector, leveraging its financial resources, deep-seated global expertise, and ability to mitigate risk and mobilize capital to foster infrastructure development that opens markets, drives economic growth, creates jobs and improves living standards in emerging markets in the development of a wide array of infrastructure sectors. The Energy Investments, Solutions Impact team (KIESI) within the WBG Infrastructure Vice Presidency seeks to accelerate critical private sector investments in energy infrastructure, including by leveraging the Knowledge Bank resources to promote initiatives and innovative financing products. Our team is united by core values of Impact, Integrity, Respect, Teamwork, and Innovation. Together, we tackle the world’s toughest challenges, and advance social and economic inclusion. KIESI is looking to recruit an (Associate) Investment Officer to contribute to the Energy Department’s priorities comprising development and dissemination of sector strategy and expertise, market creation and innovation, as well as supporting WBG decision-making processes for new energy investments, management of key global client relationships, business development, and transaction execution. D uties and Accountabilities • Work closely with other members of the team and the Knowledge Bank to support IFC investment teams globally in structuring debt, equity, and blended finance instruments. • Collaborate with interdisciplinary Knowledge Bank teams to support IFC's investment decision making process by promoting best practices and sharing global investment expertise. • Contribute to knowledge-sharing initiatives and provide insights on market trends, risks, and opportunities in the energy sector to inform WBG strategic decision-making. • Support the development and implementation of WBG strategies, as well as innovative financing solutions and initiatives to address market gaps and promote private sector participation in selected energy segments. • From time to time, as member of project teams, contribute to execution of new IFC investment transactions including preparing investment proposals, conducting due diligence as well as detailed financial, market, and risk analyses. • Work with Global relationship managers to build and maintain strong relationships with clients, industry stakeholders, and co-investors to identify and develop a robust pipeline of high-impact investment opportunities.

item.title: Senior Investment Officer - Manufacturing, Agribusiness & Services (MAS) Europe, Upstream & Advisory
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. Working at the WBG provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. Through its five global institutions — IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID the WBG works with public and private sector partners to address the world's most urgent challenges. At the core of this effort is a shared mission: creating jobs that lift people out of poverty and contribute to a world free of poverty on a livable planet. With the private sector accounting for approximately 90% of jobs in developing countries, IFC’s work is central to the World Bank Group’s jobs agenda. Through Upstream and Advisory IFC leverages WBG expertise, tools and solutions to address market barriers, support reforms, and develop impactful and investable opportunities in order to mobilize private capital and create jobs across sectors with significant growth and employment potential, such as foundational infrastructure, manufacturing, agribusiness, healthcare and tourism. MAS EUR Upstream Advisory is seeking a Senior Investment Officer (SIO), who will also serve as IFC’s Hub Lead for Poland, to drive strategic origination and impactful Upstream Advisory engagements across the MAS sectors in the Europe region. The Senior Investment Officer will lead proactive business development, support design and delivery One WBG initiatives that contextualize scalable WBG solutions to deliver on Country Partnership Framework objectives and convert early-stage engagements into a strong pipeline of bankable investments. Based in Warsaw, the Senior Investment Officer will serve as IFC’s Hub Lead for Poland — representing IFC in the local market, coordinating and championing MAS business development and Upstream activities in Poland, and building a strong pipeline of bankable investments in support of the Country Partnership Framework, while contributing to and helping shape the broader Europe regional Upstream and business development program. The role will also support IFC’s engagement in Ukraine, including private-sector origination and Upstream work that helps mobilize capital for the country’s recovery and reconstruction, and will explore the role Poland can play as a platform for reconstruction-linked investment, supply chains, and regional integration. Duties and Accountabilities: • Serve as IFC’s Hub Lead for Poland: setting MAS strategic priorities in the country, shaping the WBG country strategy and business plan to drive growth in MAS sectors, representing MAS in the local market, contributing to joint WBG engagements, serving as the primary point of contact for clients, partners and WBG counterparts, and leading and mentoring the local team. • Deliver at least five (5) bankable mandates annually for high-impact investments with >5x private capital mobilization potential, contributing to the achievement of the WBG Scorecard outcome indicators in MAS sectors in Poland and CEE. • Build and manage senior-level relationships with clients, private sector partners, financial institutions, multilaterals, and governments to originate and advance investment opportunities. • Lead MAS business development in Poland, building a strong, high-quality pipeline of bankable investments aligned with the Country Partnership Framework, while supporting and contributing to the broader Europe regional program. • Support IFC’s engagement across CEE, including investment, Upstream, and Advisory activities that mobilize private capital and support regional growth, recovery and reconstruction. • Identify and develop opportunities for Poland to play a role in Ukraine’s reconstruction — including cross-border investment, supply chains, and platforms that connect Polish and regional private-sector capacity to reconstruction needs. • Design and deliver Upstream engagements focused on originating bankable investment opportunities that convert WBG-supported reforms into private sector investments and structuring innovative financing solutions to crowd in private capital. • Design and lead the delivery Advisory engagements that strengthen private sector competitiveness, build market opportunities, and support the implementation of WBG priorities through scalable, private sector-led solutions. • Leverage market intelligence and sector insights to shape strategic priorities, identify emerging investment opportunities, and enhance the origination and structuring of high-impact transactions. • Collaborate across teams and regions to develop sector/country strategies, deliver integrated solutions, and maximize development impact of IFC investments in emerging Europe. • Mentor, coach, and develop junior team members, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability and excellence.

Bon sens de l'organisation, capacité à travailler efficacement sur la base d'instructions générales, avec la capacité de prioriser les tâches, souvent en respectant des délais très courts. Aptitude confirmée à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et axé sur le travail d'équipe et à s'adapter à l'évolution des méthodes de travail et des technologies. Très bonnes capacités de rédaction et de communication. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Durée du contrat La durée du stage est comprise entre un et six mois (renouvelable pour six mois supplémentaires jusqu’à un total de douze mois au maximum). Les stagiaires sont recrutés tout au long de l'année, afin de permettre aux étudiants de soumettre leur candidature à n'importe quel moment, en fonction de leur disponibilité et des besoins de l'équipe de recrutement. Étant donné que le processus de sélection peut durer jusqu'à trois mois, il est conseillé de postuler suffisamment à l'avance. N'oubliez pas de préciser ces dates dans le formulaire de candidature. Nous acceptons les candidatures pour ce programme de stage jusqu'au 31 décembre 2026, après cela, une nouvelle offre sera publiée. Si vous n’êtes pas contacté(e) par les équipes de recrutement de la Direction concernée dans les six mois suivant le dépôt de votre candidature, vous pouvez mettre à jour votre candidature et postuler à nouveau en utilisant la même adresse mail. Pour plus d’informations sur le Programme de stages de l’OCDE, veuillez consulter les questions fréquentes (FAQ). Note aux candidats: En raison du volume élevé de candidatures reçues, le Bureau des stages de l’OCDE n’est pas en mesure de fournir une réponse à chacune. Par conséquent, seul(e)s les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s par les Directions pour un entretien. L’OCDE promeut en son sein une optimisation de l’emploi de ses ressources, dans le but d’améliorer son efficience et son efficacité, et les membres de son personnel sont encouragés à y contribuer activement. Cliquez ici pour en savoir plus sur ce que propose l’OCDE et sur son environnement de travail exceptionnel. Feuilletez en ligne notre Guide de gestion du personnel afin d’en savoir plus sur tous les aspects touchant aux ressources humaines de l’Organisation et à notre environnement de travail et sur les mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des agents. "},"videos":{"title":"Videos To Watch","urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T0Q7LtIYg7s&t=7s"]}}},"active":true,"visibility":"PUBLIC","industry":{"id":"nonprofit_organization_mgmt","label":"Non-Profit Organization Management"},"function":{"id":"analyst","label":"Analyst"},"department":{"id":6106611,"label":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},"experienceLevel":{"id":"internship","label":"Internship"},"typeOfEmployment":{"id":"intern","label":"Intern"},"language":{"code":"fr","label":"French","labelNative":"français"}}

item.description: {"id":"744000132794823","name":"Junior Policy Analysts – Education ","uuid":"f01e324f-7905-411a-8360-385a5e613903","jobId":"6b7cf604-3e8c-460f-af57-07c15ddc1275","jobAdId":"661e7f2c-5749-4694-a517-99ba97dc1722","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3195P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000501","valueLabel":"EDU"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL3","valueLabel":"PAL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-06-18T07:49:17.397Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000132794823-junior-policy-analysts-education-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000132794823-junior-policy-analysts-education-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/f01e324f-7905-411a-8360-385a5e613903?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The Directorate for Education and Skills (EDU) leads the Organisation’s work to help member and non-member countries achieve high-quality learning for all, design better skills policies, and turn them into jobs and growth. The Directorate carries this out by providing statistics, analysis and policy advice to countries on a wide range of educational topics. EDU is looking for Junior Policy Analysts. There are positions available in: the Centre for Educational Research and Innovation (CERI) (including the Survey on Social and Emotional Skills [SSES]). CERI has a forward-looking mandate and in particular is looking for support with its work to identify research gaps, develop new methodologies to strengthen the evidence base for education policy, and open up thinking of preferred futures to help align stakeholders and support more agile policy making. the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). PISA is an international survey which aims to evaluate education systems worldwide by testing the skills and knowledge of 15-year-old students nearing the end of their compulsory education. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Under the guidance of a Senior Analyst, the successful candidate will have the following responsibilities. Analysis and drafting Identify emerging issues and research gaps in areas relevant to the work of CERI and PISA. Synthesise qualitative findings and draw meaningful conclusions for education policy. Draft analytical documents for different audiences (policy community, teachers, researchers, general public). Analyse data from international assessments/surveys and from research pilots. Draft assessment frameworks and technical specifications for data collection (PISA). Development of research tools Support the development of innovative tools to collect evidence on emerging topics and/or support greater use of evidence in policy making. Design survey questionnaires, interview protocols and data collection instruments. Support the design and implementation of randomised controlled trials (PISA). Events organisation, representation and liaison Support the organisation and delivery of stakeholder workshops, expert meetings or peer learning seminars, including liasing with experts, developing agendas and preparing presentations. Establish and maintain professional contacts with officials in national administrations, research institutions and other international organisations. Present work in meetings with researchers, delegates from national administrations and in public events. Support work on preparing contracts with experts and contractors and/or coordinating their work (PISA/SSES). "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background An advanced university degree in social sciences, education, economics, psychology, statistics, psychometrics or a related field. Professional Background At least two years of experience in education research or survey work. Strong qualitative and quantitative analytical skills. Proven ability to draft clear, concise, policy-oriented documents in different formats. Proven ability to work well with stakeholders (policy, research and/or practice). Knowledge of teacher policy or education policy (CERI). Experience in futures/scenario building techniques is an asset (CERI). Knowledge of large-scale educational assessments (PISA/SSES). Tools Knowledge of online graphic design tools (e.g. Canva, Adobe Illustrator) would be an asset. Knowledge and experience in the use of software for data management and analysis (PISA/SSES). Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 1); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. Knowledge of other languages would be an asset. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Closing Date This vacancy should be filled as soon as possible, and applications should reach us no later than Thursday 23 July 2026, 23h59 (Paris time) . Contract Duration 12 month fixed-term appointment, with the possibility of renewal to a maximum of 36 months. Please note that our Rules and Regulations stipulate that the mandatory retirement age is 67. What the OECD offers Monthly salary starts at 5 279 EUR, plus allowances based on eligibility, exempt of French income tax. Click here to consult the Staff Regulations applicable to officials of the OECD. Please note that from 1 July 2025, all Official appointments will be made under the OECD’s new contractual modalities . Click here to learn more about what we offer and why the OECD is a great place to work. Click here to browse our People Management Guidebook and learn more about all aspects relating to people at the OECD, our workplace environment and many other policies supporting staff in their daily life. Please note that the appointment may be made at one grade lower in the specified job family, based on the qualifications and professional experience of the selected applicant. This vacancy may be used to create a pool of candidates for comparable positions, both for open-ended and fixed-term functions. Selection Process For retained candidates, the selection process may include a video-recorded interview, job-based assessment and panel interviews. The OECD is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes the applications of all qualified candidates who are nationals of OECD member countries , irrespective of their racial or ethnic origin, opinions or beliefs, gender, sexual orientation, health or disabilities. The OECD promotes an optimal use of resources in order to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. Staff members are encouraged to actively contribute to this goal. "}}},"active":true,"visibility":"PUBLIC","industry":{"id":"nonprofit_organization_mgmt","label":"Non-Profit Organization Management"},"function":{"id":"analyst","label":"Analyst"},"department":{"id":6106611,"label":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},"experienceLevel":{"id":"entry_level","label":"Entry Level"},"typeOfEmployment":{"id":"permanent","label":"Full-time"},"language":{"code":"en","label":"English","labelNative":"English (US)"}}

item.description: {"id":"744000132799479","name":"Analystes juniors des politiques – Éducation ","uuid":"21d772d5-d2ac-403c-978e-8367140f77ea","jobId":"6b7cf604-3e8c-460f-af57-07c15ddc1275","jobAdId":"f564d8b9-8355-4810-ae23-74c4268d0064","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3195P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000501","valueLabel":"EDU"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL3","valueLabel":"PAL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-06-18T07:52:00.787Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000132799479-analystes-juniors-des-politiques-education-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000132799479-analystes-juniors-des-politiques-education-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/21d772d5-d2ac-403c-978e-8367140f77ea?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. La Direction de l’éducation et des compétences (EDU) dirige les travaux de l’Organisation visant à aider les pays membres et non membres à assurer un apprentissage de qualité pour tous, à concevoir de meilleures politiques en matière de compétences et à les traduire en emplois et en croissance. Elle mène ces travaux en fournissant aux pays des statistiques, des analyses et des conseils sur les politiques publiques dans un large éventail de domaines liés à l’éducation. EDU recherche des analystes juniors des politiques. Des postes sont à pourvoir au sein : du Centre pour la recherche et l’innovation dans l’enseignement (CERI), y compris pour l’Enquête sur les compétences sociales et émotionnelles (SSES). Le CERI a un mandat prospectif et recherche en particulier un appui pour ses travaux visant à identifier les lacunes de la recherche, à développer de nouvelles méthodologies afin de renforcer la base factuelle des politiques éducatives, et à ouvrir la réflexion sur les futurs souhaitables afin d’aligner les parties prenantes et de soutenir une élaboration des politiques plus agile. du Programme international pour le suivi des acquis des élèves (PISA). PISA est une enquête internationale qui vise à évaluer les systèmes d’éducation dans le monde entier en testant les compétences et les connaissances des élèves de 15 ans approchant de la fin de leur scolarité obligatoire. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Principales responsabilités Sous la supervision d’un analyste senior, la personne retenue aura les responsabilités suivantes: Analyse et rédaction Identifier les questions émergentes et les lacunes de la recherche dans les domaines pertinents pour les travaux du CERI et de PISA. Synthétiser des résultats qualitatifs et en tirer des conclusions utiles pour les politiques éducatives. Rédiger des documents d’analyse destinés à différents publics : responsables publics, enseignants, chercheurs et grand public. Analyser des données issues d’évaluations/enquêtes internationales et de pilotes de recherche. Rédiger des cadres d’évaluation et des spécifications techniques pour la collecte de données (PISA). Développement d’outils de recherche Contribuer au développement d’outils innovants permettant de recueillir des données probantes sur des sujets émergents et/ou de favoriser une meilleure utilisation des données probantes dans l’élaboration des politiques publiques. Concevoir des questionnaires d’enquête, des protocoles d’entretien et des instruments de collecte de données. Appuyer la conception et la mise en œuvre d’essais contrôlés randomisés (PISA). Organisation d’événements, représentation et liaison Contribuer à l’organisation et à la tenue d’ateliers avec les parties prenantes, de réunions d’experts ou de séminaires d’apprentissage entre pairs, notamment en assurant la liaison avec les experts, en élaborant des ordres du jour et en préparant des présentations. Établir et entretenir des contacts professionnels avec des responsables des administrations nationales, des institutions de recherche et d’autres organisations internationales. Présenter les travaux lors de réunions avec des chercheurs, des délégués des administrations nationales et lors d’événements publics. Contribuer à la préparation de contrats avec des experts et des prestataires et/ou à la coordination de leurs travaux (PISA/SSES). "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil du/de la candidat(e) idéal(e) Formation académique Diplôme universitaire de niveau avancé en sciences sociales, éducation, économie, psychologie, statistiques, psychométrie ou dans un domaine connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins deux ans d’expérience dans la recherche en éducation ou dans les enquêtes. Solides compétences analytiques qualitatives et quantitatives. Capacité avérée à rédiger des documents clairs, concis et orientés vers les politiques publiques, dans différents formats. Capacité avérée à travailler efficacement avec des parties prenantes issues des milieux de l’action publique, de la recherche et/ou de la pratique. Connaissance des politiques relatives aux enseignants ou des politiques éducatives (CERI). Une expérience des techniques de prospective et d’élaboration de scénarios serait un atout (CERI). Connaissance des évaluations éducatives à grande échelle (PISA/SSES). Outils La connaissance d’outils de conception graphique en ligne (p. ex. Canva, Adobe Illustrator) serait un atout. Connaissance et expérience de l’utilisation de logiciels de gestion et d’analyse de données (PISA/SSES). Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 1); Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1); Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1); Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2); Obtention de résultats (niveau 1); Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de compétence 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE. Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, ou disposition à l’apprendre. La connaissance d’autres langues serait un atout. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus sont à pourvoir dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard le jeudi 23 juillet 2026, 23h59 (heure de Paris) . Durée du contrat Engagement à durée déterminée de 12 mois, avec possibilité de renouvellement jusqu’à un maximum de 36 mois. Veuillez noter que notre Règlement stipule que l’âge obligatoire de départ à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Ce que l’OCDE offre Le salaire mensuel commence à 5 279 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter le Statut applicable au personnel de l’OCDE. Veuillez noter qu’à partir du 1er juillet 2025, tous les agents seront engagés selon les nouvelles modalités contractuelles de l’OCDE . Cliquez ici pour en savoir plus sur ce que propose l’OCDE et sur son environnement de travail exceptionnel. Cliquez ici pour feuilleter en ligne notre Guide de gestion du personnel afin d’en savoir plus sur tous les aspects touchant aux ressources humaines de l’Organisation, à notre environnement de travail et aux nombreuses autres mesures destinées à faciliter le quotidien des agents. Veuillez noter que le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) pourra être engagé(e) à un grade inférieur, en fonction de ses qualifications et de son expérience professionnelle. Votre candidature pourra être retenue afin de constituer un vivier de candidats pour des postes équivalents, que ce soit à durée déterminée ou indéterminée. Processus de sélection Pour les candidats retenus, le processus de sélection peut comprendre un entretien vidéo enregistré, une évaluation fondée sur les fonctions du poste et des entretiens avec un jury. L’OCDE est un employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances et accueille les candi

item.title: Chief Operating Officer
item.description: {"id":"744000133080959","name":"Chief Operating Officer","uuid":"0354da2c-f170-415e-b537-0613b57885e3","jobId":"fd15b086-0fcf-4e99-85a2-65a51fd1e3e6","jobAdId":"32a08221-4386-4b6c-99d7-0aaaedaaf5bd","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3114E","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000586","valueLabel":"EXD"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6104231","valueLabel":"Executive Leadership"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"EL3","valueLabel":"EL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-06-19T14:07:23.575Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000133080959-chief-operating-officer","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000133080959-chief-operating-officer?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/0354da2c-f170-415e-b537-0613b57885e3?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" THE OECD – Who we are, what we do The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, whose mission is to build better policies for better lives. We promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work to establish evidence-based international standards and find solutions to a broad range of social, economic and environmental challenges, from improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion. We provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. THE DIRECTORATE FOR CORPORATE OPERATIONS (DCO) The Directorate for Corporate Operations (DCO) is the steward of OECD central operations, on behalf of the Secretary-General. Our focus is on people and their wellbeing; the safety and security of staff, Delegations, visitors, and the OECD’s data; maintaining and sustaining physical and digital infrastructure; and enabling the convening power of the OECD through conferences, meetings and events, whether virtual, physical or hybrid. We provide integrated, strategic and expert advice on corporate operations, policies and management issues to the Secretary-General, Council and Standing Committees, to which we regularly report on corporate matters, also providing compliance and risk management functions. DCO operates in an increasingly complex environment, with mounting fiscal constraints, technological change, including AI, and rising expectations for efficiency, security, and workforce adaptability. DCO plays a leading role in preparing the Organisation for the future of work, ensuring that people, processes, technology and ways of working evolve in an integrated manner to support the OECD’s strategic objectives. DCO is central to safeguarding the OECD’s operational resilience and digital infrastructure, and driving operational efficiency of core corporate systems, while strengthening the Organisation’s capacity to adapt to technological and workforce transformation. DCO is instrumental in strengthening the OECD’s long-term financial sustainability through implementation of the Secretary-General’s corporate reform agenda, the promotion of management excellence, and the delivery of efficiency measures, in close collaboration with the Programme, Budget and Financial Management Service (PBF) and across the OECD. THE POSITION The OECD is looking for a dynamic and visionary Director to provide leadership and strategic direction to corporate operations. Reporting to the Secretary-General, as a key member of the Senior Leadership team, s/he will lead the development and implementation of strategic objectives in support of DCO’s stewardship role, offering high-quality corporate services to the rest of the Organisation. The Chief Operating Officer oversees the Digital, Knowledge and Information Service, the Conference, Security and Infrastructure Service, and the Human Resources Management Service. S/he will be responsible for ensuring that these functions operate in an integrated, coherent and client-focused manner, delivering reliable, efficient and responsive “One DCO” services to the Organisation. The role demands close, trust-based collaboration with the Office of the Secretary-General, PBF, policy directorates and other corporate functions. This position requires an experienced senior executive with an excellent understanding of corporate and operational functions, political processes and effective institutional settings. S/he thrives in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment, and is an innovative strategic thinker with political sensitivity and a strong, demonstrated ability to forge collaboration and teamwork across complex organisational structures. S/he has a proven track record of managing and delivering a complex Programme of Work and Budget (PWB), as well as managing large and diverse teams, while maintaining an effective professional network. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Leadership Lead the Directorate in delivering the work programme in line with the priorities set by Members and the Secretary-General and with the OECD’s strategy for corporate services, operations and management in the PWB. Shape strategic thinking, including the formulation of operations and management strategies, policies, business processes and solutions in line with best practices, ensuring full support for the Organisation to deliver on its mandate through high-quality integrated “One DCO” services. Ensure the Directorate is at the forefront of continuous improvement in processes and delivery across corporate services, operations and management, maintaining systems at leading-edge standards and shaping the OECD’s global contribution. Build trust-based relationships with leadership across the Organisation to support collaboration and teamwork across corporate and policy functions. Support the Office of the Secretary-General, ensuring timely, effective information flows with management and operational insights to support organisational objectives, advising on key priorities and risks. Identify emerging challenges and priorities, implement innovative solutions to enhance effectiveness and efficiency, and build strategic partnerships with key internal and external stakeholders to support delivery of the OECD’s mission and results. Representation and Liaison Represent DCO and the OECD internally and externally, building strategic relationships and partnerships with stakeholders, international organisations and national authorities to advance organisational objectives. Management and Co-ordination Lead the Directorates staff through merit-based talent management and performance development Ensure optimal use of resources, skills and knowledge in support of the Directorate’s business needs, overseeing cost recovery initiatives and financial sustainability, while promoting effective working methods, communication and a positive working environment. Build and lead a cohesive, multicultural and multidisciplinary team, promoting excellence, inclusion and diversity. Ensure effective co-ordination, collaboration and co-operation across the Organisation, including with the Office of the Secretary-General, PBF and policy directorates, to deliver corporate operations and services in the OECD’s decentralised operating model and advance strategic initiatives. Promote the highest professional and ethical standards in line with the OECD’s Code of Conduct in all internal and external matters. Foster an environment where staff can develop and thrive. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic and Professional Background An advanced university degree in Economics, Business Administration, Law or a related subject. An MBA would be an advantage. More than 10 years’ experience in corporate management. Excellent knowledge of current corporate services, operational management and organisational governance issues. Proven record of conducting relations at senior level and within a political decision-making environment. Well-established contacts with key players and stakeholders in relevant international communities. Excellent knowledge of DCO’s core areas, including human resources, information technology, digital transformation and AI, and the management of organisational resources. A demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across organisational boundaries and to build effective partnerships with finance, policy and other corporate functions. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Communication and Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of, or a willingness to learn, the other. Knowledge of other languages would be an asset. Core Competencies Staff in Executive Leadership are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies, which will be assessed as part of this hiring process at level 3: Vision and Strategy; Enable People; Ethics and Integrity; Collaboration and Horizontality; Achieve Results; Innovate and Embrace Change. To learn more about the definitions for each competency, please refer to the OECD Core Competency Framework . Closing Date This

item.description: {"id":"744000133078904","name":"Directeur des opérations/Directrice des opérations","uuid":"330ba96b-e192-425a-b3e6-71395a106112","jobId":"fd15b086-0fcf-4e99-85a2-65a51fd1e3e6","jobAdId":"b8349090-cc79-4946-93c4-c7b74cef92fe","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3114E","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000586","valueLabel":"EXD"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6104231","valueLabel":"Executive Leadership"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"EL3","valueLabel":"EL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-06-19T14:07:54.102Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000133078904-directeur-des-operations-directrice-des-operations","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000133078904-directeur-des-operations-directrice-des-operations?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/330ba96b-e192-425a-b3e6-71395a106112?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’OCDE : qui sommes-nous ? que faisons-nous ? L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui a pour mission de mettre en place des politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Nous œuvrons à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux, qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale. Nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. LA DIRECTION DES OPÉRATIONS (DCO) La Direction des opérations (DCO) administre les services centraux de l’OCDE pour le compte du Secrétaire général. Notre champ d’action couvre les ressources humaines et le bien-être du personnel ; la sûreté et la sécurité du personnel, des délégations, des visiteurs et des données de l’OCDE ; et la maintenance et l’entretien des infrastructures physiques et numériques. Nous permettons en outre à l’OCDE d’exercer son pouvoir fédérateur en organisant des conférences, des réunions et des manifestations, que ce soit à distance, sur place ou dans un format hybride. Nous faisons bénéficier le Secrétaire général, le Conseil et les comités permanents – auxquels nous rendons régulièrement compte des affaires internes – de nos conseils stratégiques et de notre expertise quant aux fonctions opérationnelles, aux politiques institutionnelles et aux questions liées à la gestion de l’Organisation, en suivant une approche intégrée, tout en assurant des fonctions de contrôle de conformité et de gestion des risques. DCO mène ses activités dans un environnement de plus en plus complexe, marqué par des contraintes budgétaires croissantes, des évolutions technologiques, dont l’IA, et des attentes grandissantes en matière d’efficience, de sécurité et d’adaptabilité des ressources humaines. Elle joue un rôle de premier plan pour préparer l’Organisation au travail de demain, en veillant à ce que le personnel, les processus, les technologies et les modes de travail évoluent de manière intégrée pour contribuer à la réalisation des objectifs stratégiques de l’OCDE. DCO assume une fonction essentielle pour préserver la résilience des activités de l’OCDE et son infrastructure numérique, et pour favoriser l’efficience opérationnelle des systèmes centraux de l’Organisation, tout en renforçant la capacité de l’Organisation à s’adapter aux évolutions technologiques et à la transformation des ressources humaines. Elle joue un rôle déterminant dans le renforcement de la viabilité financière à long terme de l’OCDE en mettant en œuvre le programme de réformes institutionnelles du Secrétaire général, en promouvant l’excellence en matière de gestion et en prenant des mesures au service de l’efficience, en étroite collaboration avec le Service du Programme, du Budget et de la gestion financière (PBF) et toutes les autres composantes de l’OCDE. LE POSTE L’OCDE recherche un·e Directeur/Directrice dynamique et visionnaire pour montrer la voie et donner des orientations stratégiques aux fonctions opérationnelles. Sous l’autorité directe du Secrétaire général et en tant que membre clé de l’équipe de direction, il/elle pilotera la formulation et la mise en œuvre d’objectifs stratégiques à l’appui du rôle que joue DCO dans l’administration des ressources, en fournissant des services de soutien de qualité au reste de l’Organisation. Le Directeur des opérations/La Directrice des opérations supervise le Service du numérique, de la connaissance et de l’information, le Service des conférences, de la sécurité et de l’infrastructure, et le Service de la Gestion des ressources humaines. Il/Elle devra s’assurer que ces fonctions s’organisent de manière intégrée, cohérente et centrée sur le client, de sorte à fournir à l’Organisation des services fiables, efficients et réactifs à partir d’un guichet unique DCO. Ce poste repose sur une collaboration étroite et fondée sur la confiance avec le Cabinet du Secrétaire général, PBF, les directions de substance et les autres services internes. La personne choisie pour exercer ces fonctions de haut responsable devra avoir de l’expérience, assortie d’une excellente compréhension des questions relatives aux fonctions institutionnelles et opérationnelles, aux mécanismes de l’action publique et à l’efficacité des cadres institutionnels. Il/Elle donnera toute sa mesure dans un environnement dynamique et pluridisciplinaire, et aura la capacité de réfléchir à des stratégies innovantes et de respecter les sensibilités politiques, ainsi qu’une solide aptitude avérée à nouer des liens de collaboration et à travailler en équipe au sein de structures organisationnelles complexes. Il/Elle devra avoir démontré son aptitude à gérer et exécuter un Programme de travail et Budget (PTB) complexe, ainsi qu’à encadrer de grandes équipes empreintes de diversité, tout en entretenant un réseau de contacts professionnels fructueux. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Direction et encadrement Piloter la mise en œuvre du programme de travail par la Direction conformément aux priorités définies par les Membres et le Secrétaire général et à la stratégie de l’OCDE pour les services, les opérations et la gestion internes, telles qu’elles figurent dans le PTB. Orienter la réflexion stratégique, y compris en élaborant des stratégies d’exploitation et de gestion, des politiques à mener, des processus opérationnels et des solutions conformes aux meilleures pratiques, de sorte à apporter un soutien complet à l’Organisation dans l’exécution de son mandat grâce à des services de qualité intégrés à partir d’un guichet unique DCO. Veiller à ce que la Direction soit à l’avant-garde de l’amélioration continue des processus et de la mise en œuvre à l’échelle des services, des opérations et de la gestion internes, en s’assurant que les systèmes continuent de répondre aux normes les plus avancées et en donnant forme à la contribution mondiale de l’OCDE. Nouer des relations fondées sur la confiance avec l’équipe dirigeante de l’Organisation à l’appui de la collaboration et du travail d’équipe entre les services de soutien et les directions de substance. Apporter son soutien au Cabinet du Secrétaire général en assurant une circulation rapide et efficace des informations, notamment des éclairages en matière de gestion et sur le plan opérationnel, afin de contribuer à la réalisation des objectifs de l’Organisation, en prodiguant des conseils quant aux priorités et risques clés. Identifier les défis et priorités émergents, mettre en œuvre des solutions innovantes pour renforcer l’efficacité et l’efficience des activités, et nouer avec des parties prenantes internes et externes clés des partenariats stratégiques utiles pour mener à bien la mission de l’OCDE et obtenir les résultats voulus. Représentation et liaison Représenter DCO et l’OCDE en interne et à l’extérieur, en établissant des relations et des partenariats stratégiques avec les parties prenantes, les organisations internationales et les autorités nationales, au service des objectifs de l’Organisation. Gestion et coordination Superviser les équipes de la Direction en s’appuyant sur une gestion des talents fondée sur le mérite et en s’attachant à améliorer les performances. Veiller à l’usage optimal des ressources, des compétences et des connaissances pour aider à répondre aux besoins opérationnels de la Direction, en supervisant les initiatives de recouvrement des coûts et les questions relatives à la viabilité financière, tout en promouvant des méthodes de travail efficaces et une communication de qualité dans un environnement de travail positif. Constituer et diriger une équipe soudée, multiculturelle et pluridisciplinaire, en favorisant l’excellence, l’inclusion e

item.description:
{"id":"744000134500801","name":"Head of Co-ordination Secretariat Unit","uuid":"b1686490-195c-46fa-ac0a-791e690812a4","jobId":"64281d4a-c932-48b9-bc8e-534ff9c8be37","jobAdId":"7ae0a2df-9fa1-48ef-a718-452c47ae8da3","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3216D","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001129","valueLabel":"RPS"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL8","valueLabel":"PAL8"}],"releasedDate":"2026-06-26T15:16:33.539Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000134500801-head-of-co-ordination-secretariat-unit","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000134500801-head-of-co-ordination-secretariat-unit?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/b1686490-195c-46fa-ac0a-791e690812a4?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The International Service for Remunerations and Pensions (ISRP) delivers specialised services to the Co-ordinated Organisations and to Associated Organisations, covering salary studies, statistical analysis, surveys, remuneration and pension management, legal advisory services and fund management. The ISRP is administratively attached to the OECD. The Co-ordination Secretariat Unit provides secretariat, legal and governance support to the Committee of Representatives of the Secretaries/Directors-General (CRSG), the Co-ordinating Committee on Remuneration (CCR), the Pensions Administrative Committee of the Co-ordinated Organisations (CAPOC), and related bilateral, tripartite and working group meetings. The Unit prepares meeting documentation, technical notes, proposals and reports; provides legal and administrative support on pensions and remuneration matters; monitors developments in pension schemes of other international organisations; and supports agreements on the transfer of pension rights. The ISRP is looking for a Head of Co-ordination Secretariat Unit to lead and provide senior institutional legal counsel, governance support and co-ordination across the ISRP’s legal, committee and stakeholder-facing activities. Reporting to the Head of the ISRP, the incumbent will ensure high-quality legal analysis, sound interpretation of applicable rules and regulations, effective support to committees and working groups, and the timely delivery of legally robust advice and documentation. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities 
 
Strategic legal advice and institutional governance Lead the provision of senior legal analysis and advice on pensions, remuneration, institutional obligations, governance arrangements and the interpretation of applicable rules and regulations Advise the Head of the International Service for Remunerations and Pensions (ISRP), the Committee of Representatives of the Secretaries/Directors-General (CRSG), the Co-ordinating Committee on Remuneration (CCR), the Pensions Administrative Committee of the Co-ordinated Organisations (CAPOC) and client organisations on complex legal, governance and procedural matters. Oversee the preparation and quality assurance of legal opinions, technical notes, committee proposals, reports and institutional documents submitted to the CRSG, the CCR and CAPOC. Ensure that legal advice, institutional documents and committee submissions are clear, consistent, risk-aware and aligned with the applicable legal and governance frameworks. Lead the drafting, review and presentation of complex legal, governance, policy and institutional documents in both English and French, ensuring that advice and analysis are clear, accurate, well-structured and tailored to senior legal and non-legal audiences in an international context. Committee secretariat and stakeholder co-ordination Direct the Unit’s secretariat support to the CRSG, the CCR, CAPOC, bilateral, tripartite and working group meetings, including agendas, Chair briefings, summary records, document distribution and follow-up of decisions. Ensure effective co-ordination with ISRP units, OECD legal services, committee representatives, Co-ordinated Organisations and Associated Organisations on legal, governance and policy-related matters. Represent the Unit in relevant internal and external discussions and maintain trusted working relationships with senior stakeholders, ensuring timely, accurate and professional delivery of advice and documentation. Ensure clear and effective written and oral communication in both English and French with committee representatives, senior stakeholders, Co-ordinated Organisations and Associated Organisations and International Financial Institutions, including the preparation of concise briefings, records, conclusions and follow-up documentation. Regulatory, contractual and dispute-related work Lead and oversee the drafting, review and negotiation of legal and institutional instruments, including regulations, memoranda of agreement, exchanges of letters and arrangements relating to special assistance or transfer of pension rights. Support litigation-related work and complex individual cases by providing legal analysis, drafting input and co-ordination with relevant legal services and stakeholders. Provide legal analysis and drafting input in relation to litigation-related matters, complex individual cases and dispute-related questions, in co-ordination with relevant legal services and stakeholders. Monitor legal and institutional developments affecting pension schemes, remuneration frameworks and international administrative law, and assess their implications for the ISRP and the organisations it serves. Data protection and information governance Oversee legal and governance aspects of data protection, confidentiality and information handling within the Unit’s areas of responsibility. Ensure that legal documentation, committee records and sensitive information are handled in accordance with applicable OECD rules, procedures and good governance standards. Orchestrate the implementation of data protection and information governance improvements affecting the Unit’s legal, committee and stakeholder-facing activities. Service-wide co-ordination and delivery Ensure that the Unit contributes effectively to the ISRP’s broader service delivery, including support to Co-ordinated Organisations, Associated Organisations and International Financial Institutions where relevant. Provide legal and governance input to cross-unit projects involving pensions, payroll, actuarial studies, compensation and benefits, data protection, communication and services to external stakeholders. Support the continuous improvement of Unit processes, documentation standards and knowledge management practices to strengthen efficiency, consistency and service quality. Unit leadership and people management Lead, manage and develop the Co-ordination Secretariat Unit, setting priorities, allocating work and ensuring high-quality delivery across legal, committee and stakeholder-support activities. Foster a collaborative, inclusive and accountable working environment, supporting staff development, performance management, knowledge sharing and continuity of expertise. Promote a culture of integrity, sound judgement, service orientation and continuous improvement within the Unit. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile 
 
Academic Background An advanced university degree in law, preferably with a specialisation in public law, international administrative law, institutional law, international civil service law or another field relevant to the role. Professional Background Extensive professional experience providing legal advice in an international, intergovernmental or comparable institutional environment, including on the interpretation and application of rules, regulations and governance frameworks. Proven experience supporting or advising committees, governing bodies or senior management, including the preparation of legal opinions, technical notes, reports, proposals and institutional documentation. Strong knowledge of pensions, remuneration, international civil service law or institutional administrative law would be a distinct advantage. Proven ability to advise on complex legal, contractual and procedural matters, including memoranda of agreement, exchanges of letters, transfer of pension rights, dispute-related matters and governance documentation.
