item.title: E T Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org E astern and Southern Africa Regional Context The Eastern and Southern Africa (AFE) region is diverse, spanning low-income and lower-middle-income countries and a number of upper-middle-income borrowers, with wide variation in health outcomes, fiscal space, and institutional capacity. Many countries face a high and evolving burden of disease alongside persistent inequities in access and quality, while also managing recurrent shocks, including climate-related hazards, epidemics, and food and fuel price volatility. In this context, the World Bank supports governments through analytics, policy dialogue, and financing to strengthen human capital and build more resilient health systems and essential public health functions. Through its Health, Nutrition, and Population (HNP) Global Practice, the World Bank supports countries’ efforts towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and providing quality, affordable, equity-focused health services to everyone regardless of their ability to pay by strengthening primary health care systems and reducing the financial risks associated with ill-health. Some of the ongoing health and nutrition challenges in the AFE region include: • Triple burden of disease and epidemiological transition: a continuing burden of communicable diseases (including HIV, TB, malaria and outbreaks), persistently high maternal, newborn and child mortality in many settings, and a rapidly growing burden of NCDs and injuries—often coexisting within the same populations and health systems. • Health system constraints and inequities: persistent gaps in access to quality essential services, especially for rural, remote, and vulnerable populations, driven by constraints in the health workforce, medicines and supply chains, service readiness, governance and accountability, and limited fiscal space and financial protection for households. • Nutrition and food insecurity: high levels of child stunting and micronutrient deficiencies in several countries, alongside rising overweight/obesity, compounded by food price shocks and climate variability that affect diets and worsen vulnerability throughout the life course. Summary of Botswana and Southern Africa Health Portfolio The World Bank’s health portfolio in Botswana combines investment financing with targeted technical assistance (TA) and analytics to advance the Government’s priorities on UHC, primary health care revitalization, and health security. The portfolio is anchored by the Botswana Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPRR) Project, which supports preparedness and response; strengthened surveillance, laboratory, and emergency management systems; and investments in core enablers, including digital public health infrastructure and availability of quality data. In parallel, the World Bank provides TA supporting sector planning and governance such as development of the Health Sector Strategic Plan, digital health and data use (interoperability, registries, and routine data quality and use), and improvements in supply chain performance and regulatory systems for health products. This work is complemented by analytics to inform reforms and investments, including on health financing and efficiency, equity, and service delivery performance to strengthen human capital and system resilience. Across southern Africa, the World Bank’s health engagement in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho combines investment lending with analytical and advisory services to strengthen primary health care, improve quality of care, and build more resilient health systems. In Lesotho, the portfolio includes an active health and nutrition system strengthening project focused on expanding coverage and improving the quality of essential maternal and child health, nutrition, and NCD services, alongside reforms to strengthen stewardship and service delivery readiness. There are opportunities to support the preparation of new operations and enhance the scope of TA and advisory work in southern Africa. In South Africa and Namibia, support is anchored in policy dialogue and analytics, including public expenditure and efficiency work, to inform reforms that expand effective coverage, reduce inequities, and improve the sustainability of health financing. Objectives and Scope of Work In light of the growing health portfolio, the HAEH2 team seeks an Extended-Term Consultant (ETC) with experience as a Health Specialist/Economist to provide day-to-day technical and operational support to HNP task teams and Government counterparts, primarily in Botswana and, as needed, across the southern Africa portfolio. The scope of work includes: • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in Botswana. The ETC will support implementation of the Botswana health portfolio (including the HEPRR project) by monitoring progress against the results framework (including support to M E, data quality, and results reporting) and follow-up on agreed actions; supporting planning and delivery of implementation support missions; and contributing to key operational deliverables (aide memoires, management briefs, and client-facing communications). The ETC will help convene consultations with the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders, monitor progress, and coordinate with fiduciary, safeguards, and technical colleagues to ensure timely, integrated support. • Help ensure close coordination with government, development partners, and the CMU and World Bank teams across other sectors in Botswana. The ETC will facilitate coordination and information flow across the Ministry of Health and other relevant agencies, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the Country Management Unit and colleagues in other sectors) to align priorities, timelines, and implementation support. The ETC will play a pivotal role in providing strategic sectoral guidance to the CMU and provide key inputs into country management reviews and documents. • Support policy dialogue with the Ministry of Health, relevant national institutions, and other stakeholders. The ETC will support policy dialogue by preparing briefs, talking points, and presentations, synthesizing implementation experience, sector analytics, and international lessons. The ETC will help translate discussions into clear decisions and follow-up actions to inform priority reforms in primary health care, health security, health financing, and other system strengthening areas. • Provide technical and operational support to the health portfolio in southern Africa, as needed. The ETC will support task teams in South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho, including assistance with preparation and follow-up of missions and key deliverables, and contributions to selected analytical and advisory work (e.g., service delivery performance, health financing and efficiency, and health security). Duties and Accountabilities: The ETC’s key tasks and activities will include but are not limited to: • Support implementation support for HEPRR and other Botswana portfolio activities, including monitoring implementation and results; consolidating inputs across technical, fiduciary and ESF colleagues; and proactively following up with counterparts on agreed actions. • Contribute to the planning, preparation, and follow-up of missions, technical consultations, and key portfolio engagements, including drafting agenda/talking points, preparing briefing packages, and drafting aide memoires and progress reports, and management updates as requested by Task Team Leaders. • Support monitoring and evaluation (M E) and results reporting for the portfolio, including maintaining an M E implementation plan, supporting updates to the results framework and indicator definitions as needed, compiling and quality-checking data and narrative inputs for progress reporting. • Provide technical inputs to project implementation, including review of technical specifications and Terms of References for goods and services (e.g., medical and laboratory equipment, digital systems, and technical assistance), and advise on alignment with good practice, user requirements, and World Bank procurement principles (in coordination with procurement specialists). • Support stakeholder coordination across Government, development partners, and World Bank teams (including the CMU and other sectors) by preparing coordination notes, documenting decisions, and escalating issues requiring management attention. • Contribute to selected analytical and advisory activities (ASA), including literature and data review, drafting sections of technical notes and reports, and supporting quality assurance to ensure analytical rigor and consistency of messaging. • As needed, provide operational and analytical support to the southern Africa health portfolio (South Africa, Namibia, Eswatini, and Lesotho). • Maintain well-organized records of key documents and correspondence; support timely sharing of information within task teams; and contribute to knowledge management by capturing lessons learned and good practices.

item.title: Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org Global practice for Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) The Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Department leads the World Bank Group’s policy dialogue and engagement with countries to strengthen macro‑fiscal foundations, including debt sustainability, debt management, and domestic resource mobilization, and to accelerate job and inclusive growth. FPG links the macroeconomic dialogue with programs focused on expanding the role of the private sector in economic development. In our day-to-day engagement with countries, FPG supports Ministries of Finance, Planning, Economy, Industry and Trade, and Production in their pursuit of reform agendas conducive to strengthening job creation through inclusive growth led by the private sector. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/topic/fiscal-policy-and-growth Background and General description The FPG unit for Southern Africa and East Africa (EAEM2) is looking for an Economist to be based in Luanda, Angola. The selected candidate will contribute substantially to analytical work and lending operations. She or he will report to the FPG Practice Manager covering the EAEM2 unit, which comprises 14 countries over three Country Management Units: AECS1 (South Africa, Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia), AECS2 (Mozambique, Comoros, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles), and AECC2 (Angola, DRC, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Burundi). The unit has recently seen a significant increase in work program including through Development Policy Operations (DPOs) in countries that had previously not been borrowing. The unit has a strong focus on promoting prudent macro-fiscal policies, structural reforms, inclusive growth, and job creation. The World Bank's Fiscal Policy and Growth (FPG) Global Practice has been a key partner to the Government of Angola in supporting the country's transition from an oil-dependent economy toward a more diversified, inclusive, and private sector-led growth model. Over the past decade, FPG's engagement has included successive programmatic Development Policy Financing operations—such as the Growth and Inclusion DPF series and, most recently, the Green, Resilient, Inclusive Growth, and Diversification DPL series, which included an innovative debt-for-development swap. These operations have supported reforms in fiscal consolidation and resilience, fiscal transparency, and state-owned enterprise governance and restructuring. The work program is underpinned by rigorous analytical products, including the Angola Public Finance Review, the Country Economic Memorandum and annual Economic updates. As a an Economist for EAEM2, you will be expected to contribute to the country team covering Angola and São Tomé and Príncipe, as well as the regional FPG team working on other countries as needed. The Country Economist will be based in Luanda and work closely with the Country Manager, Senior Country Economist and Lead Economist and report to the FPG Practice Manager covering Angola and São Tomé and Príncipe. You will contribute to ongoing efforts to help Angola strengthen fiscal and debt sustainability, expand non-oil revenue mobilization, and build the macroeconomic foundations needed for sustained, inclusive growth and economic diversification. The Country Economist will: • Contribute to FPG Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) in the areas of macroeconomic and fiscal management, macro modelling and data work, and public finance; • Contribute to the design of the operational and analytical work in alignment with the job creation, economic growth and poverty alleviation objectives of the country; • Serve as a task leader or a team member for country-specific financing operations and/or analytical and advisory services; • Support the Country Management Unit (CMU) in the implementation of the World Bank's program in Angola. • Establish and develop strong partnerships with other bilateral and multilateral agencies, increasing cooperation and leveraging Bank resources in analytical and operational work; • Contribute to the dissemination of the Bank’s knowledge products to a wider audience, including civil society, academia, and other key stakeholders. • Collect, analyze and maintain economic and financial data and information related to Angola’s economy, and communicate findings in concise and clear form. • Maintain macroeconomic databases and regularly prepare updated medium-term macroeconomic projections. Use/run economic/financial models and toolkits using existing software packages, or World Bank's own models;

item.title: Upstream & Advisory Manager Manufacturing & Services (M&S) - Africa
item.description: IFC — a member of the World Bank Group — is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . IFC is seeking an Upstream Advisory Manager for its Manufacturing Services (M S) department in Africa. The Manager will be responsible for IFC's efforts to enable investment opportunities, enhance investment outcomes, improve investment conditions and deliver development impact through upstream and advisory interventions across Manufacturing Services sectors in Africa. The role will support IFC's strategic objectives under IFC 3.0 by helping create markets, develop investable opportunities, strengthen private sector participation, and advance impactful sector initiatives across the region. The Manager will serve as a member of the Africa M S Management Team and will work closely with Regional Industry Managers, Joint Country Representatives, Global Industry teams, World Bank counterparts and Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) to formulate market creation strategies, scale development impact and support the generation of investment opportunities. The Manager will also ensure that upstream and advisory interventions are designed from the outset to support upstream mobilization, including by crowding in partners, sponsors, DFIs, donors and private capital around priority market creation initiatives. The Manager will oversee a joint Upstream and Advisory team and ensure coordinated delivery across the continuum of IFC operations, including market creation, project development, client preparation, investment support, and portfolio value creation. Duties and Accountabilities People and Resource Responsibilities • Lead and manage the Upstream Advisory unit and ensure the team is high-performing, collaborative, and aligned with IFC's strategic priorities. • Mentor and develop staff and promote opportunities for professional growth, mobility and continued learning. • Actively contribute as a member of the Africa M S Management Team. • Strengthen collaboration among upstream, advisory and investment teams to maximize development impact and business outcomes. • Manage resources, budgets, and donor funding efficiently to maximize operational effectiveness. Strategic Responsibilities • Formulate and implement upstream and advisory strategies for the Manufacturing Services sectors in Africa in coordination with the Regional Industry Director, Regional Industry Managers, WBG Country Representatives and Global Industry teams. • Support implementation of IFC country business plans, sector strategies and World Bank Group priorities through upstream and advisory interventions. • Lead market creation efforts that expand private sector participation and unlock new opportunities for investment. • Identify upstream opportunities with strong potential to mobilize partners, sponsors, donors, DFIs and private capital in support of IFC's market creation and investment objectives. • Embed upstream mobilization considerations into sector strategies, country business plans and priority initiatives, including tourism, gas-for-power, manufacturing competitiveness, value chain development and other high-impact sectors. • Develop scalable interventions, including job creation, productivity enhancement, competitiveness, inclusion, climate outcomes, and economic transformation. • Advance strategic regional initiatives in tourism, gas-for-power, manufacturing competitiveness, value chain development, and other priority sectors. • Leverage IFC's global sector expertise, product innovation and lessons learned to inform strategy, project design and market creation efforts. • Collaborate closely with Global Industry teams to identify emerging trends, replicate successful business models and adapt global best practices to African markets. Business Responsibilities • Enable investment opportunities by incubating high-impact projects, developing new markets, and preparing clients for investment. • Lead upstream mobilization efforts by identifying, structuring and advancing opportunities that can attract co-investors, sponsors, donors, DFIs and other partners around IFC-led market creation initiatives. • Work with Regional Industry Managers, investment teams and partnerships colleagues to translate upstream engagements into investable opportunities with clear pathways for capital mobilization. • Support the development of scalable platforms, programmatic approaches and partnership models that can mobilize resources and private sector participation beyond individual transactions. • Enhance investment outcomes through advisory and upstream interventions that improve development impact, operational performance, and sustainability. • Improve investment conditions by supporting sector reforms, market development activities, and private sector participation. • Deliver measurable development impact through upstream and advisory interventions. • Support initiatives that contribute to job creation, economic inclusion, industrial development, private sector competitiveness, and climate resilience. • Advance strategic initiatives in tourism, gas-for-power and other high-impact sectors that can catalyze economic growth and private investment. • Work closely with Regional Industry Managers and investment teams to improve conversion of upstream opportunities into investment transactions. • Track upstream mobilization outcomes, including partner commitments, donor resources, co-financing opportunities and private capital enabled through upstream and advisory work. • Ensure a high standard of project design, implementation, monitoring and development effectiveness across the portfolio. Client and Stakeholder Responsibilities • Serve as a principal focal point for collaboration with IBRD, MIGA, Joint Country Representatives and other World Bank Group partners on Manufacturing Services market creation initiatives. • Build and maintain strategic relationships with governments, regulators, sponsors, investors, industry associations, development partners and private sector stakeholders. • Convene and mobilize public and private stakeholders around priority sector platforms and upstream initiatives, with a focus on unlocking investment and scaling development impact. • Convene relevant stakeholders to address market constraints and unlock investment opportunities. • Foster integrated World Bank Group solutions that combine policy reform, advisory support and investment opportunities. Knowledge Capture and Management • Identify game-changing trends, technologies and business models with potential for high development impact across the Manufacturing Services sectors. • Serve as a bridge between Africa operations and IFC's global knowledge platform, ensuring that global expertise, sector insights and innovative practices are effectively applied to local market creation efforts. • Contribute African market insights and operational lessons to IFC's global knowledge agenda. • Strengthen IFC's external brand and reputation as a leader in market creation and private sector development.

item.title: WBG Pioneer - Data Analysis Intern
item.description: WBG Pioneer Background/Organizational Context The World Bank Group’s Women, Business and the Law (WBL) project examines laws and regulations affecting women’s prospects as entrepreneurs and employees across 190 economies. Its goal is to inform policy discussions on how to remove legal restrictions on women and promote research on how to improve women’s economic inclusion. The Women, Business and the Law index serves as a road map for reform by capturing three interdependent pillars that together shape women’s access to jobs: laws, policies and institutions, and enforcement perceptions across ten topics: Safety, Mobility, Work, Pay, Marriage, Parenthood, Childcare, Entrepreneurship, Assets, and Pension. Duties and Responsibilities Data Preparation, Cleaning, and Quality Control: • Clean, validate, and reconcile large, multi-source datasets, identifying and correcting errors in data values, structures, and formulas. • Develop and apply systematic processes to standardize, map, and reconcile data across teams, systems, and file formats, while using automated checks to flag inconsistencies for review. • Prepare API-ready data outputs, including JSON files, for data feeds, website visualizations, and other digital applications. • Develop and implement data-cleaning protocols, validation rules, and automated quality checks. Conduct data audits and produce monitoring and quality-assurance reports to identify issues and track their resolution. Data Analysis: • Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, and actionable insights, and prepare analytical, progress, and monitoring reports using tools such as Excel or Python. • Present findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences through reports, presentations, and other communication products. AI Integration: • Pilot AI-powered workflow to enhance data quality, integrity, and operational efficiency. • Conduct AI-driven analysis to support data validation and insights generation. • Establish monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to track AI model performance and ensure continuous improvement. • Ensure transparency and documentation of AI workflows, including prompt engineering, versioning, and reproducibility. • Suggest ways to automate verification of survey responses with primary data sources, check survey responses against each other and follow up with respondents until a final, verified country profile is produced. • Identify and mitigate risks related to bias, accuracy, and reliability of AI-generated outputs. Data Visualization: • Interpret complex datasets and develop clear, intuitive visualization concepts that communicate key findings to technical and non-technical audiences. • Develop prototypes, mock-ups, and data visualization products for dashboards, websites, reports, and other digital applications, using tools such as Tableau, Flourish, Power BI, or similar platforms to create compelling, user-friendly visualizations.
item.dc:creator: World Bank Group

item.title: WBG Pioneer - Financial Inclusion and Infrastructure Intern
item.description: WBG Pioneer Background/Organizational Context Our team (Financial Services Sector/Financial Inclusion) belongs to ‘the Knowledge Bank’—a part of the World Bank Group that designs and delivers ‘scalable solutions’: products or policies that help low- and middle-income countries address their most urgent development challenges. Our focus is on financial inclusion of individuals and businesses (micro, small and medium enterprises—MSMEs) and enabling digital financial services (DFS). To get there, we facilitate legal and regulatory reforms, and help countries set up their ‘financial infrastructures’: payment, clearing and settlement systems, as well as credit and collateral registries. We work globally and focus on our field of expertise rather than on any particular country or region. Because of that, many of our colleagues find themselves working with governments or regulators from many different places. It is not unusual to be simultaneously working on projects in, for example, North Africa and Latin America. Providing confidential, impartial, and evidence-based advice to central banks and other financial sector regulators around the world is the most important part of our work. However, we also spend time on developing and managing databases related to financial inclusion and infrastructure, helping other World Bank Group colleagues if they need our expertise in their projects, conducting research on financial inclusion and representing the World Bank Group at global standard-setting bodies such as the Financial Stability Board or the Bank for International Settlements. Duties and Responsibilities The intern will be helping us with day-to-day data analyst work and have the opportunity to experience how we work with clients by attending meetings and helping prepare presentations and briefs. They will also be expected to: • Design and execute creative strategies to find and acquire relevant data, including web scraping, integrating APIs, use of administrative datasets, survey data and social media. • Develop code in Stata, R, or Python to analyze data and automate workflows. • Draft sections of reports and presentations based on project work. • Support the use and integration of LLMs for drafting, coding, and handling complex data problems, including building agentic workflows, connecting models to data via protocols like MCP, and integrating AI into research. In addition to helping with ad-hoc data work, they will pursue a research or operational project, where they will be expected to take the leading role and try to deliver actionable insights with minimal supervision. The projects envisioned for the interns in the winter cycle include: • Integrating our team’s data with a corporate AI platform. This will require proactively reaching out to colleagues across the team who maintain different datasets and, for example, aligning those dataset’s formats with what is required by the Model Context Protocol server used by the World Bank Group-wide platform. The intern may also have to think creatively about how to make retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) work with data formats that are not easy to ingest, or are inefficient with their use of tokens (from PowerBI dashboards to poor-quality scanned PDFs). • Using social media data on-chain records to find information about the use of cryptocurrencies for payments, and derive additional insights from it (for example, estimate unofficial exchange rates). • Design workflow for AI-assisted review of various documents—for example, procurement documentation, payment scheme rules, or project proposals. We are also open to discussing other projects—we particularly encourage applications from students whose honors/graduation theses or other university research projects are related to our team’s remit.

item.title: WBG Pioneer - AI Engineer Intern
item.description: WBG Pioneer Background/Organizational Context The Integrity Vice Presidency (INT) investigates and helps prevent fraud and corruption in World Bank Group–financed projects. Within INT, the Data Lab is a multidisciplinary team spanning data, AI, analytics, and cloud engineering that builds and operates production-grade, responsible AI and data solutions to enable and streamline INT's core business processes. This 150-day internship offers a hands-on opportunity to work at the frontier of enterprise agentic AI. Under the direct supervision and mentorship of the Data Lab Team Lead, the AI Engineer Intern will learn to design, develop, and deploy AI agents that support INT's core functions. The role is well suited to a fast learner who stays aligned with industry trends in enterprise agentic AI and is eager to apply modern AI techniques to real-world integrity use cases within a secure, governed cloud environment. Duties and Responsibilities • Learn and apply the Data Lab's AI development practices to help design, build, and fine-tune AI agents and LLM-based solutions that streamline INT business processes. • Develop, test, and iterate on prompts to improve the accuracy, relevance, and reliability of AI outputs. • Support the optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines—indexing, retrieval, and inference—for INT's AI agents. • Use Azure cloud resources for data storage, processing, and retrieval to support AI model requirements. • Collaborate with front-end, back-end, and DevOps team members to integrate AI models into applications and resolve integration issues. • Explore and evaluate emerging enterprise agentic AI frameworks and tools, sharing findings and recommendations with the team. • Maintain clear, up-to-date documentation of AI models, prompts, design decisions, and change logs to ensure transparency and traceability. • Participate in team meetings, provide regular progress updates, and present work to the Data Lab Team Lead and management.

item.description: {"id":"744000139632209","name":"Architecte de solutions d’IA (collaboration avec les métiers) ","uuid":"300f1fce-619c-45bd-aad8-dce61b3827dc","jobId":"29102e6e-0cd5-47bf-9964-fdbdb968a24a","jobAdId":"d5737036-fd6e-45b0-a167-e7e4190d8d50","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3295N","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000430","valueLabel":"DKI"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"7038891","valueLabel":"Corporate Functions"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"CF4","valueLabel":"CF4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-07-24T14:57:39.428Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139632209-architecte-de-solutions-d-ia-collaboration-avec-les-metiers-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000139632209-architecte-de-solutions-d-ia-collaboration-avec-les-metiers-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/300f1fce-619c-45bd-aad8-dce61b3827dc?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale composée de 38 pays membres, qui œuvre à l’élaboration de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques susceptibles d’améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations partout dans le monde. En collaboration avec les gouvernements, les responsables de l’action publique et les citoyens, nous contribuons à l’établissement de normes internationales fondées sur des données probantes et à la recherche de solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques et de créer des emplois, de favoriser une éducation de qualité ou de lutter contre l’évasion fiscale internationale, nous offrons un forum unique et un centre de connaissances consacré aux données et à l’analyse, à l’échange d’expériences, au partage des meilleures pratiques, ainsi qu’aux conseils en matière de politiques publiques et à l’élaboration de normes internationales. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" La Direction exécutive (EXD) assure la gestion des ressources de l’OCDE pour le compte du Secrétaire général et est responsable des personnes et du bien-être, de la gestion budgétaire, de la sécurité, des infrastructures ainsi que des activités de rassemblement de l’OCDE. EXD fournit des services institutionnels et des conseils stratégiques en matière de gestion et de politiques internes au Secrétaire général, au Conseil et aux comités permanents. Elle exerce également, dans son domaine de compétence, des fonctions liées à la conformité et à la gestion des risques, dans un environnement dynamique axé sur l’excellence en matière de gestion. Au sein de la Direction exécutive (EXD), le Service du numérique, des connaissances et de l’information (DKI) est chargé de superviser l’infrastructure et les opérations informatiques de l’Organisation, d’assurer la sécurité numérique et la gestion de l’information, ainsi que de fournir des produits et services numériques et autres services liés aux technologies de l’information. EXD/DKI soutient également l’adoption sécurisée des technologies d’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans l’ensemble de l’Organisation. À la suite de la recommandation du Groupe de travail de l’OCDE sur l’IA et conformément à l’évolution des besoins de l’OCDE dans ce domaine, la division CAI a été créée afin de soutenir l’adoption sécurisée des technologies d’IA dans l’ensemble de l’Organisation. CAI est chargée de superviser le passage d’une phase initiale d’expérimentation à une adoption à grande échelle de l’IA, de l’exploration à l’institutionnalisation, afin de produire une valeur tangible, en mettant clairement l’accent sur le renforcement de l’impact organisationnel, l’amélioration de la productivité et la transformation des méthodes de travail. Dans le cadre de ces fonctions, vous travaillerez au sein de l’AI Lab d’EXD/DKI/CAIO. L’AI Lab contribue au développement et à la mise en œuvre opérationnelle du cadre institutionnel de l’OCDE relatif à l’IA, en identifiant, concevant et mettant en œuvre des solutions d’IA à forte valeur ajoutée qui renforcent les capacités analytiques et opérationnelles de l’Organisation. En tant que principal point de contact entre l’AI Lab et les directions de l’OCDE, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes métiers afin d’identifier les possibilités d’utilisation de l’IA susceptibles d’avoir un impact élevé, de les traduire en cas d’usage structurés et d’accompagner leur progression, depuis la phase de conception jusqu’à la preuve de concept, puis, le cas échéant, jusqu’à leur déploiement opérationnel. L’une de vos principales responsabilités consistera à déterminer l’approche technique la plus appropriée pour chaque cas d’usage, en évaluant si les solutions doivent être mises en œuvre au moyen d’outils institutionnels de productivité, de flux de travail et d’applications fondés sur l’IA, ou d’environnements expérimentaux plus avancés. À cet effet, vous prendrez en compte des facteurs tels que la sécurité, la sensibilité des données, les coûts, l’évolutivité, l’interopérabilité et l’impact organisationnel, tout en veillant à ce que la mise en œuvre de l’IA reste étroitement alignée sur les travaux analytiques et les activités de politique publique de l’OCDE et qu’elle contribue à une architecture et à un cadre de gouvernance de l’IA cohérents à l’échelle de l’Organisation. Principales responsabilités Identifier et hiérarchiser les possibilités offertes par l’IA Conception et architecture des solutions Déterminer l’architecture d’IA la plus appropriée pour chaque cas d’usage, en tenant compte des éléments suivants : sécurité et sensibilité des informations ; faisabilité technique ; coûts et implications en matière de licences ; évolutivité à l’échelle de l’Organisation ; intégration avec les systèmes existants de l’OCDE ; gouvernance et viabilité opérationnelle. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les collègues techniques de l’AI Lab afin de valider les choix d’architecture. Développement de prototypes Contribuer au développement informatique, à l’ingénierie des prompts, à l’intégration d’API, à la conception de flux de travail et à l’évaluation. Transformation des flux de travail Partage des connaissances Amélioration continue Se tenir informé(e) des avancées, des nouvelles tendances du secteur, des technologies connexes, des méthodologies et des bonnes pratiques. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil du candidat idéal Formation académique Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur en intelligence artificielle, science des données, informatique, économie, politiques publiques ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience pratique équivalente. Expérience professionnelle Capacité avérée à identifier, définir le périmètre et structurer des cas d’usage de l’IA. Compétences avérées en ingénierie des prompts et en ingénierie du contexte. Bonne compréhension de la conception et de l’évaluation des flux de travail fondés sur l’IA. Bonne compréhension des atouts et des limites des modèles propriétaires et des modèles à poids ouverts. Connaissance des modèles de déploiement dans le cloud et sur site. Capacité à évaluer les compromis architecturaux liés à la sécurité, aux coûts, à l’évolutivité et à la gouvernance. Solides compétences analytiques et de communication, ainsi qu’une capacité à traduire les besoins métiers en solutions techniques. Une expérience dans un environnement international ou multilatéral serait vivement souhaitée. Outils : Solide expérience d’au moins une grande plateforme d’IA, telle qu’OpenAI, Microsoft, Anthropic, Mistral ou Google. Langues Maîtrise de l’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE, à savoir l’anglais et le français, et connaissance de l’autre langue, avec l’engagement d’atteindre un bon niveau professionnel. Compétences clés "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Date limite de dépôt des candidatures Durée du contrat Engagement de durée déterminée de 36 mois, renouvelable, Veuillez noter que le Règlement du personnel fixe l’âge obligatoire de départ à la retraite à 67 ans. Ce que l’OCDE offre Selon le niveau d’expérience, le salaire mensuel débute à 6,838,10 EUR, auquel peuvent s’ajouter des indemnités en fonction de l’éligibilité. Ce salaire est exonéré de l’impôt français sur le revenu. Cliquez ici pour consulter notre Guide de gestion du personnel et en apprendre davantage sur tous les aspects liés aux ressources humaines à l’OCDE, à notre environnement de travail ainsi qu’aux nombreuses politiques mises en place pour accompagner les membres du personnel dans leur vie quotidienne. Informations relatives au salaire Le salaire et les conditions d’emploi dépendront du grade officiel. Processus de sélection Pour les candidats retenus, les tests écrits et/ou les entretiens vidéo enregistrés devraient avoir lieu à la fin du mois d’août 2026, les entretiens avec le panel étant prévus au début du mois de septembre 2026. L’OCDE est un employeur qui souscrit au principe de l’égalité des chances et accueille les candidatures de toutes les personnes qualifiées ressortissantes d’un pays membre de l’OCDE , sans distinction d’origine raciale ou ethnique, d’opinions ou de convictions, de genre, d’orien

Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" The Executive Directorate (EXD) stewards OECD resources on behalf of the Secretary-General, with responsibility for people and wellbeing, budget management, security, infrastructure, and the OECD’s convening activities. EXD provides corporate services and strategic advice on management and corporate policies to the Secretary-General, Council and Standing Committees, and delivers compliance and risk management functions within its remit, operating in a fast-paced environment focused on management excellence. Within the Executive Directorate (EXD), the Digital, Knowledge and Information Service (DKI) is responsible for overseeing corporate IT infrastructure and operations, maintaining digital security, information management, and delivering digital and other IT-related products and services. EXD/DKI also supports the safe adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies across the Organisation. Following the recommendation of the OECD AI Task Force and in line with the evolving AI-related requirements of the OECD, the CAI division has been established to support the safe adoption of AI technologies across the Organisation. CAI is tasked with overseeing the shift from initial experimentation towards the scaled adoption of AI (from Exploration to Institutionalisation) that delivers tangible value with a clear emphasis on enhancing organisational impact, improving productivity, and transforming ways of working. In this role, you will sit within the AI Lab in EXD/DKI/CAIO. The AI Lab supports the development and operationalisation of the OECD’s corporate AI framework by identifying, designing and implementing high-value AI solutions that strengthen the Organisation’s analytical and operational capabilities. You will be focused on building, structuring and industrialising AI solutions to support the Organisation’s adoption of advanced AI capabilities. You will also contribute to the development of internal AI capabilities. Expérience professionnelle Approche pratique de l’ingénierie et souci de la qualité technique. Capacité à travailler de manière autonome sur des sujets techniques complexes. Approche pragmatique, axée sur les solutions et l’obtention de résultats concrets. Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes et capacité d’adaptation dans un domaine en évolution rapide. Outils: Le candidat retenu devra démontrer ou posséder plusieurs des compétences suivantes: IA générative et systèmes agentiques Expérience pratique des technologies d’IA générative, notamment des grands modèles de langage (LLM), des plongements vectoriels, de la génération augmentée par récupération (RAG) et de l’ingénierie des prompts. Expérience avérée dans la conception de systèmes d’IA fondés sur des agents ou comportant plusieurs étapes, notamment en matière d’orchestration, d’appel d’outils ou de fonctions et de conception de flux de travail. Capacité à concevoir des pipelines d’IA efficaces et fiables, en tenant compte des performances, de la latence et des coûts. Plateformes d’IA et écosystèmes de modèles Expérience pratique d’au moins une grande plateforme d’IA générative, telle qu’OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI/Gemini ou Mistral. Expérience de l’intégration de services d’IA dans des applications existantes et des environnements d’entreprise. Bonne compréhension des compromis associés aux différents fournisseurs de modèles et aux différentes approches. Modèles open source et à poids ouverts Expérience pratique des modèles à poids ouverts et des environnements technologiques d’IA open source. Expérience du déploiement de modèles et des techniques d’optimisation, telles que l’ajustement fin, notamment LoRA/PEFT, la quantification et la mise à disposition de modèles sous forme de services. Capacité à mettre en œuvre des solutions d’IA sur site ou hybrides lorsque cela est nécessaire. Ingénierie logicielle et ingénierie des données Solides compétences en programmation Python et expérience de la conception d’applications adaptées à un environnement de production. Expérience du développement d’API, de services et de pipelines intégrant des composants d’IA. Familiarité avec les éléments suivants : Bases de données vectorielles et pipelines de plongements vectoriels Stratégies d’indexation et de récupération de l’information Traitement de données structurées et non structurées Solides pratiques d’ingénierie, notamment en matière de tests, de gestion des versions, d’intégration et de déploiement continus (CI/CD) et de suivi. Ingénierie des plateformes d’IA Expérience de la mise en place ou de l’exploitation de plateformes d’IA ou de services d’IA partagés. Compréhension des éléments suivants : Authentification et contrôle des accès Gestion des API Évolutivité et suivi de l’utilisation Capacité à contribuer à la fourniture sécurisée et contrôlée de services d’IA. Sécurité et IA responsable Compréhension des risques liés aux systèmes d’IA, notamment les fuites de données, les hallucinations et les injections de prompts. Expérience de la mise en œuvre de mesures de protection techniques, telles que le filtrage, les garde-fous et les modèles de conception sécurisés. Capacité à travailler dans le respect des contraintes de sécurité et de gouvernance propres à un environnement d’entreprise. Langues Maîtrise de l’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE, à savoir l’anglais et le français, et connaissance de l’autre langue, avec l’engagement d’atteindre un bon niveau professionnel. item.title: E T Consultant- Infrastructure Policy Consultant
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank consists of two entities – the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA). It is a global development cooperative owned by 189 member countries. As the largest development bank in the world, the World Bank provides loans, guarantees, risk management products, and advisory services to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries, and coordinates responses to regional and global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org. Infrastructure Vertical The WBG Infrastructure Vertical provides public and private solutions to operational teams and clients across the WBG to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs by: (i) supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, (ii) policy environment, and (iii) enabling and mobilizing private sector capital. With 60 years of experience, the WBG is poised to support the sector becoming an engine of growth and jobs through improving policies and governance, foundational infrastructure and private sector investments. The WBG lending in the sector is expected to grow substantially. The Infrastructure VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure The Global Unit for Disaster Management, Solutions Impact (KIUSD) supports low and middle-income countries to understand, manage, and reduce their risks from natural hazards and climate change. Within KIUSD, the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) umbrella trust fund is a global partnership that helps low- and middle-income countries better understand and reduce their vulnerability to natural hazards and climate change. GFDRR has 15 thematic areas, which provide grant financing, analytics, and technical assistance to the most vulnerable countries and communities where it will have the greatest positive impact. As a donor-funded program, GFDRR consults regularly with donors and actively strives to maintain and develop new partnerships for increased impact. For more information: https://www.gfdrr.org/en Please note this position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The overall objective of the assignment is to develop and apply a policy advice and technical assistance framework to support governments in identifying, assessing, adopting, and implementing infrastructure policy reforms conducive to national disaster risk reduction. The Infrastructure Policy Consultant will advise WBG clients on appropriate international standards across all infrastructure sectors, strategies to improve regulatory alignment, harmonization and coordination at the country and regional levels to promote resilient infrastructure. The Infrastructure Policy Consultant will support and provide technical guidance to GFDRR activities in the Resilient Infrastructure thematic area, including: • Take stock of infrastructure policy reforms and implementation processes for the integration of resilience and adaptation measures across all infrastructure sectors, • Support the development of knowledge products and operational toolkit to enhance capacity of task teams to deliver development policy and infrastructure investments operations related to resilient infrastructure, particularly in the use of risk assessments for decision-support, adoption of improved asset and operational standards and guidelines, disaster risk financing and contingency plans that promote disaster risk reduction and other resilience measures. • Support in-country activities through technical assistance (TA). This technical support includes demand-driven tasks for the preparation and implementation of development policy operations and lending operation projects that involve infrastructure or disaster risk management activities in cities and other infrastructure sectors, such as transport and energy. Activities include but are not limited to (i) preliminary assessment to raise awareness and identify gaps, (ii) identification of suitable solutions and opportunities from peer-learning and analytics, (iii) technical assistance during development of policy reforms, preparation and implementation of resilient infrastructure investments. • Build client capacity to use findings of policy research/ analytical work for developing and implementing new policies. Provide technical advice on key issues and strategic directions for the country’s adaptation and resilience priorities by bringing relevant international experience and research to assist in developing and implementing local solutions. • Oversee the implementation of TA activities including but not limited to planning, budgeting, preparation of terms of references, quality control, supervision of external consultants and technical specialists work as well as developing and reviewing Trust Fund Proposals, contributing to Trust Funds reporting, and developing of terms of reference. • Participate in field missions and provide technical input and guidance to client counterparts as required by operational and analytical task team leaders. • Contribute to monitoring and reporting of GFDRR grants implementation in these thematic areas. Advising on resilience metrics, indicators, and results frameworks in infrastructure operations. • Identify and nurture opportunities for partnerships in the broader policy dialogue across WBG and external parties. Ensure collaboration with IFC and MIGA to identify opportunities for integrated approaches and support to the client, leveraging the One WBG expertise and instruments. • Lead and/or participate in GFDRR and infrastructure sectors knowledge-sharing and learning activities, and organize and contribute to dissemination activities, conferences, workshops, and learning programs; present the team's work at internal and external knowledge exchange events. • Carry out other tasks relevant to support the overall objective of the position.

item.title: Finance Associate
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org The WBG Budget and Procurement Solutions Vice Presidency (WPB VPU) is organized into five Departments serving across all organizations of the world bank group: • WBPCP - WBG Corporate Procurement: Overseeing sourcing, supplier management, and operational support. • WBPCE - WBG Centers of Excellence: Leading planning, reporting, shared services, and budget solutions • WBPCU - WBG Budget Partners, Corporate, Finance, and Knowledge Units: Providing strategic and operational leadership in finance planning and budget oversight to WBG executive, compliance, corporate, finance, and knowledge VPUs. • WBPRU - IBRD/IDA Budget Partners, Regional Units: Providing strategic and operational leadership in finance planning and budget oversight to regional VPUs and Country Office Accounting management and oversight, globally. • CSDR – IFC MIGA Budget Partners: Providing strategic and operational leadership in finance planning and budget oversight to IFC and MIGA clients, globally. The unified WBG WBP VPU provides the structural framework to enable faster, simpler, and more impactful solutions for our clients all rising to the challenges of the ‘bigger and better bank’. Specifically, Finance Associate (FA) responds to the need to be where our stakeholders need us most, providing timely relevant expert advice while harmonizing and leveraging best practice solutions at speed and scale, across all country offices. In addition, in country offices, WBPAW staff performs accounting, payment processing, cash management and administration functions. Overall, WBPAW ensures that each department maintains cost efficiency and effective controls over all financial transactions and provides support for effective management and monitoring of deliverables. The primary focus of the Finance Associate will be in the Country Office Accounting workstream. Finance Associates are expected to be specialists in accounting, analytics, controls, processes, and procedures. Finance Associate is expected to support daily accounting and financial transactions and decision-making through the provision of timely, fit for purpose information on the management of financial resources. Key accountabilities are: • Financial Transactions Payments: Review and process E-payable transactions, payroll inputs, staff loans, travel and rental advances, and vendor payments, ensuring accuracy in charge codes, bank accounts, tax treatment, and supporting documentation. Conduct payment runs and respond to Chennai queries on transaction compliance. • Budgeting, Cash Management Financial Reporting: Prepare monthly expense forecasts, budget reports with variance analysis, and bank reconciliations; monitor and replenish country office bank accounts; and submit VAT refund claims while resolving outstanding items on VAT, inter-currency, transit, and suspense accounts. • Procurement Vendor Management: Monitor purchase orders, STC transactions, and vendor open items (including GRIs, SES, and invoices) through the admin portal, and oversee rental contracts in PeopleSoft to ensure timely resolution of outstanding items. • Internal Controls, Compliance Risk Management: Maintain effective financial controls through oversight of corporate cards, asset inventory, signatory management, contract monitoring, record retention, account reconciliations, and timely resolution of audit, scorecard, and compliance-related matters. • Business Advisory Staff Support: Provide guidance to the Country Manager and business area staff on WBG financial, administrative, and benefits policies — including financial assistance loans, retirement plans, dependency allowances, and overtime — and onboard new staff on finance systems, travel, and related procedures. • Reporting, Audit Process Improvement: Respond to Scorecard and audit queries, ensure orderly filing of transaction documentation, and support process harmonization, automation, and continuous improvement initiatives, including assigned COA projects such as VAT Automation and the SAP Upgrade.

item.title: E T Consultant - Intake Officer
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prospering and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: The World Bank’s Ethics and Internal Justice Services Vice Presidency (EIJ VPU) brings together, under a single umbrella, the WBG’s approach to values, ethics and the resolution of workplace conflict. The EIJ VPU’s vision is to foster a values-based workplace culture and help staff uphold the WBG’s ethical standards. EIJ provides an integrated, empathetic and efficient approach to resolving workplace conflict, allowing staff to focus with urgency on the WBG’s mission. EIJ’s work covers each of the five WBG institutions. https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/unit/ethics-and-internal-justice-services . The investigations unit (INV) of the EIJ VPU is seeking to recruit an Intake officer to support investigative activities into allegations of misconduct by WBG staff involving harassment, sexual harassment, conflicts of interest, retaliation, abuse of authority and misuse of Bank resources. Unit Context: The EIJ VPU is seeking to recruit an ETC Intake Officer to work on the INV intake team, and who will report to the Manager, INV. The incumbent will have overall responsibility for handling the initial assessment of allegations of misconduct, with the upmost quality, timeliness, and completeness and with the highest level of professionalism, diplomacy, and discretion. This role will be stationed at WBG Headquarters in Washington, D.C. Duties and accountabilities: Under the supervision and overall guidance of the INV Manager, the ETC Intake Officer will carry out the following duties and accountabilities: • Register, categorize, and track all allegations and their assessment as well as inquiries and responses in the case management system ensuring record keeping is timely and properly maintained. • Timely manage and respond to incoming allegations of misconduct, assessing, analyzing and identifying the issues of each allegation. • Interview complainants and collect from them and other sources additional information required to make an assessment of the allegation. • Make verbal and written recommendations to the INV Manager for appropriate disposition and triaging of allegations (i.e. close at intake or open a preliminary inquiry; refer to another EIJ Service), suggesting, when applicable, appropriate lines of inquiry. • Maintain optimal quality standards for the intake process ensuring compliance with INV’s KPIs and service delivery standards for review and processing of allegations. • May occasionally participate as a member of the investigation team, conducting fact finding (interviewing witnesses and obtaining/reviewing documents); drafting concise investigation reports to be submitted to the Vice President of Human Resources or case closing memos. • Participate in the sharing of best practices, trends, knowledge and lessons learned across units and with clients and partners, articulating ideas verbally and in writing in a clear and compelling way across audiences of varied levels.

item.title: Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . The WBG Planet Vice Presidency is leading WBG’s efforts to make the planet livable, as a necessary condition for job creation and poverty elimination. It is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions to our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact and business to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs, focusing on agribusiness, tourism (nature-based tourism), infrastructure (water) and health (sanitation, nutrition); supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, policy environment, and private sector mobilization; and supporting and accelerating specific targets and commitments such as Mission AgriConnect, Mission Water, Climate Change Action Plan. The VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. WBG Water Department - Water for People, Food, and Planet. The World Bank Group’s Water Strategy Implementation Plan (WSIP) translates ambition into operational action. Water security is not only about access. It is a foundation of resilient and prosperous societies where sustained water resources, reliable services, and risk management underpin growth, human development, jobs, and livelihoods. Approved in December 2025, the WSIP sets a collective target to improve water security for 400 million people by 2030 and organizes delivery through three outcome pillars: Water for People, Water for Food, and Water for Planet. Delivery is enabled by scalable solutions, knowledge for impact at scale, and programmatic approaches and partnerships. The WBG Water Department works with regions to implement the WSIP through solutions tailored to key client segments, including national and sub-national governments, private sector operators, investors, and financial institutions. Implementation is organized around three core delivery mechanisms: (i) country-led Water Compacts that deploy WBG resources in countries committed to policy and regulatory actions; (ii) coordinated public and private interventions to mobilize capital investments; and (iii) multiphase programmatic approaches that replicate and scale what works. The WBG is also expanding collaboration with partners, including MDBs and philanthropies, through Mission Water to accelerate global water security and reach many more people in developing countries. This agenda is reinforced by the World Bank Group’s shift toward a more integrated Knowledge Bank that shortens the distance from insight to implementation. In Water, the Knowledge Bank delivery model is structured into two global units that translate knowledge into impact at scale: • Policy and Regulations Unit: Provides global thought leadership and evidence-based policy support to advance water security for people, food, and the planet. It supports regional teams in strengthening water sector governance, in particular on policies, institutions and regulations (PIR), including supporting an enabling environment for private finance. The team will help ensure the WBG’s leadership in global water and development discourse through evidence-based analytics and hands-on support. The unit drives innovation and knowledge management by advancing research and leading water data and analytics for policymaking. It also supports regional task teams to meet the highest standards on inclusion, climate resilient design, and dam safety. • Solutions and Impact Unit: Scales and replicates high-impact water projects and innovations across WBG operations to deliver results for people, food, and the planet. The Unit leads the consolidation and rollout of scalable water solutions, supports regional teams to accelerate implementation of the WSIP, and provides operational support and portfolio oversight. It drives impact through robust monitoring and evaluation, knowledge sharing, and applied research, while helping country teams adapt global solutions to local contexts and political economy realities. These global units operate within the WBG Water Department’s leadership structure alongside Global Leads for the three WSIP outcome pillars and cross-cutting areas such as Financing, Governance and Regulation, and Water for Prosperity. Together, they enable a governance and regulation anchored delivery approach that strengthens institutions, improves accountability and performance, and creates the enabling conditions for investment and sustainable service delivery at scale. The WBG Water Department is comprised of 65 staff. Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation: The Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation, will report to the WBG Manager, Policy and Regulations, who is accountable to the WBG Director, Water. Key responsibilities: The Senior Water Specialist, Governance and Regulation, will be responsible for leading on water sector policies, institutions and regulatory (PIR) support to WBG internal and external clients of the WBG Water Global Leadership Team, and being a thought-leader in this space. Specific duties and accountabilities include the following: 1. Provide just-in-time strategic and hands-on advice and guidance on water sector regulatory issues, based on global lessons learned and fit-for-purpose solutions for the respective country/client context, following-through on support to help lead to tangible results for WBG operations. 2. Provide just-in-time strategic and hands-on advice and guidance on appropriate policy and institutional issues, based on global lessons learned and fit-for-purpose solutions for the respective country/client context, following-through on support to help lead to tangible results for WBG operations. 3. Lead and/or contribute to sharp and concise operations-oriented research and analysis to bring the latest knowledge and innovation to our support to clients, collaborating with others, both inside and outside the Water Global Department, to ensure full synergies. 4. Lead and/or contribute to papers on PIR for water, blogs and other communication materials, and contribute to global flagship reports, curate lessons learned and case studies, participating in select conferences and events as agreed with management, and the like. 5. Participate in relevant corporate initiatives and undertake relevant corporate reviews to ensure WBG Global Water contributions reflect the latest and context-appropriate thinking that consider PIR in the water sector. 6. Provide briefings to senior management on complex PIR on an as-needed basis. 7. Be an active participant of the Water Global Department’s Leadership Team and specifically the P R Unit’s Leadership Team. 8. Work with management to develop a core team of PIR experts to provide hands-on support to task teams on PIR, within existing budgetary and other parameters. 9. Participate in all relevant activities sponsored by the Global Water Security and Sanitation Partnership to support and inform WBG Water Global partners. 10. Other related tasks.

item.title: Principal Investment Officer, Financial Institutions Group
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . The Financial Institution Group (FIG) is one of IFC’s key Departments responsible for a significant portion of IFC’s business volume, profitability, and development reach, approximately 40%. FIG engages in a wide range of sub-sectors including Microfinance, SME, Gender, Climate, Insurance, Capital Markets, Housing, Distressed Assets, and other areas, with both investment and advisory services delivered globally to IFC’s clients through IFC’s global network. FIG has three main objectives: 1) financial inclusion 2) servicing the real economy and 3) mobilizing third-party resources. FIG’s Europe team is based across the region with main offices in Vienna, Bucharest, Warsaw and Belgrade, as well as other offices across the region. The team members work on both new business development (including transaction processing) and portfolio supervision/client relationship management across the region. Both new business and portfolio supervision activity of the FIG team entails engagement with all types of Financial Intermediaries (e.g. commercial banks, microfinance companies, insurance companies, NBFIs, etc.) across multiple products ranging from senior debt to straight equity investments. IFC is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Principal Investment Officer to be based in Kyiv, Ukraine. This is a high-impact leadership role at the forefront of the World Bank Group's crisis response and reconstruction efforts for Ukraine. The selected candidate will lead and coordinate FIG’s investment and advisory operations on the ground, playing a pivotal role in designing complex financial structures, engaging with key public and private stakeholders, and deploying blended finance to unlock private investment where it is needed most. Duties and Accountabilities: The duties and accountabilities of the role include but are not limited to: • Lead and coordinate all FIG activities in Ukraine, acting as the primary focal point. Ensure seamless integration between investment and advisory operations to drive comprehensive solutions that support the resilience and reconstruction of the Ukrainian financial sector. • Drive business development and oversee the full transaction lifecycle. Originate, structure, negotiate, and close complex financial sector transactions (debt, equity, guarantees). Oversee portfolio management, including loan restructurings, rescheduling, and capital optimization strategies. • Lead engagements with blended finance providers and development partners. Design and negotiate de-risking structures and co-financing arrangements essential for deploying capital and maximizing development impact. • Build and maintain critical, high-level relationships. Act as a senior representative to engage with public sector stakeholders, government officials, regulators, and C-suite executives to support WBG sector reform efforts, align on strategic priorities, and unlock new investment opportunities. • Champion integrated value propositions. Coordinate closely with the regional and country team, MAS, Infra, E S, CAE, CRG, and other teams to deliver holistic, pragmatic solutions to clients, mitigating risks and achieving sustainable development impact. • Supervise, mentor, and coach less-experienced investment and advisory staff. Foster a high-performing, resilient team culture capable of delivering high-quality projects and meeting regional FIG targets under pressure and in a dynamic environment. • Drive regional knowledge management. Continuously monitor geopolitical and market trends in Ukraine to adapt FIG’s strategy, contributing to institutional thought leadership on crisis response and financial sector rebuilding.

item.title: Procurement Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org Europe and Central Asia Region The Europe and Central Asia (ECA) region comprise 30 diverse countries, with a population of nearly 500 million people. Most of the countries are high and upper-middle-income countries with only three being low-income IDA countries. ECA has an active portfolio of 245 projects with a net commitment of around US$52 billion and a strong lending pipeline as well. Knowledge is critical to the Bank’s value proposition to client countries in the ECA region in both lending and advisory services. To learn more above ECA region visit: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/ECA Procurement work in ECA The Procurement Team in Europe and Central Asia (ECA) Region provides crucial operational procurement support to ECA’s diverse portfolio. Policy dialogue is also important, through DPOs, TAs and collaboration with other GPs, the procurement team in ECA is helping countries to keep transforming their procurement systems. Effective, efficient, and transparent public procurement is crucial for achieving ECA’s objectives. Scope of Work The procurement specialist will work under the guidance of the accredited practice manager and the supervision and oversight of the specific hub coordinator. His or her main responsibilities are: • Support client countries in achieving value for money in public procurement to enhance service delivery and development outcomes with integrity. • Understand relevant procurement markets using analytical tools and approaches to define more effective procurement. • Provide technical fiduciary advice on procurement activities and engage in policy dialogue on procurement with client countries. • Review procurement documents including procurement strategies, procurement plans, bidding documents, evaluation reports, etc. • Conduct procurement risk assessments • Develops relationships with government senior officials to advance policy dialogue in procurement. • Transforms policy dialogue into concrete proposals that enhance and strengthen countries’ national procurement system. • Plays a significant role within the function in guiding/mentoring other stakeholders. • Develops and executes training modules on complex sector related procurement topics. The work implies frequent interaction with the following stakeholders: • Management and Bank’s staff in his duty station and in countries in the region. • Interactions with HQ based management staff and management. • Government officials at ministerial level and equivalent contacts in other international organizations, partner entities, etc. • Other external constituencies and expert groups.
