item.title: Associate Senior Data Engineer
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 130 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context: The ITS Data Office (ITSDO) is the central entity within the World Bank Group’s Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) department responsible for enabling data, AI, information, and knowledge capabilities across the institution. It comprises four Units focused on platforms tools, product service delivery, enablement and governance. The office plays a pivotal role in advancing the Bank’s digital transformation, supporting business domains with trusted data, information and AI capabilities, and fostering a culture of responsible innovation. The Platforms Tools Unit is responsible for building, integrating, and continuously modernizing the foundational technology infrastructure that powers data, AI, archives, and knowledge services across the World Bank Group. The unit leads the rationalization and simplification of legacy systems, and modernization towards platforms that are scalable, secure, interoperable, and designed for self-service and adoption. The unit plays a critical role in enabling enterprise-wide transformation by delivering data environments, digitization infrastructure, and open knowledge repositories that are AI-ready and aligned with business needs. Duties and accountabilities: Data Transformation and Modeling • Design and build dimensional and semantic data models on top of the curated data layer (Delta Lake/Unity Catalog) that translate raw data into business-ready tables • Apply software engineering practices, including version control, modular design, and reusable macros, to data transformation code • Own the AI-ready data layer at the enterprise for both structured and unstructured data ensuring transformations are documented as patterns/codified blueprints, tested, and repeatable • Reduce duplication and inconsistency across data models by establishing canonical, reusable definitions for key business entities and metrics Semantic Layer and Metrics Governance • Define and maintain a single source of truth for enterprise metrics and business definitions, preventing divergent calculations across teams and tools • Partner with Collibra-based governance work to ensure business metadata and technical metadata stay aligned as data moves from platform to consumption • Establish data contracts between upstream data producers and downstream consumers, including AI agents and BI tools, to protect against silent schema or definition drift Testing, Documentation, and Data Quality • Implement automated data quality tests and validation checks as part of the transformation pipeline (not just at ingestion) • Maintain living documentation of data models, lineage, and business logic so analysts, data scientists, and AI agents can self-serve with confidence • Monitor data freshness, completeness, and accuracy of consumption-layer datasets and triage issues back to the appropriate upstream owner Stakeholder Enablement and AI Readiness • Work directly with business analysts, data scientists, and product teams to understand use cases and translate them into well-structured, reusable data models • Prepare and structure datasets specifically for AI/agentic consumption, ensuring enterprise AI agents and accelerators draw from governed, high-quality data rather than ad hoc extracts • Build or support last-mile dashboards and self-service data products where the underlying model is the primary complexity • Act as the bridge between the Data Engineering team and business/AI consumers, reducing the load on data engineers to answer business-logic questions Cross Cutting Analytics Standards and Interoperability • Define and publish enterprise standards for analytical data products, including naming conventions, business identifiers, metadata requirements, documentation standards, testing criteria, and quality controls to ensure consistency and interoperability across business units. • Embed analytics standards and governance requirements into platform capabilities through automated validation, testing, and compliance checks, ensuring adherence by design rather than through manual reviews and governance processes. • Build and maintain shared taxonomies, reference data, business entities, and semantic relationships that connect data products across business domains and enable cross-cutting analytics, reporting, AI, and self-service use cases.

Duties and accountabilities: Platform Architecture Engineering • Build Maintain Azure Databricks Enterprise Data Platform that enable federated data product development across lines of business. • Develop Platform as Product solutions to enable WBG Data Engineering and Data Analysts to consume data platform in self-service manner. • This role will be the technical anchor for data platform, setting standards, enforcing governance, controlling costs, and enabling data engineering teams to deliver reliably at scale. • Design, build, and maintain a production-grade Lakehouse architecture on Azure Databricks, aligned to medallion (bronze/silver/gold) design patterns. • Administer and govern Unity Catalog: managing catalogs, schemas, external locations, storage credentials, lineage, and fine-grained access controls. • Own the configuration and lifecycle of Databricks SQL Warehouses, clusters, and compute policies for both interactive and production workloads. • Establish and maintain dbt as the transformation framework: project structure, model standards, testing, documentation, and CI/CD integration. • Rationalize legacy Data Platform into modern Data Management solutions. Cost Optimization FinOps • Continuously monitor and optimize the cost of Databricks clusters, SQL Warehouses, and dbt workloads through right-sizing, autoscaling, spot/photon usage, cluster policies, and workload isolation. • Implement chargeback/showback tagging, usage dashboards, and budget guardrails to drive accountability across teams. • Recommend and enforce cost-efficient engineering practices without compromising performance or reliability. Data Governance, Quality Management • Define and enforce data governance best practices: access management, data classification, PII handling, auditing, and regulatory compliance. • Implement data quality frameworks (tests, contracts, validation, monitoring, alerting) to ensure trusted, reliable data products. • Champion data management best practices across cataloging, metadata, lineage, retention, and lifecycle management. Collaboration with Agile Teams • Participates in agile ceremonies (e.g., sprint planning, stand-ups) to align data engineering efforts with project goals • Collaborates with data scientists, analysts, and product owners to understand data requirements and deliver solutions that drive business value • Analyzes and maintains comprehensive documentation for data processes, pipelines, and systems to facilitate knowledge sharing • Develops the documentation of engineering processes and workflows to promote knowledge sharing and compliance Cloud Compute Cloud Security • Design and manage secure cloud networking for the platform: VNet injection, private endpoints/Private Link, firewalls, and connectivity to source and downstream systems. • Partner with cloud infrastructure and security teams to ensure the platform meets enterprise security and compliance standards. Production Operations Reliability • Own the operation of data platforms in production: monitoring, incident response, capacity planning, upgrades, and SLA management. • Build automation and observability (CI/CD, IaC, alerting, logging) to ensure resilient, self-healing platform operations. • Lead root-cause analysis and drive continuous improvement of platform stability and performance. Stakeholder Engagement • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to data platform engineers, setting standards and reviewing designs and code. • Engage with data vendors: evaluate tools and capabilities, manage relationships, and negotiate technical requirements. • Lead and execute RFP processes: defining requirements, evaluating vendors, and guiding selection decisions. • Serve as a trusted advisor, delivering best-practice recommendations to data engineering and analytics teams. • Gain exposure to enterprise-scale AI applications and real-world development impact • Support development, testing, and deployment of AI/ML models and platform components. • Implement and support monitoring, observability, and operational reliability practices • Collaborate with cross-functional teams and contribute to agile development processes

Duties and accountabilities: Data Pipeline Development • Design, develop, and maintain data pipelines for ingestion, transformation, and serving across batch and streaming workloads • Build ETL/ELT workflows to integrate data from diverse sources into enterprise data platforms • Build document ingestion and processing pipelines incorporating OCR, metadata extraction, content enrichment, classification, and indexing capabilities. • Develop data transformation logic using Apache Spark, PySpark, SparkSQL, and SQL • Implement change data capture (CDC) patterns for real-time and near-real-time data synchronization • Build streaming data pipelines for real-time analytics and operational use cases • Optimize pipeline performance, resource utilization, and cost efficiency Federated Data Pipelines Domain Enablement • Support federated data pipeline architecture that enables Line of Business (LOB) teams to own and manage their domain data • Contribute to self-serve data infrastructure that abstracts complexity and allows domain teams to build pipelines independently • Develop standardized pipeline deployment patterns that LOB teams can adopt while maintaining autonomy • Support domain teams in building data products that are discoverable, interoperable, and compliant with enterprise standards • Support domain teams in creating and managing structured and federated governance • Assist in establishing data contracts and interoperability standards that allow seamless data sharing across domains • Support the balance between domain autonomy and enterprise-wide governance requirements Templates, Blueprints Patterns • Develop reusable pipeline templates and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) patterns for common data product types • Create blueprints for data ingestion, transformation, quality validation, and serving that LOB teams can customize • Build standardized patterns for batch pipelines, streaming pipelines, CDC implementations, and API-based integrations • Develop reusable patterns and accelerators for document ingestion, OCR, metadata extraction, content enrichment, and indexing of unstructured content • Contribute to a pattern library covering medallion architecture, dimensional modeling, and data product packaging • Document best practices and reference architectures that guide LOB teams in building compliant, high-quality pipelines • Develop starter kits and accelerators that reduce time-to-value for domain teams building new data products • Create cookbooks and implementation guides that translate enterprise standards into actionable steps • Support LOB teams in adopting templates while allowing appropriate customization for domain-specific needs Data Integration • Integrate data from multiple internal and external sources into unified data assets • Build reusable data integration patterns and connectors for enterprise data sources • Implement data ingestion using Auto Loader, COPY INTO, and other ingestion frameworks • Develop API-based data integrations and file-based data processing workflows • Ensure data consistency and reliability across integrated sources • Support data migration efforts and legacy system integrations Data Modeling Transformation • Implement medallion architecture patterns (bronze, silver, gold) for data organization and quality progression • Develop dimensional models, fact tables, and aggregations for analytics use cases • Build data transformation logic that ensures accuracy, consistency, and business alignment • Create reusable transformation components and modular pipeline designs • Optimize data models for query performance and consumption patterns • Support schema evolution and data versioning requirements Data Quality Testing • Implement data quality checks, validation rules, and automated testing within pipelines • Develop data profiling and anomaly detection to identify quality issues • Build data reconciliation processes to ensure accuracy across systems • Implement unit testing, integration testing, and regression testing for pipelines • Monitor data quality metrics and remediate issues proactively • Document data quality rules and thresholds for pipeline outputs Data Observability Operations • Implement logging, monitoring, and alerting for pipeline health and performance • Build dashboards to track pipeline execution, data freshness, and quality metrics • Develop automated error handling, retry logic, and failure notifications • Support incident response and troubleshooting for pipeline failures • Implement data lineage tracking to support auditability and impact analysis • Implement monitoring and observability for AI and data products, including pipeline health, data quality, and retrieval effectiveness. • Ensure pipelines meet SLAs for data availability and freshness Analytics AI Enablement • Build data pipelines that enable analytics, reporting, and business intelligence use cases • Build and maintain document processing pipelines for extraction, classification, chunking, enrichment, and indexing of unstructured content • Develop content chunking, metadata extraction, indexing, and enrichment workflows to support enterprise search and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions. • Prepare and serve data for machine learning and AI workloads • Develop feature engineering pipelines for ML model development • Create semantic layers and curated datasets that enable self-service analytics • Support integration with analytics tools including Power BI and Tableau • Build data products with clear documentation and consumption guidance Collaboration Enablement • Partner with data architects to align pipeline development with architectural standards • Collaborate with business analysts and data scientists to understand data requirements • Work with platform engineers to leverage platform capabilities effectively • Contribute to technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge sharing • Contribute to platform standards, reusable frameworks, and engineering best practices for data and AI solutions • Support data consumers in understanding and accessing data assets • Participate in code reviews and follow engineering best practices

Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context: The ITS Data Office (ITSDO) is the central entity within the World Bank Group’s Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) department responsible for enabling data, AI, information, and knowledge capabilities across the institution. It comprises four Units focused on platforms tools, product service delivery, enablement and governance. Duties and accountabilities: AI Platform and Agentic Solution Engineering • Design, build, and maintain core engineering components of the Enterprise Agentic Framework and Intelligence Platform, including its model gateway, enterprise agent hub, and accelerator capabilities. • Lead development of atomic agents, agent orchestration patterns, and the MCP hub, ensuring interoperability across the enterprise agentic backbone. • Own the engineering of agent harnesses across the platform, covering orchestration (planning, state management, multi-agent coordination, human-in-the-loop controls), memory (persistent session and context management across long-running tasks), observability (structured tracing of tool calls, model responses, and decision branches, with OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation), and evaluation (offline eval suites, production trace scoring, and eval gates integrated into CI/CD to catch regressions before release). • Establish reference architectures, technical blueprints, and reusable engineering patterns (RAG, retrieval strategies, metadata-aware search, evals, multi-document synthesis) that accelerate AI adoption across business teams. • Drive engineering quality across the platform's tool registry and the broader tools and accelerators portfolio, ensuring consistency, scalability, and performance. Center of Excellence and Enablement • Act as a technical anchor within the AI COE, providing hands-on expertise to Line of Business teams building on enterprise AI platforms. • Develop templates, internal libraries, and API/client generation approaches that raise developer productivity and reduce duplication of effort. • Lead technical enablement through workshops, architecture walkthroughs, and knowledge-sharing sessions on agent patterns, modular architecture, and AI-assisted development workflows. • Support the "make the governed path the easiest path" platform philosophy by ensuring self-service AI capabilities are well-documented, discoverable, and easy to adopt correctly. Responsible AI, Governance and Standards • Ensure all agentic and AI tooling solutions align with enterprise standards for security, data classification, and responsible AI practice. • Partner with AI governance and data governance functions to embed guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and quality checks into agent and accelerator design. • Work closely with the Enterprise Architecture and Office of Information Security teams to ensure all platform and agentic solutions are enterprise-aligned and secure by design. • Contribute technical input to platform accreditation and security review processes for the Enterprise Agentic Framework and Intelligence Platform and related agentic components. item.title: ET Consultant - Mining Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career with impact? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, please visit www.worldbank.org . Infrastructure Vice Presidency (INF VPU) The WBG Infrastructure Vice Presidency is responsible for getting the right public and private sector solutions for our operational teams and to our clients, and to produce scalable impact. Its mandate is to deliver knowledge for impact to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in support of our mission and specifically: providing guidance on creating more and better jobs; supporting foundational infrastructure and human capital, policy environment, and private sector mobilization; focusing on agribusiness, healthcare, infrastructure, manufacturing, and tourism; and support and accelerate specific targets such as M300, Health 1.5bn, and SP 500. The VPU’s objectives in driving outcomes include replicating and scaling effective solutions, enhancing thought leadership and innovation, and delivering timely knowledge to client teams. For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/infrastructure Metals and Minerals Policy and Regulation Team (KIMPR) The global mining sector continues to evolve rapidly. Urbanization, agriculture, digitalization, and a soaring need for energy could double the demand for critical minerals by 2040. For many countries, meeting this demand presents a significant opportunity to create jobs and growth. Mining can generate substantial government revenue through taxes, royalties, and state equity stakes that fund schools, clinics, infrastructure, and digital services. With the right policies and safeguards, mining can progress from a purely extractive industry to one that includes manufacturing and processing. This progress ensures that value and jobs stay local with a long-lasting impact. The Metals and Minerals Policy and Regulation unit is embedded within the INF VPU’s Metals and Minerals Department of the World Bank Group. This global unit of technical experts is responsible for the design and implementation of World Bank operations and knowledge activities in mining a t both global and country levels. KIMPR works closely with a multi-donor trust fund program the Extractives Global Programmatic Support (EGPS) and KIMPR team manages global initiatives, including Coal Mines Closure – Just Transitions , and the Climate Smart Mining (CSM) , and the Resilient and Inclusive Supply Chain Enhancement (RISE) program. Within the Metals and Minerals Team, KIMPR also works closely with the Metals and Minerals Solutions and Impact team (KIMSI), which is responsible for ensuring that the right mix of best practice, investment and advisory solutions are made available to our clients and WBG operational teams in the Metals and Minerals sectors. The objective of the KIMPR Unit is to provide technical advice and support on cutting-edge policy, analytical work, and investment lending preparation for government clients, often resulting in financing to support developing countries transform their natural resource wealth into sustainable, resilient, and inclusive economic development, consistent with climate mitigation goals. NOTE : This position is financed by a Trust Fund and renewal is contingent upon availability of funding, in addition to other factors, including but not limited to business needs, staff performance and skills fit. Job Duties and Responsibilities: The selected candidate will be based in the World Bank’s office in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, contribute to the design and implementation of World Bank operations and knowledge activities supported by the EGPS program in metals and minerals sector and with primary focus on Uzbekistan (and possibly extending in the Central Asia region): I. Day-to-Day Liaison with Government Counterparts • Serve as the primary point of contact with key government counterparts in Uzbekistan, including the Ministry of Mining Industry and Geology, ensuring timely communication, follow-up on agreed actions, and continuity of engagement across workstreams. • Support the finalization and implementation of the Metals and Minerals Country Compact in Uzbekistan by facilitating coordination between government counterparts and WBG teams and tracking progress against agreed milestones. • Contribute to the development and refinement of national mining strategies, policies, or regulations, ensuring coherence with institutional capacities, implementation feasibility, and alignment with the country's broader critical minerals agenda. II. Internal Monitoring and Project Implementation • Assist in the monitoring and reporting of project implementation progress across the portfolio, including contributions to internal and external reporting tools and fiduciary requirements. • Support the implementation of project activities, missions and events, identifying emerging challenges and proposing adaptive measures in collaboration with relevant stakeholders. III. Stakeholder Engagement and Donor Coordination • Support policy dialogue and reform processes in the mining sector, engaging with government counterparts, development partners, and private sector actors across the region. • Provide technical support to the development of initiatives in collaboration with national and regional partners, including mapping of donor activities and identification of coordination and co-financing opportunities with partners such as the EBRD, ADB, and bilateral donors. • Support transparency and good governance initiatives in the extractive sector, including potential engagement with the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) process, multi-stakeholder dialogue mechanisms, and related efforts to strengthen revenue transparency, beneficial ownership disclosure, and accountable resource governance. IV. Analytical Work • Conduct analytical work that informs strategic planning along the critical minerals value chain — spanning exploration, mining, processing, and value addition — with a focus on key mining regions and territorial development considerations. • Contribute to the framing of the World Bank's strategy and service responses to evolving technical, fiscal, regulatory, environmental, and social challenges in the mineral sector. V. Advisory and Knowledge Sharing • Collaborate with WBG global and regional teams in developing mining sector and critical minerals value chain strategies, and support related policy advisory and knowledge exchange activities. • Provide technical input across thematic areas relevant to critical minerals value chains, including geology and exploration, permitting and licensing, transparency and governance, environmental and social standards, and downstream value addition. The position will work in close collaboration with the Metals and Minerals Solutions and Impact team (KIMSI), to ensure alignment with departmental priorities and the delivery of integrated, cross-cutting results. It will also strengthen the articulation between public sector engagement and private sector investments, supporting the development of bankable pipelines and investment-ready opportunities.

item.title: Operations Adviser
item.description: Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . South Asia Context The South Asia Region (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) is at a pivotal stage of development. Rapid economic growth—driven by urbanization and demographic trends—has reduced poverty, but significant disparities persist. The region also faces increasing climate risks, environmental pollution, and structural challenges, including informality and low female labor force participation. Sustained, private sector-led growth—anchored in investments in infrastructure, logistics, energy, and connectivity—is critical to generating jobs needed to employ South Asia’s sizeable youth population. At the same time, the region needs to continue building human capital so that South Asia’s population is well equipped for the jobs of the future.. More information: South Asia Region overview Unit Context SARDE is recruiting a high-performing, deeply experienced and energetic Operations Advisor who brings adaptability, flexibility and sound judgment in ensuring the highest level of operational quality management for the SAR portfolio and pipeline, taking on special assignments as they arise, acting for the SARDE Manager as needed and providing ad hoc support to the DSO. The Operations Advisor will report to the SARDE Manager, work closely with the SAR ROC Secretary/Economic Advisor and will mentor a team of 6 GF/GG and A2D staff responsible for various operational functions within SARDE. The position is based in Washington, DC with travel to the South Asia region to be anticipated twice per year. Main accountabilities include: ● Lead SARDE’s Quality and Operations Support Team, providing operational advice and resolution to CMUs, GPs and Task Teams on all complex operational matters in SAR with particular focus on policy/procedures alignment, meeting corporate targets and all aspects of OpsEE implementation. ● Lead all aspects pertaining to innovative approaches to accelerating impact in operations including but not limited to D-Ready implementation, SCCI, SAR Disbursement Challenge, dashboard and data management systems for optimized delivery and portfolio management, use of AI in operational applications, regional risk mitigation activities and relationship management with corporate functions including IEG, INT, OPCS, Legal and others. The Ops Advisor will have demonstrated experience in leading the design and implementation of innovative approaches to development solutions, will have strong communications and people management skills, with the ability to work seamlessly with corporate partners towards resolution and innovation. ● Lead all aspects of RVP clearance process for pipeline/portfolio package reviews including new operations (AOB or Full Board approvals), restructurings and waiver requests among others. Advise and guide team of SARDE “package reviewers” to ensure that all elements of quality control and compliance are reflected, including the new ADM, integration of corporate scorecard indicators (including MBJ), corporate priorities (Gender, PCM, CE, Paris alignment and climate commitments), Outcomes and Targets integration and monitoring among others. Ops Advisor will require proven experience advising and guiding teams on instrument selection, project design, results framework and TOC development, implementation readiness, procurement, E S and corporate commitments and will require deep understanding of CRI, Target Maps, MBJ and Outcomes work. ● Interface with SECPO and Board on all matters pertaining to SAR interventions at the Board including Board scheduling, SECPO comments, meetings with Board members and their advisors among others. The Ops Advisor will be expected to represent the SARDE manager at Board updates, Board meetings or other similar engagements as needed and will have the depth of operational experience, judgment and strength of communications skills to represent SAR positively, if called on. ● Collaborate closely with OPCS and task teams on all matters pertaining to instrument selection and design, FMRF, risk/ROC/OC reviews, comments on new policies/procedures and/or piloting of new initiatives among others. The Ops Advisor will work closely with the Sr. Partnerships specialist in SARDE on all matters relating to joint/parallel co-financing of pipeline operations, ensuring strong coordination with DFI, Legal and external partners. Ops Advisor must have deep experience in the design and implementation of all Bank instruments (IPF, PforR, MPAs etc) and be able to guide task teams on complex operational issues in this space. Experience with FMRF will be a plus. ● Interfaces with IFC and MIGA to identify and accelerate opportunities for deeper One WBG engagement in SAR. Operational experience with IFC will be important to this role and considered a plus in the shortlisting process. ● Coordinate with CMUs and GPs – establishing key relationships with Operations Managers, Practice Managers and RPD Representatives in particular - on key operational issues and updates to teams to ensure high-quality deliverables and full implementation of OpsEE, Knowledge Bank interfacing, new ADM, partnerships and others. Ops Advisor will need to have strong reputation for teamwork, solutions-oriented approach to complexity and strong communications skills. SAR meetings are often held in the morning EST (7 am onwards). SAR Ops Advisor will be expected to be available during these time frames as needed. ● Lead SARDE work relating to the use of AI in process simplification including the upcoming roll out of the AI Board Package Review Tool and other similar solutions. ● Prepare all materials for MDO DRM, internal DRM, quarterly updates etc including the management of SAR-specific initiatives for the full delivery of the MOU including Disbursement Challenges, Proactivity management etc. Oversee work of data team including SAR Dashboard and internal management systems. Lead deep dives on portfolio and pipeline performance to provide strategic solutions for improved performance and management of operational risks. Ops Advisor will be responsible for the full quality control of briefs prepared for DE Manager, DSO and RVP and for proactive management of portfolio and pipeline to ensure full delivery of MOU. ● Prepare and/or consolidate comments on corporate review products, non-SAR ROCs and OCs as well as corporate review products (IEG, GIA, OPCS etc) working closely with the SAR ROC Secretary. The Ops Advisor will have strong written communications skills with the ability to draft comments that challenge/question materials in a constructive and diplomatic manner, for DE Manager review. ● Lead – in partnership with ROC Secretary/Economic Advisor – all work pertaining to SAR’s contribution to major corporate milestones including those such as: MBJ integration into portfolio and pipeline project documents (working closely with Outcomes team on detailed documentation), IDA Midterm Review (connecting with DFI team and ensuring that SAR inputs are collected on time and in a high level of quality reflecting alignment with IDA commitments), Outcomes Midterm Review (maintaining close watch on the status of SAR’s impact on quarterly Target maps) and others. ● Oversee the work of various SARDE teams including those pertaining to regional risk list, operations with INT or IP challenges, work with Outcomes department, data and analytics team, team interacting with DFI on IDA, FFI, Windows and GFPP among others, TF team. Ops Advisor must have demonstrated experience working directly with elements of risk including E S, procurement or FM, must be deeply comfortable with all elements of data management in Bank systems including the Operations Workspace. ● Lead operational learning efforts, including through leadership in the design and implementation of SAR specific learning events including SAR Ops Forum, SCCI events and others. Previous experience in Knowledge and Learning will be a plus. ● Represent the SAR DE Manager as needed at different fora including OPCS COS Board, WBG Strategy Working Group, INT and IEG meetings, Knowledge and Learning Department among others. Support the SARDE Manager on the unit's management work, including acting assignments, support to the DSO and RVP Front Office on ad-hoc basis, onboarding of new staff, mentoring, and organization of meetings and retreats. Ops Advisor must be open to travel to the SAR region to participate in regional events that SARDE organizes (anticipated twice per year)

Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The OECD has earned a leading role in financial and business issues. The core mission of the Directorate for Financial and Enterprise Affairs ( DAF ) is to assist markets to fund inclusive economic growth, and in turn Better Lives, through setting and implementing standards, providing capacity building and technical assistance, acting as a forum for co-operation and collaboration across the OECD Directorates, external stakeholders and International Organisations. DAF's mission is pursued through five substantive divisions whose teams provide member and partner countries with policy guidance, analysis and support in the areas of competition, anti-corruption, corporate governance, financial markets, insurance and pensions, consumer finance, responsible business conduct and international investment. DAF currently employs about 300 staff members (economists, lawyers, statisticians, support staff, consultants, and trainees), who support work across a broad range of policy areas. The DAF/CM Division is looking for a Communications Officer to plan and conduct a wide range of communication tasks to enhance the relevance, visibility, and impact of the Division’s work on policymakers, stakeholders, and the general public. This includes working on publications, the web, traditional and social media, design, and events, in line with OECD corporate communications priorities, rules and best practices. The selected candidate will work under the supervision of CM’s head of communications and in close co-operation with the Communications Unit in the Director’s Office (DO) and the OECD Communications Directorate (COM). "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Publications Work with the Division’s analysts on preparing publications (reports, papers, policy briefs, etc.), advising them throughout the publishing process. Media Develop social media campaigns for key events (publication launches, etc.) and regularly draft content for various platforms (e.g. LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp) to promote outputs. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L'OCDE a acquis un rôle de premier plan sur les questions financières et commerciales. La mission principale de la Direction des affaires financières et des entreprises ( DAF ) est d'aider les marchés à financer une croissance économique inclusive et, par conséquent, une vie meilleure, en établissant et en mettant en œuvre des normes, en fournissant un renforcement des capacités et une assistance technique, et en servant de forum de coopération et de collaboration entre les directions de l'OCDE, les parties prenantes externes et les organisations internationales. La mission de la DAF s'exerce par l'intermédiaire de cinq divisions fonctionnelles dont les équipes fournissent aux pays membres et partenaires des orientations, des analyses et un soutien en matière de politiques publiques dans les domaines de la concurrence, de la lutte contre la corruption, de la gouvernance d'entreprise, des marchés financiers, des assurances et des retraites, du crédit à la consommation, de la conduite responsable des entreprises et de l'investissement international. La DAF emploie actuellement environ 350 personnes (économistes, juristes, statisticiens, personnel de soutien, consultants et stagiaires), qui contribuent à des travaux dans un large éventail de domaines politiques. La Division des marchés de capitaux et des institutions financières (CM) se concentre sur les domaines thématiques suivants : marchés financiers et économie financière, assurances et retraites, éducation financière et protection des consommateurs, gouvernance d’entreprise et entreprises publiques. Ces travaux sont menés sous la direction du Comité des marchés financiers et du Comité de gouvernance d’entreprise, et leurs sous-comités respectifs. La Division DAF/CM recherche un(e) chargé(e) de communication pour planifier et mener à bien un large éventail d'activités visant à renforcer la pertinence, la visibilité et l'impact des travaux de la Division auprès des décideurs, des parties prenantes et du grand public. Ces activités englobent notamment les publications, le web, les médias traditionnels et les réseaux sociaux, le graphisme ainsi que l'organisation d'événements conformément aux priorités, aux règles et aux meilleures pratiques de l'OCDE en matière de communication d'entreprise. Le/la candidat(e) retenu(e) travaillera sous la supervision du responsable de la communication de CM et en étroite collaboration avec l'unité de communication du Cabinet du Directeur (DO) ainsi qu'avec la Direction de la communication de l'OCDE (COM). "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Publications • Collaborer avec les analystes de la Division à l’élaboration de publications (rapports, documents d’analyse, notes d’orientation, etc.) et les conseiller tout au long du processus de publication. • Réviser, mettre en forme et relire les manuscrits afin de garantir la clarté et la cohérence du message et en appliquant toutes les règles et conventions de style de l'OCDE. • Rédiger des contenus courts (articles, billets de blog, etc.) pour promouvoir les publications. • Assurer la promotion des publications via divers canaux (Web, réseaux sociaux, événements, etc.) et identifier des opportunités d’accroître leur visibilité auprès de différents publics et sur diverses plateformes. Médias • Élaborer des campagnes sur les réseaux sociaux pour des événements clés (lancements de publications, etc.) et rédiger régulièrement du contenu pour diverses plateformes (par ex. LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp) afin de promouvoir les réalisations. • Assurer une veille sur les réseaux sociaux pour évaluer l'impact des campagnes. • Appuyer les relations avec les médias traditionnels, notamment en préparant des supports (projets de communiqués de presse, etc.) et en assurant le suivi de la couverture médiatique. Web • Mettre à jour et assurer la maintenance des pages web CM en respectant les règles et les meilleures pratiques de l'entreprise en matière de web, et garantir une visibilité ainsi qu'une découvrabilité optimales des informations. • Rédiger du contenu web original et adapter des textes pour le web, en respectant les meilleures pratiques en matière de SEO et de GEO. Design et multimédia • Concevoir des supports de communication de haute qualité destinés à diverses parties prenantes (par ex. dépliants, brochures, vidéos, infographies). • Proposer de nouvelles approches et de nouveaux outils promotionnels, conformes aux règles et aux outils de l’Organisation, et se tenir au fait des meilleures pratiques et des innovations au sein de l’OCDE ainsi qu’à l’extérieur. Événements • Gérer les besoins en communication liés aux événements (par ex. conférences, ateliers, webinaires), notamment par la création de sites web ou de pages web dédiés, d'identités visuelles conformément aux règles de l'OCDE en matière de marques, de programmes et d'autres activités promotionnelles. Planification stratégique et communication interne • Contribuer au plan de communication annuel de la DAF et veiller à ce que les activités de communication de CM soutiennent la mise en œuvre de ce plan ainsi que les priorités de communication du Directeur de la DAF. • Collaborer avec les autres chargés de communication de la Division et apporter soutien et renfort en cas de besoin. • Assurer la coordination avec l'unité de communication du bureau du Directeur de la DAF et COM pour la planification des activités de communication. • Soutenir le suivi de l'impact et le partage des connaissances au sein de la Division afin d'optimiser la portée des actions et de favoriser l'échange de bonnes pratiques. item.title: Extended Term Temporary (ETT)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative changes around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: East Asia Pacific (EAP) is a large and diverse region, ranging from Small Islands States of the Pacific to the Philippines and China. Despite substantial economic growth and poverty reduction, the EAP region faces huge development challenges. Growth has been uneven across and within countries, institutions still need strengthening, and most countries are heavily affected by climate change. The Bank plays a significant role on global public goods, including climate, biodiversity, water pollution, and health. The COVID pandemic, and more recently food and energy price increases are compounding the impact of the global economic slowdown. The World Bank Group is seen as a premier development institution in the region, with a leadership role on analytical and advisory services as well as financing. Unit Context: The World Bank Sydney office serves 2 Pacific divisions: Pacific 1 covers North and South Pacific currently works in nine developing countries in the Region (the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Tonga, and Tuvalu). Pacific 2 covers Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu. Over the past years, the World Bank has substantially scaled-up its program and field presence in the Pacific, with a focus on initiatives that address the challenges of fragility, isolation, size and limited capacity, and create a foothold for wider development engagement with emphasis on country-specific strategies along three axes; (i) encouraging regional/global integration; (ii) building resilience against external shocks; and (iii) promoting economic reform and private sector development. The World Bank in the Pacific Islands: https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/pacificislands Duties and accountabilities: The Extended Term Temporary (ETT) will carry out the full range of office support work, including managing processes and monitoring schedules for Task team leaders and senior staff. The work is varied involving a large amount of research – to ascertain how to perform non routine operational tasks. Most of the tasks will not be standard. The candidate would need to proactively ask questions, use the World Bank intranet and other operational programs, and proactively make connections with staff in other Country Offices and our Washington-based HQ for guidance and advice to achieve the required results. The role will also involve extensive liaison with service units, internal team members both in HQ and in the field, as well as external counterparts. The ETT will report functionally to the Manager, Portfolio Operations, who provides supervision and guidance to the office support team. The successful candidate may also be assigned responsibility for some aspects of the unit’s administrative functions. Roles Responsibilities • Work productively and effectively often from own initiative providing support to Task Team Leaders (TTL) and Senior Staff. • Draft routine correspondence, project related documents, and proofread materials using proper grammar, punctuation, and style. • Incorporate agreed comments into documents, making full use of shared drives and software capabilities. • Use word processing, spreadsheets, power point software or desktop publishing skills to produce complex text, reports, figures, graphs, etc., according to standard Bank formats and distribute. • Coordinate schedules taking priorities into account, monitor changes, and communicate information to appropriate staff, inside and outside the immediate work unit, including officials outside the World Bank (WB). • Solve non-routine problems (e.g., responding to requests requiring file searches, and identification of correct operational procedures). • Preparation and logistical planning for various events, such as conferences, workshops, negotiations. • Create AIS, update milestones and tracks assigned tasks, project steps and timetables in the Operational Portal and SAP. • Monitor task budget/trust funds for specific projects on behalf of the team. • Assist with processing Consultant contracts and travel. Coordinate with relevant staff and to provide assistance and/or information on project-related matters when requested. • Maintain current distribution lists, phone/address lists of project/product contacts, and distributes documents for the team. • Maintain up-to-date work unit project and other files (both paper and electronic). • Work will involve frequent interaction with the following: Internal Contacts, Other VP and Global Practice (GP) units, IFC and MIGA, and other institutional units. Staff in all locations, locally and internationally, external Contacts such as Government Officials, Consultants, and External Organizations.

item.title: E T Temporary, Recruitment
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org BACKGROUND AND UNIT SUMMARY The Talent Acquisition team is within the Talent Acquisition and Global Mobility Department, providing end-to-end General recruitment support. The Senior HR Assistant, Recruitment provides high-quality operational and analytical support across the full recruitment lifecycle. The role ensures the accuracy, compliance, and timely execution of recruitment processes while delivering excellent service to candidates, hiring managers, and HR colleagues. The position requires strong operational discipline, data integrity, confidentiality, cultural competence, and proficiency across HR systems and recruitment operations. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Recruitment Case Management Operations •Manage the full recruitment lifecycle from job posting to onboarding, ensuring compliance with WBG policies and standards. •Partner with hiring managers to align timelines and processes while coordinating end-to-end recruitment workflows across longlisting, shortlisting, assessments, interviews, and final selection. Candidate Review and Longlisting •Conduct detailed reviews of external applications to produce high quality longlists aligned with business requirements, leveraging both scoring questions and detailed resume review. HR Systems Data Integrity •Maintain accurate system records and manage confidential candidate data, including timely candidate disposition according to recruitment process steps and WBG data standards. Stakeholder Engagement Inquiry Management •Respond to candidate, hiring manager, and HR inquiries with accurate guidance and timely recruitment updates. •Support hiring manager / selection committees by coordinating recruitment logistics, system transactions, and process steps. Governance, Compliance Continuous Improvement •Ensure recruitment activities comply with WBG policies, quality assurance standards, and governance standards. •Identify process gaps, support workflow improvements, and track resolution of quality assurance report. Service Quality Performance Standards •Contribute to meeting or exceeding the 75-day Time to Select service standard through effective time and workload management. •Demonstrate adaptability in response to changing systems, processes, and policy requirements.

For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context The World Bank Group Technology Office (ITSTO) defines and executes the technology strategy for the World Bank Group, ensuring that technological investments and standards deliver secure, resilient, and efficient platforms to support global operations. Through strategic planning, enterprise architecture, platform engineering, and core infrastructure management, ITSTO aligns technology initiatives with the Bank Group’s mission and business objectives. ITSTO drives technology-enabled innovation, modernizes infrastructure, and enhances organizational agility. By fostering collaboration across all World Bank Group entities—including IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID—ITSTO leverages technology as a catalyst for accelerating development impact and advancing digital transformation. Unit Context The Enterprise Architecture (ITSET) unit enables strategy execution by connecting business goals with technology investments, frameworks, and delivery models. ITSET ensures coherence, interoperability, and business value realization through standards, reference architecture, and governance. The unit drives portfolio alignment, process optimization, and adoption of data-driven practices across the WBG. Duties and accountabilities: The Associate Senior Enterprise Architect • Defines and governs portfolio architectures and product architectures to enable as well as accelerate solution delivery with the ITS portfolio by leveraging enterprise architecture frameworks, accelerators, guidelines and best practices while ensuring compliance with enterprise guardrails and architectural standards. • Drives enterprise-wide adoption and optimization of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), AI/ML and Agentic AI capabilities — including services such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Agent Service, and Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — and modern integration patterns to enable secure, scalable, and intelligent solutions across the organization. • Translates organizational strategy, business priorities, and digital transformation goals into coherent, actionable enterprise architecture direction and technology roadmaps — including strategies for multi-agent orchestration, autonomous workflows, and AI-augmented business processes. • Evaluates and applies industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices — including agentic AI orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework (converging AutoGen and Semantic Kernel), Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Strands Agents SDK, and OpenAI Agents SDK pragmatically to advance the World Bank Group's digital transformation and modernization objectives. • Produces high-quality, traceable architecture artifacts — including reference architectures, design patterns, solution guides, decision frameworks, and agentic AI governance models — that enable delivery teams to execute effectively and consistently across cloud-native and multi-agent environments. • Collaborates effectively with business leaders, solution architects, platform engineers, and Agile teams to co-create solutions — including AI agent workflows, RAG pipelines, multi-agent systems, and human-in-the-loop designs — that balance innovation, feasibility, and enterprise alignment. • Acts as an enterprise enabler and trusted advisor, aligning diverse stakeholders around shared architectural standards, patterns, and governance practices — including agent lifecycle governance, agent identity and access management, and responsible AI guardrails. • Demonstrates openness to feedback, fosters inclusive decision-making, and integrates diverse technical and business perspectives into architectural recommendations. • Balances innovation with risk management, regulatory compliance, security, and operational stability — including AI content safety guardrails, agent policy enforcement, FinOps for AI workloads, and agent observability — in all architectural decisions and guidance. • Architects and governs enterprise integration strategies leveraging API management platforms (Azure API Management, AWS API Gateway, MuleSoft, Apigee), integration Platform-as-a-Service (iPaaS) solutions (Azure Logic Apps, Azure Integration Services, AWS Step Functions, Workato), and enterprise service buses to enable seamless, secure, and governed connectivity across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. • Designs and enforces event-driven architectures (EDA) using cloud-native messaging and streaming services — including Amazon EventBridge, Amazon Kinesis, Azure Event Grid, Azure Service Bus, Google Pub/Sub, and Apache Kafka — to enable real-time, loosely coupled, and resilient enterprise integrations at scale. • Leads the definition and governance of API-led connectivity patterns — including experience APIs, process APIs, and system APIs — establishing API lifecycle management standards, versioning strategies, contract-first design, and developer portal governance to promote reusability and interoperability across enterprise systems. • Drives cloud integration architecture for multi-cloud and hybrid environments, defining patterns for cross-cloud data synchronization, identity federation (Entra ID, AWS IAM Identity Center, GCP Identity), network interconnectivity (ExpressRoute, Direct Connect, Cloud Interconnect), and workload portability to ensure operational resilience and vendor risk mitigation. • Defines enterprise integration standards for data interoperability and exchange, including master data management (MDM) integration, ETL/ELT pipeline architectures (Azure Data Factory, AWS Glue, dbt), real-time data streaming, and canonical data models to ensure data consistency, quality, and traceability across enterprise systems and analytics platforms. • Governs the adoption and architectural alignment of low-code/no-code integration platforms (Power Automate, Power Platform, Copilot Studio) and RPA tools within enterprise workflows, ensuring they comply with security, data governance, and architectural standards while accelerating citizen-led automation and business process digitization. • Establishes and enforces integration security and governance standards — including OAuth 2.0, mTLS, API key management, rate limiting, payload encryption, and zero-trust network access — to ensure all enterprise integrations meet organizational security policies, data protection requirements, and regulatory compliance mandates. Enterprise Architecture Development • Leads the development, evolution, and continuous improvement of enterprise architecture frameworks, reference architectures, design patterns, and governance guidelines to ensure technology initiatives are strategically aligned with business objectives. • Oversees the creation and maintenance of comprehensive architecture documentation — including standards, blueprints, decision records, and solution guides — to promote knowledge sharing, institutional learning, and consistent adoption across teams. • Establishes and maintains an enterprise architecture artifacts catalog encompassing reference architectures, best practices, guardrails, and reusable patterns to strengthen the EA foundation and enable enforceable governance. Architecture Analysis Innovation • Guides the assessment and rationalization of existing IT infrastructure, platforms, and applications to identify opportunities for modernization, optimization, and cost efficiency. • Manages and conducts architectural reviews and Well-Architected Framework assessments, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards, security requirements, and organizational goals. • Monitors industry trends, emerging technologies — including Agentic AI, cloud-native architectures, and advanced integration paradigms — to proactively identify opportunities for innovation, capability enhancement, and competitive advantage. • Evaluates vendor solutions, platforms, and tools through structured decision frameworks and comparative analyses to inform enterprise technology selection and adoption strategies. Stakeholder Engagement • Communicates architectural strategies, trade-offs, and recommendations to executive leadership and stakeholders with clarity, ensuring alignment and informed decision-making across the organization. • Manages collaboration with business leaders and program teams to elicit, analyze, and translate business requirements and strategic priorities into actionable technical specifications and architecture direction. • Oversees partnership with Agile and SAFe teams to ensure architectural alignment, scalability, technical guidance, and governance ac

The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context: The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context: ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context: The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) provides digital support for global and country-specific products, aiding thousands of task teams and country management units in better planning, tracking, and managing their operations, thereby improving country engagement. Additionally, ITSCE enables geospatial capabilities through self-service tools and analytics, allowing teams to monitor project preparation and implementation from anywhere. The Geospatial Solutions team is responsible for the delivery, evolution, and adoption of enterprise geospatial products and services that support operational, analytical, and decision-support needs across the World Bank Group. The team develops and manages platforms that integrate geospatial, statistical, and development data to generate location-based insights supporting country programs, project design and implementation, infrastructure planning, climate resilience, disaster risk management, results monitoring, and other operational priorities. The ITSCE unit is seeking a Product Manager who is passionate about geospatial technologies and committed to maximizing business value through technology delivery. The role will lead business engagement and product strategy for the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, working closely with operational stakeholders, Country Management Units, Global Practices, regional teams, and technology partners to identify opportunities, shape demand, and ensure geospatial investments deliver measurable operational impact. The Product Manager will play a key role in connecting development and operational needs with innovative geospatial capabilities while ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and technology strategy. Duties and responsibilities • Leads the product portfolio for Geospatial Solutions, working with agile team and Country Management Units, Global Practices, Regional teams, and operational stakeholders to identify high-value opportunities where geospatial solutions can improve development outcomes, operational efficiency, decision-making, and project delivery. • Deep understanding of business and operational priorities across regions and sectors, and translates these needs into geospatial product strategies, roadmaps, and investment priorities. • Defines and communicates a clear, scalable product vision and roadmap for Geospatial solutions that balances operational demand, delivery capacity, organizational priorities, and long-term sustainability. • Builds strategic relationships across the WBG and with external partner organizations to advance the adoption and impact of geospatial solutions. • Promotes the use of geospatial intelligence and spatial analytics in support of country programs, project implementation, climate resilience, disaster response, infrastructure planning, and monitoring and evaluation activities. • Provides leadership across agile teams, ensuring alignment, coordination, and execution so that development cycles translate into timely, high-quality product releases and operational value. • Facilitates continuous stakeholder engagement and feedback, identifies emerging opportunities, and evolves the product roadmap to maximize adoption and business impact across operational teams. • Designs governance structures and operating models for geospatial products, ensuring compliance with WBG policies, technology standards, and data management requirements while maintaining agility and innovation. • Oversees vendor and partner relationships, ensuring timely access to specialized geospatial expertise, technical capabilities, and delivery support. • Evaluates and recommends strategic investments that accelerate product development, improve scalability, enable replication across regions and business units, and effectively manage technical debt. • Monitors product-level financials and investment performance, ensuring resources are utilized effectively and aligned with business value and operational outcomes. • Leads complex, cross-functional initiatives involving software engineers, data scientists, GIS specialists, solution architects, business stakeholders, and operational teams to deliver impactful geospatial capabilities. • Identifies systemic challenges and cross-cutting opportunities across sectors and regions, applying structured analysis and strategic thinking to accelerate the adoption of geospatial solutions throughout the World Bank Group. • Represents the Geospatial Solutions portfolio in strategic discussions and governance forums, advocating for investments and priorities that support operational effectiveness and development impact.

Unit Context The Technology Platforms Team (ITSPL) is anchored in the Chief Technology Officer (ITSTO) division in ITS. ITS Technology Office (ITSTO) drives technology-enabled innovation and delivers the digital backbone for WBG's mission. It develops future-ready technology strategy, modernizes infrastructure, manages innovation, and fosters agility. The unit collaborates across the organization to leverage technology as a force multiplier, accelerating development impact and digital transformation globally. ITSPL delivers secure, cloud-first IT platforms with automation, self-service, and Platform Engineering (IaC). It manages databases, integrations, cloud ops to ensure reliable, scalable, cost-effective alignment with enterprise standards. The primary programs that the ITSTO unit is responsible for is providing a wide range of technical infrastructure services to meet the institution's computing needs, from mid-range servers, large scale servers, and the respective system, network, and supporting software on those platforms. It provides engineering, integration, and system administration services for Server Administration, Server Security, Backup/Restore, Storage, Virtual infrastructure (on premise and in cloud) and Data Center Management. Duties and accountabilities: The role will work as part of the Developer Experience (DevEx) team within the Shared Services Platform Engineering team in ITSPL. The role is responsible for designing and evolving developer-facing platforms that reduce cognitive load, minimize delivery friction, and provide consistent self-service experience for application teams. The role focuses on platform product engineering, including the Internal Developer Portal (IDP), standards, and golden paths, rather than operational execution or production support. The role requires a hands-on approach in a multicultural environment which supports diversity, continuous learning, enhancing skillsets and collaboration. The ideal candidate must demonstrate excellent communication skills as the position requires frequent interaction with multiple cross-functional teams. The candidate must possess a strong sense of curiosity, adaptability, and the drive to learn and innovate. We provide a meaningful, open, and collaborative environment. We have many interesting problems to solve, providing you an opportunity to develop your skills while contributing to the mission of the bank. We value teamwork, openness, curiosity, and persistence. Key Responsibilities: • Design, engineer, and evolve developer-facing platform services that improve developer experience by reducing cognitive load and unnecessary complexity. • Identify friction points across the application delivery lifecycle and translate them into platform capabilities, abstractions, and self-service workflows. • Define and maintain golden paths, templates, and standards that guide developers toward secure, compliant, and efficient delivery patterns. • Design and operate an Internal Developer Portal (IDP) that serves as the primary interface for platform capabilities, documentation, and workflows. • Build and maintain shared platform services using Infrastructure as Code and reusable automation components. • Design platform-level CI/CD capabilities as standardized services rather than application-specific implementations. • Implement governance-by-design through automated guardrails, policy-as-code, and embedded controls that do not burden developers. • Partner with cloud, security, architecture, and observability teams to ensure platform services are cohesive and aligned with enterprise standards. Continuously evaluate platform adoption, usability, and effectiveness, refining services to reduce bespoke engagement and manual coordination.

item.title: Underwriter
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . In February 2024, the World Bank Group announced a major upgrade to its guarantees business, by establishing as of July 1 2024, the Guarantee Platform (Platform) housed at MIGA. The Platform will deliver improved guarantee access through a unified team of guarantee specialists as well as innovative new guarantee solutions. These new reforms will help position the Platform/MIGA to achieve the goal of tripling annual guarantee issuance to $20 billion by 2030. MIGA’s Operations Department (MIGOP) leads MIGA’s guarantee business development and origination activities, structures transactions, leads projects through the underwriting and approval process, and manages guarantees portfolio. Within MIGOP, the Global Transaction Team (GTT) is a dedicated team of Analysts, Underwriters, and Senior Underwriters with a focus on underwriting MIGA’s guarantee transactions. MIGOP is seeking a highly experienced, motivated, and proactive Underwriter with strong project finance, public sector finance, political risk insurance, trade finance and/or structured finance underwriting skills, as well as client and new business origination skills, preferably gained in the energy and general infrastructure or financial sectors. While reporting to the Manager for GTT, the day to day activities of the Underwriter will focus mainly on leading transaction teams (comprised of individuals from across the Agency/Platform) and underwriting guarantee transactions as the transaction lead. Depending on experience, the activities may also include supporting business origination and transaction structuring activities. Through this role, the underwriter will develop a broad knowledge of the Platform’s guarantee activities by working on transactions across the Platform’s full product line and across regions and sectors (energy and extractives industries, infrastructure, financial institutions, capital markets, manufacturing, agriculture, services, etc.). Note that this is initially a Washington, DC-based position, however given the regionalization agenda, there is a strong possibility of this position being selected for decentralization. If shortlisted, this will be discussed with you at interview. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES • Lead a multi-disciplinary transaction team (sector, legal, environment and social, climate finance, reinsurance, gender, integrity, risk, development impact, etc.) through the transaction underwriting and approval process, which includes the organization and coordination of due diligence meetings and missions. • Conduct sector and project risk assessments, including contractual risk allocation and the technical and commercial viability of the investment project • Prepare and use complex financial models to, amongst others, analyze the financial viability of the investment project or support credit analysis for credit enhancement transactions • Work together with the risk management officers to analyze country/sub-sovereign project risks and mitigants and with the credit risk officers to support the analysis of state-owned enterprises (credit profile, institutional capacity, legal status and relationship with the government) • Collaborate with risk management officers and the transaction team to conduct development impact analyses of investment projects, including assessing the contribution to the host country's development, the broader impact on the industry and the private sector, and the benefits delivered to both direct and indirect stakeholders • Develop, together with the transaction team, recommendations for the contract of guarantee terms and conditions, including recommendations on appropriate guarantee structures and risk mitigants • Lead the negotiation of new contracts of guarantee with prospective guarantee holders and/or their advisors, in close coordination with the relevant Team Lead/Sector Manager and MIGA’s Legal Department • Engage closely with MIGA’s clients, conduct in-country and virtual due diligence meetings with host country government officials, and collaborate with partners (e.g., World Bank, IFC, and other development finance partners) • Prepare high quality guarantee proposal documents and present them for consideration to MIGA’s Senior Management and Board of Executive Directors • In close coordination with MIGA Senior/Sector Underwriters, Sector Managers, and Regional Heads, support MIGA’s new business origination and client management efforts aimed at generating a robust pipeline of business • As required, create and deliver new business origination-focused presentations to sponsors, government officials, state-owned enterprises, financial institutions, specialist industry groups, and forums
