item.title: Director General, WBG Independent Accountability Mechanism
item.description: Identifying and addressing environmental and social (E S) risks is critical to the World Bank Group (WBG)’s mission of ending poverty and promoting shared prosperity on a livable planet. To ensure that E S issues are properly identified and addressed, the WBG has put in place policies and procedures that guide WBG staff when they are supporting the design, implementation, and supervision of WBG-financed operations. The WBG has made significant efforts to leverage its private and public sector arms to provide better results and integrated solutions for its clients. To this end, a new integrated WBG E S structure has been established to better support public- and private-sector clients in achieving their sustainable development objectives and to establish a more robust system for proactive risk management. This new structure aims to: (i) ensure that attention to E S matters remains constant during the project life cycle; (ii) facilitate escalation of issues for rapid response; and (iii) strengthen technical oversight to ensure E S risks are flagged, monitored, and adequately addressed. Ultimately, the new E S structure aims to further strengthen development outcomes through better implementation of WBG E S policies in WBG-financed operations. To ensure that the WBG accountability framework remains effective and fit for purpose, on June 8, 2026, the Boards of Executive Directors of IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA (“the WBG Boards”) established a new, single WBG Independent Accountability Mechanism (WBG IAM). This new WBG IAM builds on decades of operational experience, institutional knowledge, and best practices of the IFC/MIGA Compliance Advisor Ombudsman (“CAO”), the WB Inspection Panel (“IPN”), and the WB Dispute Resolution Service (“DRS”). Its primary role remains to provide an independent and accessible forum for people who believe that they have been, or are likely to be, adversely affected by a WBG-financed operation to file a complaint and seek recourse, improve accountability and learning, facilitate dispute resolution, ensure compliance with the E S policies of the WBG, enhance E S sustainability and reduce the risk of harm to people and environment. The WBG embraces the vital role that a robust independent accountability mechanism plays in its broader role as a development institution. To ensure that E S issues are properly addressed, the WBG is committed to reinforcing the WBG IAM as a credible, effective, and responsive mechanism to help deliver environmentally and socially sound operations and enhance the WBG’s contribution to sustainable development. The WBG IAM serves as a forum for addressing the concerns of project-affected people in a manner that is independent, fair, and constructive. For this reason, the IAM is headed by a Director General (DG) reporting directly to the WBG Boards, under the oversight of CODE, and is independent from WBG operational management. About the World Bank Group Independent Accountability Mechanism To discharge its mandate, the WBG IAM has three functions: Dispute Resolution (DR) . Through Dispute Resolution, the mechanism works with affected communities and WBG clients to resolve grievances using a voluntary, flexible, neutral, and collaborative problem-solving approach, including mediation, negotiation, and facilitated dialogue. Compliance. Through its Compliance function, the mechanism serves as an independent, factfinding investigative body on behalf of the WBG Boards. In the case of public sector operations, the mechanism assesses the Bank’s alleged failure to follow its operational policies and procedures with respect to the design, appraisal, and/or implementation/supervision of a project financed by the Bank. For complaints on private sector operations, the mechanism carries out reviews of IFC/MIGA compliance with their E S obligations set out in the Sustainability Framework , assesses related harm, and recommends remedial actions to address non-compliance and harm where appropriate. The compliance function is not a judicial, quasi-judicial, or legal enforcement mechanism, nor is it designed as a substitute for national courts or regulatory processes. Advisory. The IAM’s advisory function provides independent and ad hoc advice to the WBG Boards and Management on systemic issues identified from case data with the view of improving WBG performance on E S sustainability and reducing the risk of harm to people and the environment. Duties and Responsibilities The WBG IAM DG will be appointed by and will report to the WBG Boards under the oversight of the Committee on Development Effectiveness (CODE). The DG is directly accountable to the Boards and is not part of, and does not report to, Management. The DG’s key duties and responsibilities include: • Supporting the development and implementation of the new WBG IAM policy; facilitating the transition process from the current accountability system to the new WBG IAM; and leading the change management required to integrate WBG IAM operations, while safeguarding the IAM’s independence and credibility. • Ensuring the effective functioning of the IAM’s three arms—Dispute Resolution, Compliance, and Advisory—by overseeing cases, meeting timelines, maintaining process integrity and quality control, establishing internal procedures and guidelines with DR, Compliance, and Advisory staff, and supervising the receipt, acknowledgment, eligibility assessment, and further processing of complaints. • Directing complex, multi-disciplinary investigations and ensuring impartial and thorough factfinding. • Managing the IAM’s day-to-day operations, including planning, directing, and organizing its work program, budget, and staff performance, while ensuring budget resources are managed in line with relevant WBG rules, policies, and internal controls. • Presenting IAM budget requests to the Boards annually and ensuring adherence to budgetary levels established by the WBG Boards. • Monitoring and reporting on key performance indicators to assess the IAM’s continued effectiveness, tracking progress against institutional objectives, and supporting continuous improvement. • Communicating with complainants and affected parties while managing retaliation risks and safeguarding confidential business information; maintaining appropriate communication with relevant WBG departments; and fostering strong relationships with key stakeholders, including requesters, civil society organizations, academia, and other relevant parties. • Providing strategic leadership to the IAM team, overseeing delivery of the IAM’s objectives, goals, guidelines, and work programs, and managing staff while fostering a culture of integrity and inclusion, supporting professional development, and ensuring compliance with applicable administrative, staff rules and workplace standards. • Hiring staff and consultants/independent contractors as needed, in line with Bank policies, procedures, and with due attention to budget considerations; resolving issues arising from coordination across IAM functions; and managing staff, including approving work programs and administrative matters such as contracts, leave, mission travel, and expenses. Building and maintaining as needed a roster of independent experts (e.g., in areas such as mediation, dispute resolution, compliance, auditing, resettlement, indigenous peoples, E S safeguard policies, among others). • Ensuring the integrity, quality, coherence, and accuracy of IAM reports, findings, recommendations, and other products, in line with applicable Bank policies and procedures. • Representing the IAM in public and private fora, overseeing stakeholder outreach and guidance, and ensuring that the IAM’s website, public registry, archive system, and social media provide current, relevant, and accurate information on its work and activities. • Meeting regularly with the relevant Board Committee Chairs to keep the Committees and the Boards informed of the IAM’s activities, preparing reports for the Boards as needed, and performing other IAM-related functions as assigned by the WBG Boards. • Ensuring and safeguarding independence from all stakeholders possibly linked to a case and maintaining its reporting line to the Boards. • During the transition period the DG will report periodically to the Board through CODE and participate in the development of the new IAM policy, taking into consideration the Board’s decision on the seven policy principles and building on the relevant provisions of the current IAM policies, and lead in its implementation. The DG will also lead in developing the operating procedures for the new IAM, and undertake workforce planning, adjustment of processes and systems while ensuring continuity, credibility, and effectiveness during the transition. • The DG will coordinate with CAO, DRS, and IPN to develop transitional arrangements, including with regard to existing cases, and manage the closure of the current mechanisms while launching the new, integrated WBG IAM. The incumbent for this position will be a full-time staff of the WBG at the level of Vice President, with this level of seniority reflecting the institutional importance of the role. S/he is subject to the confidentiality provisions set forth in WBG policies on access to information and will be subject to the Group Staff Rules and Staff Code of Conduct. The appointment is for a period of five (5) years, non-renewable and s/he will not be employed by the WBG following the end of their term. Only the WBG Boards may terminate the employment of the DG for cause.

item.title: Investment Officer - Portfolio, Data and Transformation AI Officer
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . The Manufacturing, Agribusiness, and Services (MAS) department is one of IFC’s key industry groups responsible for a significant portion of IFC’s business volume, profitability, and development reach. MAS operates across a wide range of sub-sectors, including manufacturing, chemicals, healthcare, education, property, retail, tourism, agribusiness, and forestry, among others, providing investment and advisory services delivered globally to IFC’s clients through its global network. These sectors represent a significant share of economic activity and are central to job creation and sustainable growth. Do you want to build a career leading the oversight of a fast-growing portfolio of long-term sustainable investments while shaping how AI and data-driven investment decisions and portfolio management are conducted across IFC? MAS Latin America and the Caribbean and Europe (MAS LAC Europe) is seeking to recruit an Investment Officer – Portfolio, Data and AI Transformation Lead to collaborate on MAS LAC Europe current ~US$11.2 billion portfolio, while driving the adoption of data and AI to enhance efficiency, risk management, and decision-making across both portfolio management and new business. Duties and Accountabilities A. Portfolio Oversight Risk Management • Active portfolio management. Participates in the oversight of portfolio performance, including credit quality, profitability, E S compliance, development impact, and climate alignment. • Proactively provide data-driven portfolio monitoring reports and ad hoc analyses by combining IFC's rating methodologies and other internal data sources with external data to track portfolio trends, identify emerging risks and recommend timely actions. • Oversee portfolio actions (waivers, consents, restructurings, equity exits, etc.), ensuring consistency and quality of decision-making. • Lead portfolio reviews and management reporting, including risk trends, stress tests, watchlists, equity valuations, NPLs, and adequacy of individual loss reserves. • Portfolio credit rating reviews and team support. Participates in the timely review of credit ratings and related portfolio actions to maintain quality and consistency across the portfolio. Support investment and portfolio teams in their assessments and rating submissions, including guiding junior staff and building analytical and data literacy capability across the team. • Investment and risk assessment. Support teams and the Chair on new transactions, particularly small transactions, providing efficient, high-quality assessment of financial and non-financial risk and helping assign and substantiate credit and facility ratings, in line with IFC's risk appetite, policies, and procedures. B. AI Data-Driven Transformation • Lead the responsible deployment of AI and automation to enhance efficiency, consistency, and quality across the investment lifecycle. • Drive adoption of AI in: o Financial spreading and data extraction o Credit and risk analysis o Portfolio monitoring, dashboards, and reporting o Preparation of investment documentation and internal analysis • Ensure AI solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned with IFC standards, including model governance, explainability, and bias controls. • Act as a focal point for data analytics and AI working groups across-regional initiatives, promoting knowledge sharing and consistent approaches. • AI for efficiency across the cycle. Lead the responsible use of AI and automation to improve efficiency and quality in both investment processing and portfolio management, automating data extraction, financial spreading, and routine analysis and reporting, and supporting investment analysis and risk assessment so officers can focus their time on judgment. C. Client Management Portfolio Optimization • Manage key client relationships and lead restructurings, rescheduling, and complex portfolio situations. • Minimize NPLs and optimize portfolio risk-return profile. • Oversee equity portfolio performance, including valuations, ratings, exits, and governance. D. Innovation, Knowledge Capability Building • Mentor junior staff and strengthen analytical, data, and AI literacy across the team • Promote best practices in portfolio management, AI use, and investment analysis • Contribute to knowledge sharing across MAS LAC Europe and global MAS teams E. Compliance Governance • Ensure adherence to IFC policies, procedures, and portfolio scorecard metrics • Coordinate with ESG, legal, insurance, and governance teams to address portfolio risks and compliance gaps

item.title: Associate Senior Service Management Officer (Agentic AI & Hyperautomation Portfolio Lead)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context: The World Bank Group (WBG) is accelerating its use of artificial intelligence and automation to enhance operational efficiency, knowledge management, and development impact. As part of this effort, the Information Technology Solutions (ITS) vice presidency—and specifically the ITSSG team—is expanding its capacity in Hyperautomation. This involves integrating advanced AI with core business processes to create a seamless, intelligent automation fabric. A key component of this strategy is the development of agentic AI systems: autonomous, multi-step AI workflows capable of reasoning, tool use, and decision-making. This Terms of Reference outlines the scope of work for a Lead Agentic AI Hyperautomation Strategist at the GG staff level, based in Washington DC, USA to lead the design, strategy, and implementation of these transformative solutions. Objective The Agentic AI Hyperautomation Portfolio Lead will serve as a strategic leader within ITSSG, helping to advance the adoption of Agentic AI, intelligent automation, and AI orchestration capabilities across ITS. Working closely with business, product, architecture, engineering, and platform teams, the role will identify opportunities to drive operational efficiency, improve service delivery, and accelerate digital transformation through AI-powered automation. The successful candidate will influence strategic direction, help shape technology and investment decisions, foster enterprise adoption, and provide leadership across a portfolio of AI and automation initiatives. The role requires a combination of technology expertise, strategic thinking, stakeholder engagement, and the ability to translate emerging capabilities into measurable business outcomes. Scope of Work The staff will be responsible for the following: 1. Strategic Leadership Portfolio Management • Serve as a strategic advisor on Agentic AI, AI orchestration, and Hyperautomation opportunities across ITS. • Help shape priorities, roadmaps, and investment decisions relating to intelligent automation and AI-enabled transformation. • Identify, assess, and prioritize opportunities where Agentic AI and Hyperautomation can deliver measurable operational and business value. • Develop business cases, value realization frameworks, and recommendations to support decision-making and investment planning. • Monitor market developments, emerging technologies, and industry trends, providing guidance on their potential application within WBG. 2. AI Orchestration Hyperautomation Enablement • Promote a cohesive approach to Agentic AI and Hyperautomation across platforms, products, and business domains. • Partner with architecture, engineering, service management, and platform teams to develop scalable patterns and reusable capabilities. • Support the evolution of enterprise AI orchestration capabilities that enable complex workflows spanning multiple systems and technologies. • Influence the design and adoption of solutions that combine AI, workflow automation, and enterprise platforms to improve business outcomes. • Encourage reuse, standardization, and alignment across AI and automation initiatives to maximize value and reduce duplication. 3. Governance, Risk Responsible AI • Support the development and adoption of governance frameworks, standards, and controls for Agentic AI and intelligent automation. • Partner with security, risk, legal, compliance, procurement, and architecture stakeholders to ensure solutions align with institutional policies and standards. • Promote responsible AI practices, including transparency, security, auditability, and operational oversight. • Contribute to the development of guardrails and governance mechanisms that enable innovation while appropriately managing risk. • Advocate for scalable approaches to lifecycle management, monitoring, and operational governance of AI-enabled services. 4. Stakeholder Engagement Organizational Influence • Build strong relationships across ITS and business stakeholders to promote the effective adoption of Agentic AI and Hyperautomation capabilities. • Facilitate alignment across product, platform, architecture, and operational teams on strategic priorities and implementation approaches. • Communicate opportunities, risks, recommendations, and outcomes to senior leaders and governance forums. • Act as a champion for AI-enabled transformation, helping stakeholders understand emerging capabilities and their practical application. • Influence decision-making through collaboration, thought leadership, and trusted advisory relationships. 5. Innovation, Platform Vendor Strategy • Lead assessments of emerging Agentic AI, orchestration, and automation technologies and their applicability within the WBG environment. • Provide recommendations on platform capabilities, technology direction, and strategic investments. • Engage with strategic vendors and industry partners to understand product roadmaps, innovation trends, and emerging capabilities. • Identify opportunities to leverage common enterprise platforms and services to accelerate adoption and value realization. • Foster innovation and knowledge sharing through communities of practice and cross-functional collaboration. 6. Delivery Oversight Value Realization • Provide strategic oversight and guidance across a portfolio of AI and automation initiatives. • Establish measures to track adoption, business value, operational improvements, and organizational impact. • Identify and address barriers to adoption, scalability, and value realization. • Support successful implementation by aligning stakeholders, managing dependencies, and promoting sustainable operating models. • Help ensure initiatives deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, effectiveness, employee experience, and service outcomes.

item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . VPU Context The mission of the Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) is to leverage information and technology as a force multiplier to accelerate, deepen, and sustain development impact. Their vision is to harness information and technology for a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information on ITS, check this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w . Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital solutions that support global and country-specific products, enables systems aligned with the World Bank Group’s Country Engagement Model, and provides geospatial capabilities that enhance project visibility, spatial analysis, and impact tracking. The unit also drives the design and delivery of AI-powered business solutions that strengthen regional operations and country engagement. The ITSCE unit is seeking a Solutions Architect to define and oversee the technical architecture for digital solutions supporting country teams, including the Country Partnership Framework (CPF) and Country Policy and Institutional Assessment (CPIA) platforms. These products are central to country engagement, strategy development, and operational assessment processes, requiring secure, scalable, maintainable, and well-integrated technology solutions. The Solutions Architect will work closely with country teams, Operations Policy and Country Services (OPCS), product owners, IT delivery teams, platform and security specialists, and operational support teams to ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and the World Bank Group’s strategic priorities. The role is responsible for translating business needs into sustainable technical designs, providing architectural leadership throughout the solution lifecycle, and ensuring the successful delivery of high-quality digital products. Specific Responsibilities: • Define solution architecture, integration patterns, and low- and high-level designs for CPF, CPIA, and related ITSCE Country Solutions products, ensuring alignment with business, enterprise, security, and operational requirements. • Partner with product owners, country teams, OPCS, and IT delivery teams to translate business priorities into feasible solution options, implementation guidance, and technical decisions. • Assess trade-offs, dependencies, risks, non-functional requirements, and total cost of ownership to support secure, scalable, and sustainable technology solutions. • Collaborate with platform, security, infrastructure, and operations teams to ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and operational requirements. • Prepare architecture diagrams, technical presentations, decision records, recommendations, and solution walkthroughs to support alignment, governance, and informed decision-making. • Provide technical leadership throughout the solution lifecycle, including design reviews, implementation guidance, code reviews, and mentoring of engineering teams. • Promote reuse, standardization, interoperability, security-by-design, maintainability, and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including AI-enabled capabilities. • Support Agile and SAFe delivery practices by participating in planning, design discussions, technical reviews, and continuous improvement activities.

item.title: Operations Analyst, Eastern Europe
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) is a member of the World Bank Group with a mission to promote foreign direct investment into developing countries to help end extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet. MIGA houses the World Bank Group (WBG) guarantee platform which brings together products and experts from the World Bank, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and MIGA for simplicity, efficiency, and speed. MIGA serves as a one-stop shop for all WBG guarantee business, providing the best guarantee solutions for clients to meet project needs and development priorities. The platform provides three types of coverages: credit guarantees for loans to the public or private sector; trade finance guarantees for trade finance projects involving public entities; and political risk insurance against non-commercial risks for private sector projects or public-private partnerships. For more information, visit www.miga.org . MIGA’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia (ECA) Regional Hub is currently recruiting an Operations Analyst to support MIGA activities in ECA including business development, relationship management with key clients and partners, and coordination of relationships with MIGA stakeholders including shareholders, development partner agencies, development finance institutions, and private sector players in Eastern Europe. The position will be based in Vienna, Austria or Paris, France and, supervised by the Eastern Europe Regional Head. Duties and Accountabilities Business development: • Perform independent research on various topics across different sectors and regions, including preparation of briefing notes for senior management; background information and financial analysis of specific companies; trends in foreign direct investment (FDI); identification of business opportunities across sectors and regions • Conduct mapping of potential clients and partners for MIGA, including coordination with country and sector specific business development strategies • Collect data, analyze, and synthesize data from public and WBG sources for business development and project assessment • Research and identify investor/sector conferences relevant for sectors and regions • Prepare reports, presentations, talking points and minutes for the team and other groups in MIGA • Support relationship activities with clients and partners: use the client management system and provide reports as requested; prepare client pitch books and other marketing presentations; support client meetings and necessary follow-ups • Develop and maintain database and tracking systems related to special sector initiatives Execution: • Assist in underwriting political risk insurance (PRI) and credit enhancement guarantees in various sectors and support team members on complex transactions with an emphasis on financial modeling and credit analysis • Prepare sections of relevant reports (sector updates, sub-sector information, strategy documents, briefing notes, underwriting papers, etc.) and contribute to the formulation of conclusions and recommendations • Liaise with counterparties to ascertain data quality in MIGA databases • Coordinate follow- up as required with sponsors, financiers, and public sector counterparties involved in project specification, definition, bidding preparation, negotiation, awarding of contract and project implementation and monitoring • Track status of projects at various stages in MIGA systems and provide regular updates as agreed with country representative or another designated person • Perform other duties as may be assigned by the manager

item.title: Operations Analyst-Climate and Sustainable Finance Analyst
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org. VPU Context: As part of the World Bank Group’s Planet Vertical, the Climate Department supports WBG delivery on climate and development. It helps operational teams integrate mitigation, adaptation, resilience, and climate risk considerations into projects, programs, analytics, and client engagement. The Department works across WBG institutions, Global Practices, regions, and corporate functions to strengthen delivery, credibility, and consistency. Unit Context: The Climate Department’s Sustainable Finance and Transaction Solutions unit (KTCSS) helps the WBG develop scalable solutions that respond to client demand and support credible implementation across IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA. Its work spans sustainable finance solutions for mitigation and adaptation, climate co-benefits measurement, Paris Alignment, climate risk management, GHG accounting, and climate outcomes metrics. KTCSS also develops the methodologies, tools, and systems needed to mainstream these approaches and support consistent, efficient delivery across operations. It supports operational teams, develops practical guidance and knowledge, strengthens data and reporting, and advances product innovation and data- and AI-enabled solutions. The unit is seeking a versatile analyst to provide analytical, operational, and coordination support across this portfolio. The assignment mix will evolve with team priorities. The role is suited to a strong climate generalist with sound core skills, an interest in climate and sustainable finance, good judgment, and a willingness to learn quickly and roll up their sleeves Duties and accountabilities: •Conduct industry, market, project, and institutional research. Analyze economic, financial, technical, and portfolio data to support operational work, business development, and management decisions. Synthesize findings for different audiences. •Support team workstreams and WBG operations on Paris Alignment, climate co-benefits, sustainable finance, adaptation and resilience, climate risk, and related topics, under guidance from senior colleagues. •Support GHG accounting and climate outcomes metrics. Collect, clean, validate, and analyze data; document assumptions and results; and contribute to improving methodologies, tools, and reporting. This may include gross, net, and financed emissions and resilience outcomes. •Prepare briefs, presentations, reports, guidance, checklists, training and knowledge materials, and communications for internal and external audiences. Support editing, quality review, and dissemination. •Support practical tools, dashboards, data systems, workflow improvements, automation, and AI-enabled solutions, including testing, quality control, user support, and maintenance. •Provide project-management and internal delivery support, including work planning, portfolio monitoring, procurement and contract coordination, meetings and events, stakeholder follow-up, and tracking deliverables. •Collaborate across WBG institutions, regions, Global Practices, operational teams, and corporate functions. Take ownership, respond quickly, shift flexibly between workstreams, and undertake additional assignments as priorities evolve.
item.dc:creator: World Bank Group

item.title: Digital & AI Specialist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank Group provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank Group is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, www.worldbank.org Unit(s) Context The South Asia Region The South Asia Region comprises six countries (India, Bhutan, , Maldives, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Sri Lanka) that range in size from India (with a population of over 1 billion) to Maldives (with 0.3 million people). The region has experienced a long period of robust economic growth, averaging 6% a year over the past 20 years. This strong growth has translated into reducing extreme poverty and strong improvements in human development. At the same time, the region remains home to one-third of the world’s poorest, and persistent structural challenges threaten to undermine sustained growth, hindering the region’s ability to create jobs and respond to climate shocks. The South Asia Region: https://www.worldbank.org/en/region/sar Digital AI Vice Presidency Digital technologies offer a unique opportunity to transform development through digital solutions. The Digital AI Vice Presidency and its global and regional teams will support client countries in building the foundational and cross-cutting elements of digital transformation through: • Building broadband connectivity infrastructure, last mile access and data platforms (including last mile connectivity and data infrastructure) • Strengthening digital public infrastructure (DPI), including digital ID, data sharing, verifiable credentials and digitalizing government services that improve accountability and transparency • Protecting institutions, businesses, and citizens through cybersecurity and data protection privacy • Developing ICT sectors and supporting digital entrepreneurship, skills, and jobs • Enabling AI-ready economies by supporting governments in building the policy, regulatory, data, and infrastructure foundations needed to harness AI responsibly and at scale • Supporting the Vice presidencies of People, Prosperity, Planet, and Infrastructure in the digitalization efforts of their clients, and in leveraging digital solutions, including building client sectoral digital capacity, defining and implementing sectoral specific AI strategies, and designing AI-powered solutions For more information: https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/digital The roles and responsibilities include but are not limited to: The Opportunity The World Bank Group’s (WBG) engagement on digital development is rapidly growing in the South Asia region (SAR) in response to increased client demand for knowledge, technical assistance, and financing. The overall SAR Digital agenda aims to enhance the speed, scale, and impact of the WBG’s support to enable countries to make the most of digital opportunities and address emerging challenges in an effective and agile manner. SAR Digital Unit is looking for a Digital AI Specialist to be based in New Delhi, India. The position will report to the South Asia Regional Practice Manager for Digital AI and work with the Digital AI team in India, as with other team members based globally. The Specialist will bring hands-on expertise in the design, architecture, and deployment of AI systems in the public sector. Beyond policy and regulatory advice, the role requires the ability to guide governments through the full lifecycle of AI adoption - from use-case identification and feasibility assessment, through solution architecture, data readiness, model selection and procurement, to responsible deployment, monitoring, and scaling. A particular focus will be on applying AI to development challenges in sectors such as health, agriculture, education, social protection, and service delivery, and on building the technical capacity of client institutions to sustain these solutions More specifically, the roles and responsibilities are to: The Digital AI Specialist, together with the Digital AI Team in India, and the broader team will be responsible for Supporting client engagements in India and supervising activities in the sector as a technical expert. These include • Support policy dialogue with senior government officials, coordinate across relevant government agencies, development partners and other World Bank Global Departments and verticals. • Contribute to the design, preparation and supervision of World Bank Group financed investment and policy reform programs on digital and AI, with a particular emphasis on (i) strengthening infrastructure for an AI ready economy, including data centres and cloud, by leveraging private sector investments, (ii) Design and implementation of digital public infrastructure systems for citizen centric service delivery Advise clients on strategies, best practices and design of programs to develop the foundations of their digital economies. This may include participating in technical assistance activities and providing just-in-time technical and strategic expertise on the design of the overall policy, that includes designing national AI strategies, AI governance and regulatory frameworks, data governance regimes, and AI ethics and responsible AI policies that are contextually appropriate for developing country contexts. • Liaise and provide guidance to colleagues working in other sectors (including agriculture, health, education, energy, financial services, transport, etc.) on how to leverage digital technologies and AI to improve public service delivery and efficiency in the respective sectors and to stimulate digital innovation, entrepreneurship and investment in those sectors by private sector actors. • Provide technical leadership on the design and deployment of AI solutions in government, including solution architecture, data pipelines and data readiness assessments, choice of models and platforms (including open-source and frontier models), cloud/compute arrangements, integration with digital public infrastructure, and MLOps/deployment practices appropriate for public sector environments. • Advise clients on sectoral AI applications for development — e.g., AI for health diagnostics and supply chains, agricultural advisory services, personalized learning, social protection targeting and G2P delivery — including assessing use-case feasibility, cost, risks, and pathways to scale. • Support clients in operationalizing responsible AI in deployed systems, including bias testing, safety evaluations, human-in-the-loop design, grievance redress, and post-deployment monitoring. • Contribute to building client-side technical capacity for AI adoption, including institutional arrangements (e.g., AI units/centers of excellence), procurement approaches for AI systems, and talent and skills strategies.

item.description: {"id":"744000141742372","name":"Junior Power Sector Analyst","uuid":"fa9ad93f-ffb7-4a9d-b501-af2d11b2eb4b","jobId":"f204b628-f7b3-4abf-af0e-b0b5f4e2ad25","jobAdId":"430beef4-4469-4dd7-a0ff-992f29633839","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3349P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL4","valueLabel":"PAL4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-05T14:57:55.953Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141742372-junior-power-sector-analyst","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141742372-junior-power-sector-analyst?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/fa9ad93f-ffb7-4a9d-b501-af2d11b2eb4b?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation committed to advancing security of energy supply, economic growth and environmental sustainability through energy policy co-operation. The IEA operates as an autonomous body within the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The IEA seeks to recruit Junior Power Sector Analysts to contribute to its analytical work on power systems and markets in the Electricity Systems and Markets Division (ESM). The Power Sector Analysts will contribute to the Division’s work on electricity systems and markets, with a particular focus on grids. This includes providing quantitative and qualitative analysis, modelling, and drafting, including for the IEA’s flagship annual Electricity report. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Modelling, analysis and drafting Monitor and analyse technical, regulatory and policy developments in electricity systems and markets at the global, regional and country level. Support the Division’s analytical output on grids, system flexibility and regulation. Contribute to the modelling of the medium-term electricity forecast. This involves the development, operation and maintenance of power sector models. Update and improve relevant technical, regulatory and policy databases on electricity demand, supply and grids (transmission and distribution). Support the end-to-end preparation of the IEA’s Electricity report. Contribute to relevant reports, working papers, presentations and briefing notes for senior management. Collaboration and outreach Support preparations as needed for meetings of IEA standing committees, working parties and other groups as required; participate in relevant meetings of other international organisations; provide support for the development of reports, analyses and information items for these meetings. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate Profile Academic Background Advanced university degree or PhD in Electrical / Power / Energy Systems Engineering, Energy Economics, Physics or a related discipline. Professional Background A minimum of three years experience of direct power systems work experience in the electricity industry, economic consulting or grid technology companies working on transmission or distribution networks, system operation, energy management and related fields. Strong technical background in power systems and experience working with power utilities and/or grid operators. In-depth understanding of electricity security concepts, power market fundamentals, and the interaction between system operations and market incentives. Solid knowledge of medium- and low-voltage distribution grids, with an understanding of the frameworks governing connection processes and the integration of distributed energy resources. Experience with network planning and operational practices aimed at enhancing the efficiency and utilisation of existing infrastructure is desirable. Experience with power system modelling, such as steady‑state network modelling, dynamic and transient stability modelling, or grid planning and expansion studies, would be an advantage. Proven analytical abilities and excellent writing skills as demonstrated in past work products (analytical reports, quantitative analysis, operative models, and/or published papers). Tools Excellent command of Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel. Solid knowledge of relevant coding languages (e.g. Python, R). Experience with data visualisation tools (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) and database management (SQL) is desirable. Experience with optimisation models and platforms such as Pyomo, PyPSA or GAMS would be an asset. Languages Excellent written and oral command of English, including drafting and proofreading. Knowledge of one or more other working languages would be an asset. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . Contract Duration 2 years fixed-term appointment, with the possibility of renewal. Please note that our Rules and Regulations stipulate that the mandatory retirement age is 67. Selection Process For retained candidates, the selection process may include a video-recorded interview, job-based assessment and panel interviews. This is recruitment is meant to develop a roster for IEA Managers’ consideration for future upcoming roles at the Agency. Successful candidates may be cleared and following this process further interviews may follow to assess the suitability of the profiles towards specific needs. Following this recruitment process cleared further interviews may follow for cleared candidates depending on the needs of the Agency and the expertise/area of interest of the candidate. Closing Date This vacancy should be filled as soon as possible, and applications should reach us no later than 14th September 2026 at 23h59 CET (Paris time). What the OECD offers Monthly salary starts at 6 008 EUR, plus allowances based on eligibility, exempt of French income tax. Click here to consult the Staff Regulations applicable to officials of the OECD. Please note that from 1 July 2025, all Official appointments will be made under the OECD’s new contractual modalities . Click here to learn more about what we offer and why the OECD is a great place to work. Click here to browse our People Management Guidebook and learn more about all aspects relating to people at the OECD, our workplace environment and many other policies supporting staff in their daily life. Please note that the appointment may be made at one grade lower in the specified job family, based on the qualifications and professional experience of the selected applicant. This vacancy is intended to be used to create a pool of candidates for comparable positions, both for open-ended and fixed-term functions. The OECD is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes the applications of all qualified candidates [who are nationals of OECD Member Countries ] , irrespective of their racial or ethnic origin, opinions or beliefs, gender, sexual orientation, health or disabilities. The OECD promotes an optimal use of resources in order to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. Staff members are encouraged to actively contribute to this goal. Learn more about what we offer and why the OECD is a great place to work. item.description: {"id":"744000141745339","name":"Analyste junior du secteur de l’électricité","uuid":"5e6c8476-3d80-44c6-93f4-4bb306ae803a","jobId":"f204b628-f7b3-4abf-af0e-b0b5f4e2ad25","jobAdId":"556ed716-3c68-4089-9373-8da09b8d4930","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3349P","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10000727","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"5a9445ef-058b-4346-8dca-ef49c8638ded","valueLabel":"IEA"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL4","valueLabel":"PAL4"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-05T15:03:43.330Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141745339-analyste-junior-du-secteur-de-l-electricite","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000141745339-analyste-junior-du-secteur-de-l-electricite?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/5e6c8476-3d80-44c6-93f4-4bb306ae803a?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. L’ Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE) est une organisation intergouvernementale qui œuvre en faveur de la sécurité des approvisionnements énergétiques, de la croissance économique et de la durabilité environnementale en promouvant la coopération dans le domaine des politiques énergétiques. L’AIE fonctionne en tant qu’organe autonome au sein de l’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques. L’AIE recherche des analystes juniors du secteur de l’électricité pour contribuer à ses travaux d’analyse sur les systèmes et les marchés de l’électricité au sein de sa Division des systèmes et marchés de l’électricité (ESM). Les personnes retenues prendront part aux travaux de la Division sur les systèmes et marchés de l’électricité et, en particulier, les réseaux. Il s’agira de produire des analyses quantitatives et qualitatives, de réaliser des modélisations et de rédiger des textes, notamment pour le rapport phare annuel de l’AIE consacré à l’électricité. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Modélisation, analyse et rédaction Suivre et analyser les avancées techniques et les évolutions de la réglementation et de l’action publique en lien avec les systèmes et les marchés de l’électricité, aux niveaux mondial, régional et national. Prêter son concours aux travaux d’analyse de la Division sur les réseaux, la flexibilité du système électrique et la réglementation. Contribuer à la réalisation de modélisations en vue d’établir des prévisions à moyen terme relatives à l’électricité : à cet effet, mettre au point, appliquer et actualiser des modèles du secteur de l’électricité. Mettre à jour et améliorer les bases de données pertinentes sur les avancées techniques, la réglementation et l’action publique, qui concernent l’offre et la demande d’électricité ainsi que les réseaux (transport et distribution). Aider à préparer, de bout en bout, le rapport de l’AIE sur l’électricité. Participer à la rédaction de rapports et de documents de travail, et à la préparation d’exposés et de notes de synthèse à l’intention de l’équipe de direction. Collaboration et relations avec l’extérieur Prêter son concours, en tant que de besoin, aux préparatifs des réunions des comités permanents, des groupes de travail et, si nécessaire, d’autres groupes de l’AIE ; participer aux réunions pertinentes d’autres organisations internationales ; concourir à l’établissement des rapports, analyses et éléments d’information destinés à ces réunions. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur ou doctorat en génie électrique, génie énergétique, génie des systèmes énergétiques, économie de l’énergie, physique ou dans une discipline connexe. Expérience professionnelle Au moins trois ans d’expérience directement acquise sur les systèmes électriques dans une entreprise du secteur de l’électricité, une société de conseil économique ou une entreprise axée sur les technologies de réseau, travaillant sur les réseaux de transport ou de distribution, l’exploitation des systèmes, la gestion de l’énergie ou un domaine connexe. Solide connaissance technique des systèmes électriques et expérience du travail avec des compagnies d’électricité et/ou des gestionnaires de réseau de transport. Compréhension approfondie des concepts liés à la sécurité de l’approvisionnement en électricité, des fondamentaux du marché de l’électricité et de l’interaction entre l’exploitation du système et les incitations du marché. Solide connaissance des réseaux de distribution de moyenne et de basse tension, avec une bonne compréhension des cadres régissant les processus de raccordement et l’intégration des ressources énergétiques décentralisées. Une expérience de la planification du réseau et des pratiques opérationnelles visant à améliorer l’efficience et l’utilisation des infrastructures existantes est souhaitable. Une expérience de la modélisation des systèmes électriques, notamment la modélisation des réseaux en régime stationnaire, en régime dynamique ou en stabilité transitoire, ou de l’étude de la planification ou de l’extension du réseau constituerait un avantage. Capacités d’analyse avérées et excellente compétence rédactionnelle, confirmées par les produits de travaux antérieurs (rapports analytiques, analyses quantitatives, modèles opératoires et/ou textes publiés). Outils Excellente maîtrise des applications Microsoft Office, en particulier d’Excel. Solide connaissance de langages de programmation pertinents (Python ou R, par exemple). Une expérience des outils de visualisation des données (Power BI, Tableau, par exemple) et de la gestion de base de données (SQL) est souhaitable. Une expérience des modèles et des plateformes d’optimisation telles que Pyomo, PyPSA ou GAMS constituerait un atout. Langues Excellente maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral, avec des compétences rédactionnelles et éditoriales. La connaissance d’une ou de plusieurs autres langues constituerait un atout. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de deux ans, avec possibilité de renouvellement. Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Processus de sélection Pour les personnes retenues à l’issue de la présélection, la procédure de recrutement peut comporter l’enregistrement d’un entretien vidéo, une évaluation des compétences professionnelles et un entretien avec un jury. Le présent processus de sélection permettra d’établir une liste de personnes qualifiées que les responsables de l’AIE pourront prendre en considération dans le cadre de futurs recrutements à l’Agence. Les personnes inscrites sur cette liste à l’issue de ce processus de sélection pourront être invitées à des entretiens ultérieurs destinés à permettre l’évaluation de l’adéquation des profils avec des besoins spécifiques. Ces entretiens seront fonction de la spécialisation/du domaine d’intérêt des personnes concernées. Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus seront pourvues dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard le 14 septembre 2026 à 23h59 (heure de Paris). Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Le salaire mensuel minimum s’élève à 6 008 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, la rémunération globale étant exonérée d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, Règlement et Instructions applicables aux agents de l’Organisation. Veuillez noter que tout

item.title: (Associate) Investment Officer, Manufacturing, Agribusiness and Services, LAC Region
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, is the largest global development institution focused on the private sector in emerging markets. We work in more than 100 countries, using our capital, expertise, and influence to create markets and opportunities in developing countries. In fiscal year 2025, IFC committed a record $71.7 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries, leveraging private sector solutions, and mobilizing private capital to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. Manufacturing, Agribusiness and Services (MAS) is one of IFC's key industry groups, responsible for a significant portion of IFC's business volume, profitability, and development impact. MAS invests across a diverse range of sectors, including agribusiness, forestry, manufacturing, chemicals, healthcare, education, tourism, property, retail, and other industries, delivering both investment and advisory services through IFC's global network. The MAS Latin America and the Caribbean (MAS LAC) team is seeking a qualified and experienced Associate Investment Officer, or Investment Officer to originate, structure, execute, and supervise investment projects across the region. The selected candidate will play a key role in business development and portfolio management, including restructurings, reschedulings, capital increases, and equity supervision. The candidate should have a demonstrated track record of leading complex investment transactions from origination through commitment and portfolio supervision, preferably across multiple MAS sectors. The position will be based in Guatemala City, Guatemala or San José, Costa Rica. The final duty station and title will be determined based on business needs. Duties and Accountabilities Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to: • Support or Lead business development efforts across MAS in the country. • Together with the Central America and Caribbean MAS Hub Lead and the WBG country team, lead the scoping and identification process of priority companies to target as IFC clients in the country, considering the strategic areas of focus for MAS in the country. • Actively develop a local network with target companies, financial institutions, financial advisors, and credit agencies in the country. • Lead transaction execution and portfolio management activities across the MAS LAC region. • Evaluate, structure, negotiate, and close new investment transactions, portfolio restructurings, reschedulings, capital increases, equity sales, and other portfolio management activities. • Develop innovative and appropriate financial structures for complex transactions. • Lead or participate in negotiations, leveraging strong financial expertise and influencing skills to achieve successful outcomes. • Work independently and collaborate with senior colleagues to develop a strong pipeline of high-quality investment opportunities in the countries. • Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, sponsors, financial institutions, private sector partners, and multilateral organizations to originate new investment opportunities. • Mentor and coach junior investment staff on all aspects of investment processing, portfolio management, and client engagement. • Support dissemination of best practices within the team. • Collaborate closely with Advisory, Environmental Social, Legal, Treasury, and other internal partners to deliver integrated client solutions, manage transaction risks, and maximize development impact. • Collaborate closely with the Upstream team to support market creation efforts and develop a robust pipeline of future investment opportunities. • Collaborate on the preparation of Country Private Sector Diagnostics (CPSD), Country Partnership Framework (CPF), Senior Management Briefs, Country Climate and Development Reports (CCDR), etc. • Engage with World Bank colleagues on MAS-related issues. • Build effective working relationships across multidisciplinary teams and influence internal and external stakeholders to achieve successful transaction outcomes.

item.title: E T Consultant (Regional Engagement Analyst )
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital support for global and country-specific products, supports systems aligned with the new Country Engagement model, and provides geospatial solutions to improve spatial visibility and impact tracking. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. The unit’s geospatial portfolio supports operational teams in applying location-based insights, mapping, imagery, and related digital tools to strengthen project design, implementation, monitoring, and communication. The Regional Engagement Analyst serves as a focal point for the ITSCE Solutions. The incumbent supports stakeholder engagement, solution awareness, and adoption across both portfolios, helping country teams, regional teams, and Global Practices identify opportunities where technology, geospatial capabilities, and advisory services can address operational challenges and support development outcomes. Working closely with management, product owners, geospatial specialists, architects, and advisory teams, the coordinator will facilitate engagement, connect stakeholders with relevant expertise and solutions, and help make the ITSCE geospatial portfolio visible, accessible, and relevant across regional, country, and local engagements. The role does not require technical implementation of geospatial solutions but does require sufficient familiarity with available products and geospatial concepts to identify use cases, communicate value propositions, and support adoption. Specific Responsibilities Regional Operations Studio • Serve as the primary point of contact for the Regional Operations Studio and act as an ambassador for ITSOE products, advisory services, and innovation initiatives. • Coordinate Studio activities, ensuring country teams are welcomed, oriented, and connected to appropriate ITSOE products, advisory services, and subject matter experts. • Facilitate workshops, demonstrations, co-design sessions, and engagement activities involving country teams, OPCS, and ITSOE specialists. • Capture and qualify operational needs, technology challenges, and business opportunities and connect stakeholders to the appropriate product, service, or advisory pathway. • Lead outreach, communications, and stakeholder engagement activities to expand awareness, participation, and adoption of the Regional Operations Studio. • Build and maintain relationships with country teams, Regional teams, Global Practices, OPCS, and other stakeholders to strengthen regional engagement and utilization of ITSOE services. • Monitor engagement outcomes and stakeholder feedback to continuously improve the Studio experience and operational impact. Geospatial Solutions Engagement and Adoption • Act as a regional engagement and promotion focal point for the ITSCE Geospatial Solutions portfolio, working closely with product owners and geospatial specialists to identify and advance opportunities with country teams, Regional teams, and Global Practices. • Promote awareness and adoption of geospatial products, services, and advisory capabilities through demonstrations, clinics, roadshows, and targeted outreach activities. • Maintain working knowledge of the ITSCE geospatial portfolio, including project geo-tagging, mapping solutions, imagery-enabled applications, and digital twin use cases, and communicate their operational value in accessible language. • Identify operational challenges that may benefit from geospatial approaches and connect stakeholders with the appropriate product owners, advisors, and technical specialists. • Support the development of presentations, communication materials, demonstrations, and map-based narratives that showcase how geospatial insights can strengthen project design, implementation, monitoring, and decision-making.

item.title: E T Consultant (Associate Platform Engineer)
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? The World Bank Group is a unique global partnership of five institutions driven by a bold vision to create a world free of poverty on a livable planet. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, we help solve the world’s greatest development challenges. When you join the World Bank Group, you become part of a dynamic, diverse organization with 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide. We work with public and private sector partners, invest in groundbreaking projects, and use data, research, and technology to bring tangible and transformative change around the globe. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org . ITS Vice Presidency Context The Information and Technology Solutions (ITS) Vice Presidential Unit (VPU) enables the World Bank Group to achieve its mission of ending extreme poverty and boost shared prosperity on a livable planet by delivering transformative information and technologies to its staff working in over 150+ locations. For more information on ITS, see this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?reload=9 v=VTFGffa1Y7w Unit Context The ITS Country Engagement unit (ITSCE) delivers digital support for global and country-specific products, supports systems aligned with the new Country Engagement model, and provides geospatial solutions for geo-tagging of projects to improve spatial visibility and impact tracking. It also drives the delivery of AI-powered business solutions to support business priorities and accelerate data-driven decision-making across the institution. Department Context ITS Operations and Country Engagement Department (ITSOE) delivers innovative products and services to frontline staff working on over 6,000 projects throughout every Region and Global Practice. Our teams support and enable Bank priorities, boost operations efficiency and effectiveness, and facilitate Operational knowledge discovery. Our delivery model leverages global expertise, design and architecture, leading technology, and robust processes to deliver business solutions that ensure value for money. The Associate Platform Engineer will support the design, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of platform engineering and DevSecOps capabilities within the Geospatial Solutions portfolio. Working as the primary DevSecOps resource embedded within the Geospatial Solutions Agile Release Train (ART), the incumbent will be responsible for release management, deployment automation, security remediation, platform operations, and cloud-based solution delivery. The role will support the development and maintenance of scalable, secure, and reliable delivery platforms through the implementation of CI/CD pipelines, Azure DevOps administration, cloud technologies, and operational best practices. The Platform Engineer will collaborate closely with software engineers, product owners, architects, security teams, and business stakeholders to ensure efficient software delivery, operational excellence, compliance with organizational requirements, and continuous improvement across the geospatial solutions ecosystem. Specific Responsibilities • Manage end-to-end release management activities for the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, overseeing the deployment, promotion, and validation of applications and services across development, testing, and production environments. • Design, implement, maintain, and optimize Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines to automate build, testing, security scanning, and deployment processes, enabling reliable, efficient, and secure software releases. • Analyze, identify, and remediate security vulnerabilities across applications, platforms, and environments within the Geospatial Solutions portfolio, supporting secure software delivery and compliance with organizational security requirements. • Administer and maintain Azure DevOps services, including repositories, boards, pipelines, release processes, access controls, and environment management to support Agile software delivery. • Support the deployment, operation, and maintenance of cloud-based solutions and infrastructure across Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS) environments. • Support containerized application deployments using Docker and related platform technologies to improve scalability, consistency, and operational efficiency. • Lead and support OIS accreditation activities for the Unified Geospatial Platform, Geospatial Sector Solutions, and Geospatial Data Integrations with the Development Data Hub (DDH) and Data360 (D360), ensuring alignment with corporate security, architecture, and compliance requirements. • Support Program Increment (PI) Planning, SAFe Agile ceremonies, and Agile Release Train (ART) activities in coordination with the Release Train Engineer (RTE), contributing to cross-team planning, dependency management, and delivery alignment. • Serve as the primary DevSecOps resource supporting the Geospatial Solutions Agile Release Train (ART), providing technical guidance, operational support, and release coordination across multiple geospatial solution teams. • Collaborate with software engineers, architects, product owners, and platform teams to support solution delivery, operational readiness, and continuous improvement initiatives. • Monitor and troubleshoot deployment processes, DevSecOps workflows, and platform configurations to maintain system reliability, availability, and operational performance. • Analyze and maintain technical documentation for release management processes, CI/CD pipelines, security controls, deployment procedures, operational standards, and accreditation activities.
