Risk Issue Management • Monitor social media conversations, digital platforms, and online communities to identify emerging issues, stakeholder sentiment, reputational risks, and opportunities related to regional priorities and reform initiatives. • Analyze online sentiment and digital narratives to provide timely insights that support communications around policy reforms, implementation challenges, and priority regional initiatives. • Prepare regular social media listening reports and digital insights summaries highlighting emerging narratives, influential voices, stakeholder concerns, and opportunities for proactive engagement. • Support communications around priority reforms by providing timely digital insights that help shape messaging, stakeholder engagement, and advocacy approaches. • Support rapid digital communications during major announcements, reform milestones, emerging issues, or high-profile events by coordinating timely publication of approved content and monitoring audience response. • Coordinate with regional, country, and corporate communications colleagues to ensure digital listening informs advocacy campaigns, stakeholder engagement, and issue management across the region.

Its mission is to deliver world-class communications and marketing leadership—driving clarity, creativity, innovation, and impact across every audience and channel. Through compelling storytelling, global brand stewardship, and data-driven engagement, the team advances the Bank Group’s vision of creating a world free of poverty on a livable planet. Together, we shape the institution’s voice, strengthen trust and reputation, and connect the World Bank Group’s work to people and partners around the world. The Senior External Affairs Officer plays a strategic role in strengthening narrative discipline and advancing a coherent, institution-wide communications approach across the World Bank Group. The position leads the Messaging team, providing strategic direction, oversight, and leadership while driving the development and implementation of the Bank Group’s corporate narrative and strategic priorities. Working closely with the Internal and Executive Communications Manager, Director of Communications and Marketing, and communications colleagues across the WBG, this role provides strategic counsel on messaging, storytelling, and communications priorities. Serving as a trusted thought partner and connector across teams, the position helps align Senior Leadership communications, identify high-impact storytelling opportunities, and strengthen consistency of voice across major institutional moments and priority initiatives. Key Responsibilities Narrative Strategy and Corporate Storytelling • Lead and manage the CERCM Messaging team, providing strategic direction, oversight, and leadership to ensure the development and delivery of clear, consistent, and impactful corporate messaging across the World Bank Group. • Help shape and reinforce the World Bank Group’s corporate narrative, ensuring communications consistently reflect institutional priorities and leadership objectives. • Champion narrative discipline across communications activities, ensuring messaging, stories, and leadership communications reinforce a consistent institutional narrative. • Identify and elevate high-impact stories that showcase the World Bank Group’s work across regions, sectors, and institutions. • Monitor emerging issues and external trends to identify opportunities and risks that inform communications strategy and narrative development. Strategic Communications Counsel • Serve as a strategic advisor to CER communications teams, providing guidance on messaging, positioning, and storytelling for high-profile initiatives and complex issues. • Review and provide strategic input on high-profile communications products to ensure consistency with the World Bank Group’s narrative, voice, and strategic priorities. • Act as a thought partner to CER leadership, connecting emerging themes, institutional priorities, and external developments into cohesive communications strategies. • Contribute to the continuous improvement of communications processes, templates, and playbooks that strengthen narrative consistency and strategic planning. Senior Leadership Communications • Liaise with Senior Leadership Team communications colleagues across the Bank Group to ensure coordinated messaging and alignment around institutional priorities. • Support communications planning for select leadership engagements, speeches, and major institutional moments, translating leadership priorities into clear messaging and communications products. • Lead select executive writing assignments, including speeches, op-eds, thought leadership pieces, and strategic messaging for senior leadership. • Coordinate across communications, operational, and regional teams to ensure narrative coherence and effective delivery. Cross-Institution Collaboration • Convene and connect communications colleagues across CER and the wider World Bank Group to identify shared storytelling opportunities, align messaging, and strengthen collaboration across teams. Special Projects and Other Tasks • Serve as a trusted strategic partner on high-priority projects requiring senior-level judgment, coordination, and execution. • Support strategic communications initiatives assigned by the Internal and Executive Communications Manager and the Director of Communications and Marketing.

Communications and External Affairs The Communications and External Affairs Officer, a key member of the Western and Central Africa Communications and External Affairs team, will be based in the Nouakchott, Mauritania Country Office. The position supports the design and delivery of stakeholder engagement, communications, advocacy, and reputational risk management activities that advance the World Bank Group's priorities in Mauritania. The position contributes to delivery across CER's four business lines: Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Business Marketing, Advocacy Campaigns, and Risk Issue Management. The role requires sound judgment, political awareness, strong communications skills, and the ability to build relationships, identify opportunities and risks, and deliver high-quality external affairs support. Working closely with country and regional management, operational teams, and colleagues across IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, the External Affairs Officer helps advance a coordinated One World Bank Group approach to stakeholder engagement and communications across the Senegal and Mauritania Country Management Unit (CMU). Responsibilities 1. Stakeholder Engagement • Build and sustain trusted relationships with government counterparts, development partners, private sector, media, academia, youth, and civil society to deepen understanding of the WBG’s role and value. • Spearhead strategic partnerships that drive impact for our work. • Map and maintain an active network of influencers and validators who can help communicate WBG priorities and results. • Advise the Country Manager [GC1.1]as well as operational teams on stakeholder engagement approaches that enhance ownership, transparency, and results. • Support proactive two-way communications by gathering insights from the ground and feeding them into operational planning and narrative development. • Lead or contribute to outreach programs and dialogues that promote open and informed discussion of reform challenges and opportunities. • Manage media relations and broaden outreach opportunities with media based in the CMU. 2. Strategic Business Marketing • Showcase the WBG’s integrated offer by linking public policy reforms to private capital mobilization and knowledge services. • Develop and implement communication strategies that highlight results, demonstrate the impact of WBG support, and help generate demand for future engagement. • Position the CMU country program as part of a broader regional story of resilience, private-sector–led growth, and regional integration. • Identify and promote success stories, case studies, and thought leadership products that illustrate how WBG support is transforming key sectors. • Develop and disseminate results stories and visuals through WBG and partner digital platforms to reinforce credibility and relevance. 3. Advocacy and Campaigns • Contribute to regional and global advocacy efforts by localizing messages and providing examples from the CMU. • Lead or support the rollout of country-specific campaigns that mobilize client and partner networks around reforms or flagship programs. • Design and deliver communications plans for major project or knowledge launches, ensuring consistent messaging across all channels and exercising selectivity. • Draft and edit communications materials, including press releases, speeches, talking points, and social media content. • Work with technical teams to simplify complex concepts and translate them into compelling, actionable narratives. 4. Corporate Coordination and Innovation • Serve as an integral member of the regional communications network, contributing to regional priorities, campaigns, and storytelling initiatives. • Ensure close collaboration with IFC and MIGA counterparts to present a unified WBG narrative and leverage cross-institutional opportunities. • Champion innovative, data-driven communication approaches—short-form video, digital storytelling, influencer engagement, and visual explainers—to increase reach and impact. • Serve as an integrated member of the WBG-wide Communication Network, actively engaging in professional development opportunities and supporting key corporate priorities.

The position contributes to advancing the World Bank Group's regional stakeholder engagement agenda through delivery across CER's four business lines: Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Business Marketing, Advocacy Campaigns, and Risk Issue Management. Senior Communication and External Relations Officer The WBG is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Senior Communications and External Affairs Officer based in Buenos Aires, Argentina. The position supports the Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay country programs and combines strategic advisory responsibilities with hands-on delivery. The successful candidate will serve as a core member of the Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay communications team and work in close partnership with the communications leads based in Asunción, Paraguay, and Montevideo, Uruguay. The position contributes across CER’s four business lines: Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Business Marketing, Advocacy Campaigns, and Risk Issue Management. The role requires sound judgment, political awareness, excellent communications and stakeholder engagement skills, and the ability to build trusted relationships, identify opportunities and risks, and translate complex development issues into compelling narratives that demonstrate impact and advance country priorities. Working closely with country and regional management, operational teams, and colleagues across IBRD, IFC, and MIGA, the Senior Communications and External Affairs Officer will lead the development and delivery of integrated communications, stakeholder engagement, and risk management strategies for Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, while contributing to a coordinated One World Bank Group approach across the three country programs. Success in the role requires a highly collaborative working style and the ability to operate effectively in a matrixed environment, partnering across institutions and disciplines to support the World Bank Group’s development and private sector objectives. Responsibilities 1. Stakeholder Engagement • Lead the design and execution of a strategic stakeholder engagement plan that deepens relationships across government, private sector, development partners, civil society, academia, media, and youth. • Build high-level partnerships that expand WBG influence and support reform momentum. • Provide authoritative advice to the Division and Regional Directors and operational teams on engagement strategies, political dynamics, and stakeholder risks. • Serve as the senior liaison with national and subnational organizations, strengthening trust and enhancing the visibility of WBG programs. • Convene dialogues and public forums that support policy discussions and amplify reform solutions. • Lead proactive two-way communications, capturing insights and feeding them back into country strategy, operations, and narratives. • Proactively identify, assess, and elevate stakeholder-driven issues with the potential to cause reputational risk for the World Bank Group. 2. Strategic Business Marketing • Position the WBG as a strategic partner in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay articulating how the integrated public-private WBG helps to accelerate reforms and maximize development impact. • Develop high-impact communications strategies that shape country and regional narratives around jobs, private-sector-led growth, resilience, energy security, and institutional reform. • Develop and manage a marketing suite of products including strong client testimonials to inform outreach to prospects (governments, companies) and partners; success stories; reform overviews showing progress; strategic business narratives; case studies; thought-leadership products • Identify and elevate flagship projects, reform milestones, and success stories that demonstrate results and generate demand for WBG engagement. • Lead engagement with communications counterparts in WBG private sector arms (IFC and MIGA) to highlight private capital mobilization and private-sector solutions messages in the country program. 3. Advocacy and Campaigns • Lead the design and rollout of high-visibility advocacy campaigns that mobilize stakeholders around reform priorities and WBG-supported initiatives in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. • Coordinate participation in regional and global advocacy efforts by localizing messages and providing examples from Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. • Ensure consistent, selective, and strategically targeted messaging across all channels. • Oversee production of speeches, op-eds, press releases, talking points, and multimedia content with high standards of clarity and quality in relevant languages. • Translate complex policy and technical concepts into compelling, accessible narratives for diverse audiences. • Strengthen the country office’s capacity to deliver impactful campaigns and digital storytelling. 4. Risk and Issue Management • Anticipate, identify, and assess emerging political or reputational risks and proactively manage issues that may affect WBG engagement in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. • Provide timely, senior-level advice to the Division and Regional Directors, CER management, and regional leadership on risk exposure, positioning, and response options. • Maintain and contribute to reputational risk reports, ensure heatmap entries are up to date. Develop issue notes, scenario plans, and other materials as needed. • Lead mitigation strategies for sensitive operations and high-profile issues and inspection panel cases, ensuring coordinated institutional responses. • Lead mitigation and response strategies for sensitive operations, high profile issues, and Inspection Panel cases, ensuring coordinated, institutionally aligned actions across WBG and CER teams. • Serve as the primary point of contact with CER’s regional and corporate risk teams to ensure alignment, speed, and consistency of responses. • Provide analysis on political developments that may have implications for WBG engagement. • Guide media engagement and manage high-stakes inquiries with discretion and sound judgment. • Review key corporate documents for messaging, stakeholder issues, and reputational risk and provide written comments if needed. 5. Corporate Coordination and Innovation • Lead efforts towards a unified WBG narrative and leverage cross-institutional opportunities, by ensuring that both public and private perspectives/impact are reflected. Maintain equal and solid understanding of IBRD, IDA, IFC and MIGA operations in team under supervision, if any. • Work closely with other communications staff supporting the county team to jointly manage priorities, coordinate messaging, share workload, and ensure consistent delivery across countries and business lines. • Drive innovation in communications through creative approaches—such as content partnerships, influencer engagement, dissemination via key partner and client channels, third-party expert voices, digital storytelling, and data-driven communications—to amplify strategic campaigns. • Represent the region in global CER initiatives, contributing to professional development, best practices, and WBG-wide priorities. • Mentor—and sometimes supervise —junior staff and contribute to strengthening capacity across the regional communications network. • Support CER management efforts to drive integration of communications function across WBG through active team collaboration, delivery against joint objectives, implementation of joint systems and processes.

item.title: Senior Communications & External Affairs Officer
item.description: The World Bank Group (WBG) is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries. It is a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions for the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit www.worldbank.org. Communications and External Relations (CER) The mission of Communications and External Relations (CER) is to help deliver financial and political support for the World Bank Group, strengthen the Bank Group’s role as a global thought leader in development by enhancing and safeguarding its reputation, and supporting operational teams to achieve country outcomes. CER manages corporate communications and global engagement with key stakeholders, including media, civil society, foundations, private sector, donor countries, and international organizations, as well as employee engagement. CER also manages strategic communications for the World Bank Group’s Regions and technical units and leads the management of reputation risk. Regional Context The World Bank Group serves 33 client countries across Latin America and the Caribbean, a highly diverse region ranging from sophisticated middle-income economies to IDA countries, small Caribbean states, and one fragile state, all facing three interrelated challenges: low growth and productivity, insufficient quality jobs, and high vulnerability to shocks. Growth has returned to its pre-pandemic low trajectory, inequality remains among the highest in the world, and limited human capital continues to constrain opportunity and productivity. Although unemployment appears moderate, the deeper challenge is job quality, with weak labor earnings, high informality, infrastructure gaps, skills shortages, restrictive regulatory environments, limited access to finance, shallow capital markets, and low private investment holding back the creation of better jobs. At the same time, the region remains highly exposed to climate-related disasters and natural hazards, particularly in Central America and the Caribbean, where hurricanes, droughts, storms, and floods have significant economic and social impacts. In response, LCR is advancing a selective and coordinated One World Bank Group approach, leveraging the complementary strengths of IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, and working with regional partners to support infrastructure, human capital, business-enabling reforms, private capital mobilization, productive sectors, and resilience to shocks. Senior Communications External Affairs Officer The Senior Communications External Affairs Officer is a key member of the Latin America Communications and External Affairs team and will be based in São Paulo, Brazil. The position supports the Brazil country program and serves as a strategic advisor to country and regional management on stakeholder engagement, communications, advocacy, and reputational risk management. While the role covers the full range of responsibilities expected of a senior communications and external affairs officer, it will have a particular focus on private sector engagement and communications support for IFC’s program in Brazil. This includes helping position the World Bank Group’s public-private solutions, strengthening engagement with private sector stakeholders, and supporting communications around IFC priorities, investments, partnerships, and broader private capital mobilization efforts. The role is central to advancing the World Bank Group’s external affairs agenda in Brazil, driving delivery across CER’s four business lines: Stakeholder Engagement, Strategic Business Marketing, Advocacy Campaigns, and Risk Issue Management. It requires strong strategic judgment, political awareness, business acumen, and the ability to anticipate risks, influence stakeholders, shape narratives, and mobilize support for development priorities. Working closely with country and regional management, operational teams, and colleagues across IBRD, IFC, and MIGA, the Senior Communications External Affairs Officer helps advance a coordinated One World Bank Group approach across the Brazil portfolio. The position combines strategic advisory responsibilities with hands-on delivery and is expected to lead complex assignments, support priority country initiatives, and contribute directly to execution across the country program, with a particular emphasis on private sector-facing initiatives and IFC engagement. The successful candidate will serve as a core member of the Brazil communications team and work in close partnership with the Senior Communications and External Affairs Officer based in Brasília, who also supports the CMU. The position requires a highly collaborative working style and the ability to operate effectively in a matrixed environment where priorities, communications products, and stakeholder engagement activities are jointly developed and delivered across IBRD, IFC, MIGA, and CER. Key Responsibilities 1. Stakeholder Engagement • Lead stakeholder engagement strategies that advance World Bank Group priorities, support country outcomes, and strengthen the institution's influence in Brazil. • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including national and subnational government officials, development partners, private sector leaders, civil society organizations, media, academia, youth, and other influential actors. • Lead stakeholder intelligence efforts, including stakeholder mapping, analysis, and monitoring of actors, coalitions, and trends that may affect World Bank Group priorities, reform efforts, or reputation. • Advise the Country Director(s)/Manager(s), regional management, and operational teams on stakeholder dynamics, political economy considerations, coalition-building opportunities, and engagement approaches. • Ensure stakeholder insights and external perspectives are incorporated into country strategies, operations, communications strategies, advocacy efforts, and risk management. • Convene and support dialogues, consultations, and public forums that advance policy discussions, amplify reform solutions, and strengthen understanding of World Bank Group priorities. • Proactively identify, assess, and elevate stakeholder-driven issues with the potential to affect World Bank Group operations, stakeholder relationships, or reputation. 2. Strategic Business Marketing • Position the World Bank Group as a trusted development partner in Brazil by articulating the value of integrated public-private solutions and the One World Bank Group approach. • Develop strategic narratives, engagement approaches, and communications products that support country and regional priorities, operational objectives, and client engagement. • Identify and elevate flagship operations, reform milestones, knowledge products, client testimonials, and success stories that demonstrate impact and generate demand for World Bank Group engagement. • Identify opportunities to strengthen visibility and understanding of the World Bank Group's work among government, investors, private sector partners, foundations, and development stakeholders. • Work closely with communications counterparts across IFC and MIGA to highlight private capital mobilization, private sector solutions, and the value of integrated World Bank Group engagement in the country program. 3. Advocacy Campaigns • Lead advocacy and communications campaigns that support development priorities, reform efforts, and institutional objectives in Brazil. • Develop compelling messaging and narratives that translate complex development issues into clear, accessible, and persuasive communications for local and regional audiences. • Coordinate country contributions to corporate, global, and regional campaigns, adapting messages and approaches to the Brazil context. • Oversee the development of speeches, op-eds, press releases, talking points, digital content, multimedia products, and other communications materials for senior management and key stakeholders. • Help ensure consistent, targeted, and effective messaging across communications, stakeholder engagement, digital, and media channels. • Strengthen the country office's capacity to deliver impactful campaigns, digital storytelling, and effective engagement with stakeholders. 4. Risk Issue Management • Serve as a senior advisor on reputational risk and issue management, helping country and regional management anticipate, assess, and respond to developments that could affect World Bank Group operations, stakeholder relationships, or reputation in Brazil. • Lead or coordinate risk assessments, stakeholder analyses, issue management efforts, and mitigation strategies for sensitive operations, reforms, Inspection Panel cases, and institutional priorities. • Advise the Country Director(s)/Manager(s), CER management, regional leadership, and operational teams on positioning, stakeholder considerations, and communications approaches related to complex or high-profile issues. • Develop issue briefs, risk assessments, scenario plans, leadership briefing materials, and response strategies to support informed decision-making. • Monitor political, economic, and social developments and assess their implications for World Bank Group operations, reform efforts, stakeholder relationships, and institutional reputation. • Guide media engagement and manage high-stakes inquiries with discretion and sound judgment. • Review key corporate documents and operational materials, as needed, for messaging, stakeholder issues, and reputational risk. • Serve as a primary point of contact with CER's regional and corporate risk teams to ensure alignment, speed, and consistency of responses. 5. item.title: (Associate) Industry Specialist – Transport and Logistics
item.description: Build a career with impact. Working at the World Bank Group (WBG) provides a unique opportunity to help countries solve their greatest development challenges. As one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries, the WBG is a unique partnership of five global institutions dedicated to ending poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, the WBG works with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. The Knowledge Bank’s Transport and Logistics Solutions and Impact team is responsible for ensuring that the right mix of best practice, investment and advisory solutions are made available to public and private sector clients and WBG operational teams in the Transport and Logistics sectors. The team is looking to recruit an (Associate) Industry Specialist (AIS) covering the Transport and Logistics sectors. The AIS will provide knowledge and criteria regarding business feasibility, assessment or diagnosis of the assigned projects. Also involved in the supervision of WBG’s ongoing transport investments along with other Industry Specialist colleagues from the Transport and Logistics Group. The AIS will bridge operational experience with knowledge management, ensuring that lessons learned and innovative solutions are captured and shared across the World Bank Group and its clients. The selected candidate will be based in Washington DC and will report to the Manager for Transport and Logistics Solutions and Impact. The position will have a global focus and some travel may be required. Duties and Accountabilities: Among other duties, the (Associate) Industry Specialist will provide support to investment or advisory activities by evaluating transport projects, providing sector advice and guidance, and monitoring transport portfolio. More specifically: • Upstream-related activities: o Identify opportunities for advisory services to clients at various stages of project development, including early-stage business development and pipeline creation. o Support the development of the sector strategy and the creation of new business opportunities. o Advise Transport and Logistics Policy and Regulation Unit and other investment teams within the WBG in early stage assessment of investment proposals from a technical, managerial, commercial and development impact perspective. • Investment-related activities: o Apply sector knowledge in appraising new investment proposals across transport and logistics subsectors (ports, roads, railways, urban transit, airports, transportation logistics warehousing, shipping and barging, airlines, electric mobility), providing independent assessment of project feasibility, risk and impact, including supporting senior specialists within the Knowledge Bank Transport and Logistics Group in such appraisals. o Liaise with client’s technical staff, project engineers, consultants and lenders’ engineers as needed. o Review and analyze major contracts, including EPC, O M, and Concession agreements. o Develop market assessments, revenue projections, cost benchmarks, and operational parameters to inform financial models prepared by investment teams. o Draft Terms of Reference, hire and supervise technical and market consultants as necessary. o Prepare timely project appraisal reports alone or collaborating with other specialists, including risk assessment, mitigation measures and impact evaluation. • Portfolio-related activities: o Provide technical supervision of WBG’s portfolio of transport sector investments, including field inspection as necessary. o Identify and assist in resolving operational weaknesses and take notes of lessons learned and best practices to apply on future projects. • Other activities: o Support other specialists in their duties when necessary. o Maintain an active WBG network that provides visibility of WBG activities relevant to the sector, and coordinate activities as appropriate. o Keep updated on sectoral and industry news, trends, related technology developments and cost references. o Develop industry knowledge to share within WBG and with external clients as part of WBG’s knowledge management programs in a permanent format (lessons learnt, industry trends, basic technical knowledge, benchmarking, etc.) o Collaborate with operational teams of the Transport and Logistics Policy and Regulation Unit and with other teams of the WBG to integrate knowledge into project design and implementation.

Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The Statistics and Data Directorate (SDD) ( www.oecd.org/sdd ) provides statistics and data on a comparable basis and from a variety of sources to analysts, policy makers and members of civil society. SDD also develops new metrics and innovative digital tools to address emerging policy issues, leads the development of international statistical standards, advances statistical methodology and co-ordinates statistical and data-related activities within the Organisation and with other international organisations. The Directorate currently employs more than 90 staff members who support statistical work across a broad range of policy areas . Within SDD, the Trade and Productivity Statistics Division (TPS) oversees the development and dissemination of productivity, prices, purchasing power parities (PPPs), labour, business and international trade statistics and undertakes studies related to measurement in these fields. SDD/TPS is looking for a Statistician to contribute to its work programme on PPPs and other topics covered by the Division. The successful candidate will have advanced skills in applying statistical and econometric techniques, excellent programming skills, and previous experience in research and analytical activities. Proven ability to handle large datasets, as well as good drafting skills would be an advantage. S/he will be able to work independently but also collaborate with other team members. The successful candidate will report to the Head of the Prices and Productivity Statistics Section in TPS. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main Responsibilities Statistical work, economic research and drafting Contribute to the production (i.e. calculation, survey management and validation, data checks, etc.) of PPPs and related indicators, such as comparative price levels, for countries under the responsibility of the OECD in the joint Eurostat-OECD programme and all the associated documentation, briefing materials etc. Contribute to blog posts or short papers to disseminate and promote the OECD’s work on PPPs. Contribute to the analytical and research activities of the Division and to the production of working papers and publications related to measurement issues. Keep abreast of research on PPPs and relevant methodological developments. Assist with the maintenance of core databases, as needed. Support the continuous improvement and modernisation of PPP update processes and data infrastructure, including through the expansion and maintenance of related documentation. Communication, liaison and representation Develop good working relationships with colleagues across the OECD and other relevant OECD directorates to ensure co-ordination on work associated with the work programme on PPP statistics and other statistics covered by the Division. Establish contacts with data producers in national statistical offices, national administrations and other international organisations, and with academics in the wider research community working on related topics. Participate in expert meetings and workshops related to productivity measurement and analysis, and prepare and present research papers to a wide array of audiences. Provide overall support to the Head of the Section and undertake other tasks as required. item.description: {"id":"744000142881829","name":"Statisticien(ne) - Prix et parités de pouvoir d’achat","uuid":"b6b63195-d544-4d72-9848-28e2c24e7ed5","jobId":"6192243d-bcde-4eb4-86d3-4c4d99ea7853","jobAdId":"057f20a0-4e30-4b17-9fcb-f8c4f8acaceb","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3332C","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":true,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001187","valueLabel":"SDD"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL3","valueLabel":"PAL3"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-11T13:43:52.111Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000142881829-statisticien-ne-prix-et-parites-de-pouvoir-d-achat","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000142881829-statisticien-ne-prix-et-parites-de-pouvoir-d-achat?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/b6b63195-d544-4d72-9848-28e2c24e7ed5?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. La Direction des statistiques et des données (SDD) ( www.oecd.org/fr/sdd/ ) produit, à l’intention des analystes, des responsables de l’action publique et des membres de la société civile, des statistiques et des données qui reposent sur des sources diverses et permettent d’établir des comparaisons. SDD met au point de nouveaux indicateurs et des outils numériques innovants pour traiter les problématiques émergentes, pilote l’élaboration de normes statistiques internationales, fait progresser la méthodologie statistique et coordonne, au sein de l’Organisation et avec d’autres organisations internationales, les activités portant sur les statistiques et les données. La Direction emploie actuellement plus de 90 agents qui concourent aux travaux statistiques menés dans un large éventail de domaines de l’action publique . Au sein de SDD, la Division des statistiques du commerce et de la productivité (TPS) supervise l’élaboration et la diffusion de statistiques sur la productivité, les prix, les parités de pouvoir d’achat (PPA), le travail, les entreprises et le commerce international. Elle mène également des études sur la mesure dans ces domaines. SDD/TPS est à la recherche d’un ou d’une statisticien(ne) qui contribuera à l’exécution de son programme de travail sur les PPA et d’autres thèmes couverts par la Division. La personne retenue sera experte dans l’application des techniques statistiques et économétriques ainsi que dans la programmation, et aura une expérience préalable des activités de recherche et d’analyse. Une aptitude avérée à traiter de grands ensembles de données ainsi qu’une bonne compétence rédactionnelle seraient un atout. Elle saura faire preuve d’autonomie, mais aussi collaborer avec d’autres membres de l’équipe. Le/La candidat(e) retenu(e) travaillera sous la direction du Chef de la Section des statistiques de la productivité, des prix et des PPA de TPS. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Effectuer des travaux statistiques, des travaux de recherche économique et de rédaction. Contribuer à la production (calcul, gestion et validation des enquêtes, vérification de données, etc.) de PPA et d’indicateurs connexes, comme des niveaux de prix comparatifs, pour les pays relevant du périmètre d’activité de l’OCDE dans le cadre du programme conjoint Eurostat-OCDE, ainsi que de documents, supports d’information, etc. associés. Contribuer à la rédaction de billets de blogs ou de courtes notes permettant de diffuser et de promouvoir les travaux de l’OCDE sur les PPA. Apporter sa contribution aux activités d’analyse et de recherche menées au sein de la Division ainsi qu’à la production de documents de travail et de publications traitant de questions métrologiques. Se tenir informé(e) de l’état de la recherche sur les PPA et des évolutions méthodologiques pertinentes. Aider à l’entretien des principales bases de données, en tant que de besoin. Contribuer à l’amélioration et à la modernisation continues des procédures d’actualisation des PPA et des infrastructures de données, notamment en assurant le développement et la maintenance des documents connexes. Communication, liaison et représentation Nouer de bonnes relations de travail avec des collègues dans l’ensemble de l’Organisation et d’autres directions de l’OCDE de façon à assurer la coordination des travaux associés au programme de travail sur les statistiques des PPA et d’autres données statistiques relevant de la Division. Prendre contact avec des responsables de la production de données au sein des offices statistiques nationaux, des administrations nationales et d’autres organisations internationales, ainsi qu’avec des acteurs universitaires du monde de la recherche travaillant sur des questions connexes. Participer à des réunions et ateliers d’experts en lien avec la mesure et l’analyse de la productivité, et préparer et y présenter des rapports de recherche destinés à un large éventail de publics. Assister le Chef de la Section et mener à bien d’autres tâches en fonction des besoins. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Un diplôme universitaire de niveau supérieur ou équivalent en statistique, en économie ou en économétrie, assorti de bases solides en analyse quantitative et en statistique. Expérience professionnelle Au moins deux ans d’expérience professionnelle du travail sur les statistiques économiques ; une expérience du travail sur les statistiques des prix et les PPA serait un atout décisif. Expérience de la production, de l’entretien et de l’assurance qualité des indicateurs statistiques. Une connaissance des outils de visualisation de données serait un avantage. Expérience antérieure des activités de recherche et d’analyse ; une expérience de l’analyse quantitative, y compris une solide connaissance des concepts macroéconomiques, serait un atout. D’excellentes compétences du traitement de grands ensembles de données seraient un avantage. De bonnes compétences rédactionnelles constitueraient un avantage. L’expérience de la préparation de documents de recherche acquise au sein d’établissements universitaires et d’une organisation internationale constituerait un atout. Outils Connaissance approfondie de MS Excel. La connaissance de VBA constituerait un atout. Excellentes compétences de programmation et expérience de la gestion et de l’analyse de données moyennant R, Python ou Stata. Une expérience dans l’utilisation de logiciels d’extraction de données et/ou de techniques d’apprentissage automatique constituerait un avantage. "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 1) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 1) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 1) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que la personne retenue s’engage à porter à un bon niveau. La maîtrise de l’espagnol constituerait un atout. Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus seront pourvues dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard le 15 septembre 2026 à 23 h 59 (heure de Paris). Durée du contrat Engagement de durée indéterminée, sans terme prévu. Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut, Règlement et Instructions applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. Ce qu’offre l’OCDE Salaire mensuel de base à partir de 5 279.34 EUR, plus allocations/indemnités en fonction de la situation personnelle, exonérés d’impôt sur le revenu en France. Cliquez ici pour consulter notre Simulateur de rémunération et d’indemnités. Cliquez ici pour consulter les Statut, règlement et instruction

item.description: {"id":"744000143056820","name":"Policy Analyst - Global Science Forum ","uuid":"c54b177f-c46c-4d6a-baaa-a2fb17890c0a","jobId":"e64c2531-a997-4c90-85d6-adbe48583add","jobAdId":"0339d847-eb3a-4de2-8df6-690ce87c0cf4","defaultJobAd":true,"refNumber":"REF3343R","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001210","valueLabel":"STI"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-12T09:00:04.849Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000143056820-policy-analyst-global-science-forum-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000143056820-policy-analyst-global-science-forum-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/c54b177f-c46c-4d6a-baaa-a2fb17890c0a?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Company Description","text":" The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting. The Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Directorate, in line with the strategic objectives of the Secretary-General, helps OECD member countries and other key economies build an environment conducive to translating science, technology and knowledge into innovation in order to create economic and social value added. The Science and Technology Policy Division (STP) within the STI is responsible for developing evidence-based policies that (i) encourage cooperation among OECD Members Countries and with Partners, (ii) support good policy practices and analysis in areas such as human resource development and mobility; the strengthening of links between research, higher education and innovation; national and regional research and innovation systems; mission oriented research and innovation policies; policies that promote inclusivity, and policies for anticipatory governance of emerging technologies, and (iii) help policymakers reorient STI systems towards addressing economic growth, competitiveness and societal challenges. The Global Science Forum (GSF) Secretariat is a part 2 funded activity and a Working Party of the Committee for Scientific and Technological Policy (CSTP). The focus of the Forum is science policy. This includes a long- term interest in research infrastructures and a variety of other priorities, including research funding and the research workforce, as defined by the member countries of the Forum. More recently the Forum has been working on research integrity and security. STI/STP/GSF is looking for an experienced Policy Analyst to join a team of 3 persons and work with countries to develop and implement its agenda. The selected person will lead new project activities in one of the following areas: research infrastructure, research funding, research workforce. She/he will also contribute to other cross-cutting areas of interest to CSTP, including research and technology security and science diplomacy. The selected person will work under the supervision of the Lead Coordinator of the GSF Secretariat, under the responsibility of the Head of the Science and Technology Policy Division. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Job Description","text":" Main responsibilities Analysis, research and management Scope work areas to develop terms of reference for projects. This will involve consulting with donors and national experts, and desktop analysis of data and information from OECD and other relevant sources. Lead the implementation of projects. This will involve establishing and working with an International Expert Group, conducting survey work and interviews and organising and moderating on-line and in-person seminars and workshops. Design policy frameworks or toolkits and drafting policy reports and briefs in line with countries’ interest. Present work to GSF, CSTP and other OECD bodies, as appropriate, and work with Members to build consensus and ensure their approval for project outputs. Liaison and co-ordination Liaise with other parts of STP to ensure that the work is aligned with the CSTP Programme of Work and other ongoing projects and contributes to the overall STI priorities. Liaise with other STI divisions and OECD Directorates and leverage mutual interests. Work closely with experts, delegates and government officials from GSF member countries and liaise with other relevant international bodies. Actively participate in activities to maximize the awareness and uptake of the GSF work through close co-operation with CSTP, other Divisions of the STI directorate, other OECD directorates, and appropriate entities outside the OECD. Act as the STP/STI expert in this subject area. Promote and proactively disseminate the work of GSF and CSTP, including the judicious use of social media tools and active participation in relevant meetings and seminars. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Ideal Candidate profile Academic Background A university degree in natural or social sciences or humanities and a postgraduate qualification (MSc or equivalent) in a relevant area for science and innovation policy. A PhD would be an advantage. Professional Background Minimum of five years’ experience of policy analysis in the field of science and/or higher education policy acquired in a national or local administration and/or an international organisation. Substantive knowledge and experience of working in GSF priority areas. Proven capacity for analytical and policy-oriented work, ability to conduct research assignments and synthesise policy-oriented issues for intergovernmental audiences. Languages Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and knowledge of the other, with a commitment to reach a good working level. Core Competencies OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 2); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 2); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 2); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). To learn more about the definitions for each competency for levels 1-3, please refer to OECD Core Competencies . "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Additional Information","text":" Contract duration 24-month fixed term appointment, with the possibility of renewal to a maximum of 36 months. Closing Date This vacancy should be filled as soon as possible, and applications should reach us no later than 23h59 on 16 September 2026 (Paris time). Please note that our Rules and Regulations stipulate that the mandatory retirement age is 67. What the OECD offers Monthly salary starts at 8,098 EUR, plus allowances based on eligibility, exempt of French income tax. Click here to consult the Staff Regulations applicable to officials of the OECD. Please note that from 1 July 2025, all Official appointments will be made under the OECD’s new contractual modalities . Click here to learn more about what we offer and why the OECD is a great place to work. Click here to browse our People Management Guidebook and learn more about all aspects relating to people at the OECD, our workplace environment and many other policies supporting staff in their daily life. Please note that the appointment may be made at one grade lower in the specified job family, based on the qualifications and professional experience of the selected applicant. This vacancy may be used to create a pool of candidates for comparable positions, both for open-ended and fixed-term functions. Selection Process For retained candidates, the selection process may include a video-recorded interview, job-based assessment and panel interviews. The OECD is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes the applications of all qualified candidates who are nationals of OECD member countries , irrespective of their racial or ethnic origin, opinions or beliefs, gender, sexual orientation, health or disabilities. The OECD promotes an optimal use of resources in order to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. Staff members are encouraged to actively contribute to this goal. item.description: {"id":"744000143056984","name":"Analyste des politiques - Forum mondial de la science ","uuid":"10170082-f414-4270-b6bb-e7b9527d0ebc","jobId":"e64c2531-a997-4c90-85d6-adbe48583add","jobAdId":"e31bd3b6-8aa8-4273-90c7-d70874488563","defaultJobAd":false,"refNumber":"REF3343R","company":{"name":"OECD","identifier":"OECD"},"location":{"city":"Paris","region":"Île-de-France Region","country":"fr","remote":false,"hybrid":false,"fullLocation":"Paris, Île-de-France Region, France"},"customField":[{"fieldId":"648821a3b6b69322b51f3093","fieldLabel":"Directorate","valueId":"10001210","valueLabel":"STI"},{"fieldId":"COUNTRY","fieldLabel":"Country/Region","valueId":"fr","valueLabel":"France"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4cccb","fieldLabel":"Department","valueId":"6106611","valueLabel":"Policy Analysis and Legal"},{"fieldId":"633d99302e608549cea4ccca","fieldLabel":"Brands","valueId":"default","valueLabel":"OECD"},{"fieldId":"64882104a519d256d6751438","fieldLabel":"Grade","valueId":"PAL6","valueLabel":"PAL6"}],"releasedDate":"2026-08-12T09:00:41.941Z","creator":{"name":"","avatarUrl":""},"postingUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000143056984-analyste-des-politiques-forum-mondial-de-la-science-","applyUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/OECD/744000143056984-analyste-des-politiques-forum-mondial-de-la-science-?oga=true","referralUrl":"https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/external-referrals/company/OECD/publication/10170082-f414-4270-b6bb-e7b9527d0ebc?dcr_ci=OECD","jobAd":{"sections":{"companyDescription":{"title":"Description de l'entreprise","text":" L’Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques ( OCDE ) est une organisation internationale regroupant 38 pays Membres, qui œuvre pour la mise en place de politiques meilleures pour une vie meilleure. Notre mission consiste à promouvoir des politiques de nature à améliorer le bien-être économique et social des populations du monde entier. Aux côtés des gouvernants, des responsables publics et des citoyens, nous nous employons à établir des normes internationales fondées sur des éléments probants et à trouver des solutions à un large éventail de défis sociaux, économiques et environnementaux. Qu’il s’agisse d’améliorer les performances économiques, de créer des emplois, de renforcer les systèmes éducatifs ou encore de lutter contre la fraude fiscale internationale, nous proposons un forum et une plateforme de connaissances sans équivalent, qui permettent aux parties intéressées de trouver des données et des analyses, de partager des expériences, de mutualiser des bonnes pratiques, et d’obtenir des conseils sur les politiques publiques et l’établissement de normes internationales. Conformément aux objectifs stratégiques du Secrétaire général, la Direction de la science, de la technologie et de l’innovation (STI) aide les pays Membres de l’OCDE et d’autres grandes économies à bâtir un environnement propice aux innovations issues de la science, de la technologie et des connaissances, en vue de créer une valeur ajoutée économique et sociale. Au sein de STI, la Division de la politique de la science et de la technologie (STP) est chargée d’élaborer des politiques fondées sur des données probantes permettant (i) d’encourager la coopération entre les pays Membres de l’OCDE et avec les économies partenaires ; (ii) de favoriser les bonnes pratiques et d’étayer les analyses des politiques dans des domaines tels que le développement et la mobilité des ressources humaines ; le resserrement des liens entre la recherche, l’enseignement supérieur et l’innovation ; les systèmes nationaux et régionaux de recherche et d’innovation ; les politiques de recherche et d’innovation à orientation précise ; les politiques inclusives et les dispositifs de gouvernance anticipative des technologies émergentes ; et (iii) d’aider les décideurs publics à réorienter les systèmes STI vers la croissance économique, la compétitivité et les défis sociétaux. Le Secrétariat du Forum mondial de la science (FMS) apporte son soutien au Forum, dont les activités sont financées au titre de la Partie II et qui constitue un Groupe de travail au sein du Comité de la politique scientifique et technologique (CPST). Les travaux du Forum portent sur la politique scientifique. Ils couvrent notamment les infrastructures de recherche, qui constituent un domaine d’intérêt de longue date, ainsi que diverses autres priorités définies par les pays membres du Forum, comme le financement de la recherche et le personnel de recherche. Plus récemment, le Forum a travaillé sur l’intégrité et la sécurité de la recherche. STI/STP/FMS recherche un·e analyste des politiques expérimenté·e qui rejoindra une équipe de trois personnes et travaillera avec les pays à l’élaboration et à la mise en œuvre de son programme d’action. La personne retenue dirigera les nouvelles activités menées dans le cadre de projets relevant de l’un des domaines suivants : infrastructures de recherche, financement de la recherche, personnel de recherche. Elle contribuera également à d’autres domaines transversaux intéressant les travaux du CPST, notamment la sécurité de la recherche et de la technologie et la diplomatie scientifique. Elle travaillera sous la direction du Coordinateur principal du Secrétariat du FMS et sous la responsabilité de la Cheffe de la Division de la politique de la science et de la technologie. "},"jobDescription":{"title":"Description du poste","text":" Responsabilités principales Analyse, recherche et gestion Définir les domaines de travail afin d’élaborer le cahier des charges des projets. Cela supposera notamment de consulter des donneurs et des experts nationaux, et de procéder à des analyses documentaires de données et d’informations de l’OCDE et d’autres sources pertinentes. Piloter la mise en œuvre des projets. Cela supposera notamment de mettre en place un groupe international d’experts et de collaborer avec lui, de mener des enquêtes et des entretiens, et d’organiser et de modérer des séminaires et des ateliers en ligne et en présentiel. Concevoir des cadres d’action ou des boîtes à outils et rédiger des rapports de fond et des notes de synthèse répondant aux intérêts des pays. Présenter les travaux menés au FMS, au CPST et à d’autres organes de l’OCDE, le cas échéant, et collaborer avec les membres pour dégager un consensus et pour faire en sorte que les résultats des projets reçoivent leur approbation. Liaison et coordination Assurer la liaison avec les autres composantes de STP pour veiller à ce que les travaux menés soient en adéquation avec le Programme de travail du CPST et avec les autres projets en cours et contribuent à la concrétisation des priorités générales de STI. Assurer la liaison avec d’autres divisions au sein de STI et d’autres directions au sein de l’OCDE, et tirer parti des intérêts communs. Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les spécialistes, les délégations et les responsables publics des pays membres du FMS et assurer la liaison avec d’autres instances internationales lorsque cela est pertinent. Prendre une part active aux initiatives visant à faire connaître autant que possible les travaux du FMS et à favoriser leur adoption, en étroite coopération avec le CPST, d’autres divisions de la DSTI, d’autres directions de l’OCDE et les entités concernées en dehors de l’OCDE. Faire office d’expert·e STP/STI dans ce domaine. Promouvoir et diffuser de manière proactive les travaux du FMS et du CPST, notamment en utilisant judicieusement les médias sociaux et en participant activement aux réunions et séminaires pertinents. "},"qualifications":{"title":"Qualifications","text":" Profil idéal Formation Diplôme universitaire en sciences naturelles, sciences sociales ou sciences humaines et diplôme post-licence (master ou équivalent) dans un domaine pertinent pour la politique de la science et de l’innovation. Un doctorat constituerait un avantage. Expérience professionnelle Au moins cinq années d’expérience de l’analyse des politiques dans le domaine de la science et/ou des politiques d’enseignement supérieur, acquise dans une administration nationale ou une collectivité territoriale et/ou une organisation internationale. Connaissances de fond et expérience professionnelle dans les domaines prioritaires du FMS. Aptitude avérée à mener des travaux d’analyse et axés sur l’action publique, capacité à mener des travaux de recherche et à faire la synthèse de questions intéressant l’action publique pour des publics intergouvernementaux. Langues Parfaite maîtrise d’une des deux langues officielles de l’OCDE (le français et l’anglais) et connaissance de l’autre langue, que la personne retenue s’engage à porter à un bon niveau. Compétences clés Les membres du personnel de l’OCDE sont censés faire preuve d’un comportement conforme aux six compétences clés qui seront évaluées dans le cadre de la procédure de recrutement organisée au titre de la présente offre d’emploi : Vision et stratégie (niveau 2) ; Renforcement des capacités des personnes (niveau 1) ; Éthique et intégrité (niveau 2) ; Collaboration et horizontalité (niveau 2) ; Obtention de résultats (niveau 2) ; Innovation et acceptation du changement (niveau 2). Pour en savoir plus sur les définitions des niveaux de maîtrise 1 à 3 associés à chaque compétence, veuillez vous référer au Cadre de compétences clés de l’OCDE . "},"additionalInformation":{"title":"Informations supplémentaires","text":" Durée du contrat Durée déterminée de 24 mois, avec possibilité de renouvellement jusqu’à un maximum de 36 mois. Date de clôture Les fonctions décrites ci-dessus seront pourvues dès que possible, et les candidatures devront nous parvenir au plus tard à 23h59 le 16 septembre 2026 (heure de Paris). Veuillez noter que, conformément aux Statut et Règlement applicables aux agents de l’Organisation, l’âge de départ obligatoire à la retraite est fixé à 67 ans. item.title: Senior Economist
item.description: Do you want to build a career that is truly worthwhile? Working at the World Bank provides a unique opportunity for you to help our clients solve their greatest development challenges. The World Bank is one of the largest sources of funding and knowledge for developing countries; a unique global partnership of five institutions dedicated to ending extreme poverty, increasing shared prosperity, and promoting sustainable development. With 189 member countries and more than 120 offices worldwide, we work with public and private sector partners, investing in groundbreaking projects and using data, research, and technology to develop solutions to the most urgent global challenges. For more information, visit https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/home VPU Context: The South Asia Region (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka) is at a crucial stage of development. Rapid economic growth, driven by urbanization and demographic dividend, has brought down poverty rates, but severe forms of exclusion and disparities based on ethnicity, caste, and gender remain. Rapid growth has also come with congestion and pollution in cities. South Asia is more than other regions affected by changes in temperature and extreme weather event. Additional challenges are that South Asia is underperforming in exports, has large informal sectors and low female labor force participation rates. All these challenges must be addressed to secure rapid growth in coming decades. Private sector led growth, focused on investments in infrastructure, energy, logistics and cities are essential to generate the jobs needed to employ South Asia’s sizeable youth population. At the same time, the region needs to continue building human capital so that South Asia’s population is well equipped for the jobs of the future. The World Bank in South Asia: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/region/sar Unit Context: The Finance, Competitiveness and Investment (FCI) Global Practice of the World Bank combines expertise in the financial sector with expertise in private sector development to foster private-sector led growth and help create markets in client countries. FCI’s core lines of business are: (a) Financial Stability Integrity; (b) Financial Inclusion, Infrastructure Access; (c) Firm Capabilities Innovation; (d) Long-Term Finance; (e) Climate Risk Management; (f) Markets and Technology; and (g) Investment and Competition. For more information, please visit https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/unit/fci SAR FCI unit is seeking a Senior Economist for a locally recruited, 3-year term appointment based in New Delhi, India, to support our growing portfolio of advisory and lending projects focused on private sector development. The selected candidate will contribute to financing and lending operations, analytical and advisory services (ASA), and policy dialogue related to financial sector development. Duties and accountabilities: • Provide intellectual and technical leadership on financial sector development issues in India. Engage in strategic dialogue with senior government counterparts (e.g. Ministry of Finance and financial regulators) and private sector stakeholders to identify challenges and opportunities in the financial sector. Offer policy advice and technical input on reforms related to financial stability and development. • Lead / co-lead the development of lending operations aimed at mobilizing private capital. Structure innovative financing solutions, including blended finance instruments, to leverage private sector resources for development projects. This includes conceptualizing project design, preparing project documentation, and coordinating across teams to align operations with the new World Bank’s country strategy. • Drive the creation of high-quality analytical work on financial sector topics. This entails leading economic and sector work that address key development challenges in India’s financial sector. Ensure analytical outputs are rigorous, relevant, and actionable, communicating complex financial concepts in clear terms for policymakers. • Work in close collaboration with colleagues across the FCI Global Practice and other Global Practices to deliver integrated solutions. Coordinate with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), and other World Bank Group teams to harness synergies and ensure a unified approach in engagements with clients. • Champion private capital mobilization as a cross-cutting priority across all dimensions of the engagement, whether policy advocacy, the design of lending operations, analytical work, or collaboration with other Global Practices and sister organizations. Embed private capital solutions systematically into the team's work program, ensuring that opportunities to crowd in private finance are identified and pursued consistently rather than treated in isolation. • Serve as a key point of contact for financial sector engagements in India, maintaining strong client relationships built on trust and technical expertise. Represent the World Bank in meetings, workshops, and conferences related to the financial sector. Proactively identify client needs and emerging issues, and respond with relevant World Bank support or knowledge offerings. • Mentor and guide junior staff and team members, fostering a positive and inclusive team environment. Share knowledge and best practices within the team and across the Global Practice. Demonstrate a collaborative team spirit, working effectively in multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams.
